同考試官教諭張旆批：詞理兼至，美不忘規，溫柔敦厚之意，子其得之，可錄。
考試官教諭鄭延年批：語意婉切。
考試官教諭魏體謙批：雋永有味。
魯人願遠人格心而致貢，忠愛之情見矣。夫淮夷之為魯患也久矣，詩人乃願其格心而致貢焉，其忠愛之情為何如哉！且其意謂，夫內治之隆汙，遠人所視以為向背者也。我侯既作泮宮，所以脩內治者得矣，而遠人之服也當何如哉？
translation_en:
…the king’s heart: this assuredly was no accident! Nevertheless, King Xuan did not rely exclusively on this. “The Milky Way” was sung, and the August One drew near; “No Sheep” was chanted, and households lived in harmony. His reverence for Heaven and diligence on behalf of the people were already long established. With orderly government within and imposing authority abroad, was this not the natural response?
“Those distant Huai tribes come to present their treasures: great tortoises and elephant tusks, and ample offerings of southern bronze.”
Song Kerou
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang Jingbin, Instructor: “The language is clear and the meaning fully expressed; it captures the poet’s manner of blessing and praise.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiong Yinchen, Instructor: “The meaning is substantial, and the language fully adequate to express it. It certainly merits a high recommendation.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang Pei, Instructor: “Language and reasoning alike attain excellence. In praising, you do not forget admonition. You have captured the spirit of gentleness and sincerity. Worthy of selection.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng Yannian, Instructor: “The language and meaning are tactful and apt.”
Comment by Examiner Wei Tiqian, Instructor: “Rich in lasting savor.”
The people of Lu wished that those from afar would reform their hearts and bring tribute: their feelings of loyalty and affection are evident here. The Huai tribes had long troubled Lu, yet the poet wished that they would reform their hearts and bring tribute. How profound were his loyalty and affection! His meaning, moreover, was that the excellence or deficiency of internal government is what people from afar consider when deciding whether to give or withhold their allegiance. Our lord has now built the Pan Palace, the state school, and has thus found the means to cultivate internal government. What, then, should the submission of those from afar be like?

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
是故蠢兹淮夷向嘗負固不服矣今則仰涖泮
之風適鼓其歸德之念無知之類盡爲有覺之
良也沐崇文之敎自起其向化之機匪茹之眾
皆知自新之善也悔今是而昨非咸心悅而誠
服蓋無復有向之負固者矣然是淮夷也豈徒
其心之覺悟而已哉吾見相率以來歸者則亦
必相率以來貢而輸將之忱自有所不容已莫
敢不來同者則亦莫敢不來享而寶琛之納自
有所不容後其庭實之旅陳者雖非一端也而
===
卽其貴重難得者言之其殆不惟有元龜也而
又有象齒者乎其方物之畢獻者雖難悉數也
而卽其奇絕可貴者言之其殆不惟有象齒也
而又有南金者乎雖曰君子不貴異物我魯固
不樂寶乎此也然彼有歸附之誠自不得不竭
其難繼之物耳容非其所自盡歟雖曰王者厚
往薄來我魯固不厚責乎彼也然就其愛戴之
心自不得不備其多儀之享耳容非其所必至
者歟至此則兵不必試而淮夷不但孔淑已也
punctuated: 是故蠢兹淮夷，向嘗負固不服矣。今則仰涖泮之風，適鼓其歸德之念，無知之類盡爲有覺之良也；沐崇文之敎，自起其向化之機，匪茹之眾皆知自新之善也。悔今是而昨非，咸心悅而誠服，蓋無復有向之負固者矣。然是淮夷也，豈徒其心之覺悟而已哉？吾見相率以來歸者，則亦必相率以來貢，而輸將之忱自有所不容已；莫敢不來同者，則亦莫敢不來享，而寶琛之納自有所不容後。其庭實之旅陳者，雖非一端也，而卽其貴重難得者言之，其殆不惟有元龜也，而又有象齒者乎？其方物之畢獻者，雖難悉數也，而卽其奇絕可貴者言之，其殆不惟有象齒也，而又有南金者乎？雖曰君子不貴異物，我魯固不樂寶乎此也，然彼有歸附之誠，自不得不竭其難繼之物耳，容非其所自盡歟？雖曰王者厚往薄來，我魯固不厚責乎彼也，然就其愛戴之心，自不得不備其多儀之享耳，容非其所必至者歟？至此則兵不必試，而淮夷不但孔淑已也。
translation_en:
Thus these unruly Huai Yi formerly relied on their strongholds and refused submission. Now, looking up to the civilizing influence of the lord’s presence at the Pan school, they are stirred to turn toward his virtue: those who lacked understanding all become good people possessed of discernment. Bathed in teachings that honor culture, they spontaneously incline toward transformation: even those who were violent all recognize the goodness of renewing themselves. Repenting, they recognize that their present course is right and their former course was wrong [?]; all submit sincerely, with hearts gladly convinced. None now remain who rely on their strongholds as before. Yet could these Huai Yi do no more than awaken in their hearts? I see that those who lead one another in coming to submit must also lead one another in bringing tribute; their sincere desire to convey offerings cannot be restrained. Those who dare not fail to come and acknowledge allegiance likewise dare not fail to present offerings; they cannot bear to delay the presentation of their treasures. Although the gifts arrayed in the courtyard are of many kinds, if we speak of those that are precious and difficult to obtain, surely there will be not only great tortoises but also elephant tusks? Although their local products, offered in their entirety, are too numerous to enumerate, if we speak of those that are exceptionally rare and valuable, surely there will be not only elephant tusks but also metal from the south?

Although it is said that the gentleman does not prize exotic objects, and our state of Lu certainly takes no delight in treasuring these things, their sincerity in submitting leaves them unable to do otherwise than offer to the utmost even goods difficult to supply repeatedly. Surely this is their way of giving their all? Although it is said that a true king gives generously and receives sparingly, and our state of Lu certainly does not exact heavy contributions from them, their love and reverence leave them unable to do otherwise than prepare offerings of many kinds. Surely this is what they must inevitably do? At this point, weapons need not be put to the test, and the Huai Yi will be more than merely ‘very good’…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
謀不必用而淮夷不但卒獲已也玆之所以願
於我侯者豈其微哉吁若魯人可謂忠愛之至
而善於頌禱者矣雖然淮夷猖獗未易服也何
魯人之願君也言之若是其易易哉蓋忠信禮
義之威愈於堅甲利兵之銳使魯侯果能順長
道克明德如詩人之所咏焉則於淮夷之格心
致貢也何有夫何不能盡然卒使之病杞病鄫
史不絕書焉其亦未識魯人祝頌之微意歟
春秋
===
夏齊侯衛侯胥命于蒲桓公三年
王來潤
同考試官學正張介批相命信諭卽爲近正此作
獨能得之可以錄矣
考試官敎諭鄭廷年批文有斷制
考試官敎諭魏體謙批得聖人善胥命之旨
春秋善二國之相命以其近正也甚矣聖人以
古道望天下也胥命則不盟而有以近古矣春
秋惡得而不善之且蒲之命齊衛相推爲牧伯
punctuated:
謀不必用，而淮夷不但卒獲已也。玆之所以願於我侯者，豈其微哉！吁！若魯人，可謂忠愛之至而善於頌禱者矣。雖然，淮夷猖獗，未易服也，何魯人之願君也，言之若是其易易哉？蓋忠信禮義之威，愈於堅甲利兵之銳。使魯侯果能順長道、克明德，如詩人之所咏焉，則於淮夷之格心致貢也何有？夫何不能盡然，卒使之病杞病鄫，史不絕書焉？其亦未識魯人祝頌之微意歟？

春秋

夏，齊侯、衛侯胥命于蒲。桓公三年。
王來潤

同考試官學正張介批：相命信諭，卽爲近正，此作獨能得之，可以錄矣。
考試官敎諭鄭廷年批：文有斷制。
考試官敎諭魏體謙批：得聖人善胥命之旨。

春秋善二國之相命，以其近正也。甚矣，聖人以古道望天下也！胥命則不盟，而有以近古矣，春秋惡得而不善之？且蒲之命，齊衛相推爲牧伯
translation_en:
…Strategies need not be employed, and the submission of the Huai Yi would amount to more than merely their eventual capture. Could what the people thus wish for our lord be of little consequence? Ah! The people of Lu may indeed be called supremely loyal and loving, and skilled in offering praise and prayers. Nevertheless, the Huai Yi were unruly and not easily subdued. Why, then, did the people of Lu speak of their wishes for their ruler as though fulfillment were so very easy? Because the power of loyalty, trustworthiness, ritual propriety, and righteousness surpasses the force of stout armor and sharp weapons. If the lord of Lu could truly follow the great Way and make his virtue shine, as the poet sang, what difficulty would there be in winning over the hearts of the Huai Yi and bringing them to offer tribute? Why, then, was this not fully achieved, so that in the end they were allowed to afflict Qi 杞 and Zeng 鄫, as the historical records repeatedly recount? Could it be that the subtle intent of the people of Lu’s prayers and praises had not been understood?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In summer, the lord of Qi and the lord of Wei exchanged pledges at Pu.” Third year of Duke Huan.
By Wang Lairun 王來潤.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang Jie 張介, Instructor: “Exchanging pledges and giving assurances in good faith comes close to proper conduct. This composition alone grasps that point; it merits inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng Tingnian 鄭廷年, Instructor: “The writing displays decisive judgment.”
Comment by Examiner Wei Tiqian 魏體謙, Instructor: “It grasps the Sage’s intention in approving the exchange of pledges.”

The Spring and Autumn Annals approves the two states’ exchange of pledges because it approached proper conduct. How earnestly the Sage hoped that the world would follow the Way of antiquity! In exchanging pledges, they did not swear a covenant and thus came somewhat closer to ancient practice. How could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to approve? Moreover, in the pledges exchanged at Pu, Qi and Wei mutually advanced one another as leaders of the regional lords…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
也諸侯相命古未之聞也而春秋顧善之也何
君子曰玆命也其猶有古之遺乎古者不盟結
言而退自夫盟載之法設而亂是用長是故巧
言之詩所爲刺也逮至春秋之世盟愈煩畔愈
甚而風會之下也久矣何幸齊之僖衞之宣而
有玆命耶惟以言而相孚不以牲而共歃自後
日而觀之言以時異固難必其不變自今日而
觀之言以成信而其心固已咸喻矣噫虞夏之
道降而敬信之風微吾意齊衞之君囿於習俗
===
而莫之悟也而乃胥命若此是雖以國相推若
有戾于先王侯伯之命而以信相諭亦不泥于
周官司盟之法矣使諸侯而皆齊衞皆不盟焉
則傾危俗革而於穆之風不可復見耶聖人有
志于大道之行與三代之英嘗嘆其不可得而
見也而得見不盟如齊衞者斯可矣是故特起
胥命之文以善之非謂胥命之盡善也有胥命
之不盟則無末世之滋弊而古道庶乎可幾矣
其亦挽回斯世之一機乎或曰世日降矣春秋
punctuated: 也。諸侯相命，古未之聞也，而春秋顧善之也，何？君子曰：「玆命也，其猶有古之遺乎！」古者不盟，結言而退。自夫盟載之法設，而亂是用長，是故《巧言》之詩所爲刺也。逮至春秋之世，盟愈煩，畔愈甚，而風會之下也久矣。何幸齊之僖、衞之宣，而有玆命耶！惟以言而相孚，不以牲而共歃。自後日而觀之，言以時異，固難必其不變；自今日而觀之，言以成信，而其心固已咸喻矣。噫！虞夏之道降，而敬信之風微。吾意齊衞之君囿於習俗，而莫之悟也，而乃胥命若此。是雖以國相推，若有戾于先王侯伯之命，而以信相諭，亦不泥于《周官》司盟之法矣。使諸侯而皆齊衞，皆不盟焉，則傾危俗革，而於穆之風不可復見耶？聖人有志于大道之行與三代之英，嘗嘆其不可得而見也，而得見不盟如齊衞者，斯可矣。是故特起胥命之文以善之，非謂胥命之盡善也。有胥命之不盟，則無末世之滋弊，而古道庶乎可幾矣。其亦挽回斯世之一機乎？或曰：「世日降矣，春秋
translation_en:
…The lords of the states mutually appointing one another was unheard of in antiquity. Yet why does the Spring and Autumn Annals approve of it? The gentleman says: “Might this appointment still preserve something handed down from antiquity?” In ancient times, men did not swear covenants; they pledged their word and withdrew. Once the practice of written covenants was instituted, disorder thereby increased. This is what the poem “Clever Words” (Qiao yan) censures. By the Spring and Autumn period, covenants grew ever more frequent and betrayals ever more severe; prevailing customs had long been in decline. How fortunate that Duke Xi of Qi and Duke Xuan of Wei should have made this appointment! They trusted one another solely on their word, without jointly smearing their lips with the blood of sacrificial victims. Viewed from a later day, words change with circumstances, and one certainly cannot guarantee that they will remain unchanged. Viewed at the time, however, their words established trust, and their intentions were already mutually understood.

Alas! The Way of Yu and Xia declined, and the spirit of reverence and trust faded. I would have thought that the rulers of Qi and Wei were confined by customary practices and unable to awaken to this; yet they mutually appointed one another in this fashion. Although their states’ mutual endorsement appeared to contravene the former kings’ authority to appoint leaders of the regional lords, their communication through trust was also unfettered by the rules of the Director of Covenants in the Offices of Zhou (Zhou guan). If all the regional lords acted like Qi and Wei and refrained from sworn covenants, would treacherous customs not be transformed, and might that profoundly harmonious spirit not appear again?

The sage aspired to the practice of the Great Way and to the excellence of the Three Dynasties, and once lamented that he could not witness them. Yet to witness rulers forgoing sworn covenants, as Qi and Wei did, would suffice. Thus he specially introduced the wording “mutually appointed one another” to commend them. He did not mean that mutual appointment was wholly good. If there were mutual appointments without sworn covenants, the mounting abuses of a declining age would cease, and the ancient Way might nearly be attained. Might this too be an opportunity to turn the age back toward it? Someone says: “The world declines by the day. In the Spring and Autumn period…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
之不盟僅有如二國者而欲以挽之得毋難與
不知古今之時不同而理同理也者人心所同
具者也故曰斯民也三代之所以直道而行也
行帝道而帝行王道而王顧倡導者何如耳如
以爲盡不可變也而安于習焉吾知聖人望天
下之志荒矣
齊人歸我濟西田〔宣公十年〕齊人來歸鄆
謹龜陰田〔定公十年〕齊人歸謹及闡〔哀
公八年〕
===
張庸
同考試官學正張〔介〕批文有繩墨而心服處尤爲
透徹佳士也取之
考試官敎諭鄭〔延年〕批辭嚴義正
考試官敎諭魏〔體謙〕批得聖人自序之旨
春秋詳大國歸地而於心服者特異其詞焉此
鄆謹龜陰齊感聖人之化以誠而歸之也春秋
書之特異其詞者意蓋如此且齊之歸田于魯
也數矣前之濟西後之謹闡皆直書歸而獨於
punctuated:
之不盟，僅有如二國者，而欲以挽之，得毋難與？不知古今之時不同，而理同。理也者，人心所同具者也。故曰：「斯民也，三代之所以直道而行也。」行帝道而帝，行王道而王，顧倡導者何如耳。如以爲盡不可變也，而安于習焉，吾知聖人望天下之志荒矣。
齊人歸我濟西田〔宣公十年〕。齊人來歸鄆謹龜陰田〔定公十年〕。齊人歸謹及闡〔哀公八年〕。
張庸
同考試官學正張〔介〕批：「文有繩墨，而心服處尤爲透徹，佳士也，取之。」
考試官敎諭鄭〔延年〕批：「辭嚴義正。」
考試官敎諭魏〔體謙〕批：「得聖人自序之旨。」
春秋詳大國歸地，而於心服者特異其詞焉。此鄆謹龜陰，齊感聖人之化，以誠而歸之也。春秋書之，特異其詞者，意蓋如此。且齊之歸田于魯也，數矣。前之濟西，後之謹闡，皆直書歸，而獨於
translation_en:
…the only cases in the Spring and Autumn Annals of refraining from a covenant are those of these two states. Would it not be difficult to reverse the decline through them? This fails to recognize that, although ancient and present times differ, their principle is the same. Principle is what all human hearts possess in common. Thus it is said: “These are the people through whom the Three Dynasties proceeded along the straight Way.” Practise the Way of the emperors and one becomes an emperor; practise the Way of the kings and one becomes a king. It depends only on those who take the lead. If one considers all this incapable of change and rests content with customary practices, I know that the sage’s aspirations for the world will come to nothing.
“The men of Qi returned to us the lands west of the Ji River.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Xuan.〕 “The men of Qi came and returned the lands of Yun, Huan [?], and Guiyin.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding.〕 “The men of Qi returned Huan [?] and Chan.” 〔Eighth year of Duke Ai.〕
Zhang Yong
Associate Examiner Zhang Jie, School Instructor, comments: “The composition observes proper standards, and its treatment of submission from the heart is especially penetrating. A worthy scholar: accept him.”
Examiner Zheng Yannian, Instructor, comments: “The language is rigorous and the interpretation correct.”
Examiner Wei Tiqian, Instructor, comments: “It grasps the intent of the sage’s own narration.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals records in detail the return of territory by great states, but gives distinctive wording to cases arising from submission from the heart. These lands of Yun, Huan [?], and Guiyin were returned sincerely by Qi, moved by the sage’s transforming influence. This, presumably, is the intention behind the Annals’ distinctive wording in recording the event. Moreover, Qi returned lands to Lu on several occasions. In the earlier case of the lands west of the Ji River and the later case of Huan [?] and Chan, it simply records “returned”; only in the case of…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
鄆讙龜陰之田特以來歸書者何曰事待於人
爲者未必其由衷而感出於天機者不容於勉
强濟西之田惠也悅魯之媚巳讙闡之田悼也
悅魯之歸邾要之皆緣請而歸非誠也乃若三
田則異是矣定也用孔子以相會孔子行王道
而化齊示之以華夏盟好之重明之以人神德
義之常始而以禮相見焉終而以禮罷享焉不
于其勢而于其理雖有犁彌之奸萊夷之劫其
心亦有不容不屈者由是晏子之語方陳景公
===
之良頓悟數十年之侵疆遂章章歸焉故宇復
周公之舊人曰齊之謝過也不知其謝之以質
者中心之悅也惠徼太公之靈人曰齊之心服
也不知其服之以誠者俄頃之化也不然齊自
鞌陵之後代盟主合諸侯雖盡魯之力以臨之
猶不能下而肯以其田歸哉甚哉魯之禮足以
服人齊之强可以禮服而過化存神之妙於是
乎不可掩矣故特書來歸而異於濟西讙闡之
文者見齊則以誠而歸魯非以請而得亦以自
punctuated: 鄆讙龜陰之田特以來歸書者何？曰：事待於人爲者，未必其由衷；而感出於天機者，不容於勉强。濟西之田，惠也，悅魯之媚巳；讙闡之田，悼也，悅魯之歸邾。要之，皆緣請而歸，非誠也。乃若三田，則異是矣。定也，用孔子以相會，孔子行王道而化齊，示之以華夏盟好之重，明之以人神德義之常。始而以禮相見焉，終而以禮罷享焉。不于其勢，而于其理，雖有犁彌之奸、萊夷之劫，其心亦有不容不屈者。由是晏子之語方陳，景公之良頓悟，數十年之侵疆遂章章歸焉。故宇復周公之舊，人曰齊之謝過也，不知其謝之以質者，中心之悅也；惠徼太公之靈，人曰齊之心服也，不知其服之以誠者，俄頃之化也。不然，齊自鞌陵之後，代盟主，合諸侯，雖盡魯之力以臨之，猶不能下，而肯以其田歸哉？甚哉！魯之禮足以服人，齊之强可以禮服，而過化存神之妙，於是乎不可掩矣。故特書來歸，而異於濟西讙闡之文者，見齊則以誠而歸，魯非以請而得，亦以自
translation_en:
…why, specifically for the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin, does the record say “came and returned”? The answer is this: an undertaking that depends on human contrivance does not necessarily come from the heart, whereas a response arising from the spontaneous workings of Heaven cannot be forced. The lands west of the Ji River were returned by Duke Hui, who was pleased that Lu flattered him; the lands of Huan and Chan were returned by Duke Dao, who was pleased that Lu had returned Zhu. In sum, these returns all followed requests; they were not sincere. The three tracts, however, were different.

Duke Ding employed Confucius to assist him at the meeting. Confucius practiced the Kingly Way and thereby transformed Qi. He showed them the importance of maintaining alliances and amity among the states of Huaxia, and made clear the constant principles of virtue and righteousness governing humans and spirits. At the outset, he conducted their meeting according to ritual; at its conclusion, he invoked ritual to have the banquet canceled. He relied on principle rather than power. Despite Li Mi’s treachery and the intimidation by the Lai tribesmen, their hearts could not but yield. Thus, scarcely had Yanzi spoken when Duke Jing’s innate goodness suddenly awakened, and territories encroached upon over several decades were duly and openly returned.

The former domains were restored to their extent under the Duke of Zhou. People said that Qi was apologizing for its wrongdoing, unaware that its apology in deeds expressed heartfelt delight. Beneficence invoked the spirit of the Grand Duke [?]. People said that Qi had submitted in its heart, unaware that its sincere submission resulted from a transformation accomplished in a moment. Otherwise, since the events at Anling [?], Qi had succeeded to leadership of the covenant and assembled the feudal lords. Even had Lu brought all its strength to bear against Qi, it could not have subdued it. Would Qi then have willingly returned those lands?

How profound! Lu’s ritual propriety sufficed to win submission, and even mighty Qi could be brought to submit through ritual. Here the marvelous power of the sage—to transform wherever he passes and exert a spiritual influence wherever he abides—could not be concealed. Thus the distinctive wording “came and returned,” differing from the entries concerning the lands west of the Ji River and those of Huan and Chan, shows that Qi returned the lands sincerely, and that Lu obtained them without making a request. It also served for him to…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
序其績也自序其績是誠以天自處而不以爲
嫌者其斯以爲聖人矣乎嗚呼三田歸而變齊
二邑墮而變魯所謂朞月而可此其徵也使得
志而行乎魯焉則必一變至道文武成康之治
可復見也惜也女樂受膰肉不至而齊人之沮
又復行其計矣噫魯不用孔子吾其東周雖有
聖人其奈之何哉
禮記
夫然後足以化民易俗近者說服而遠者
===
懷之此大學之道也
王同文
同考試官敎諭張邦臣批 講夫然後處殊有根據而
化民易俗輕輕說去尤得本旨取之
考試官敎諭鄭延年批 說得足字出
考試官敎諭魏體謙批 不泥官使之効良是
記者推大成者之裕於用因著其爲大學之道
焉夫學至大成而其用自裕大人之事備矣謂
非大學之道而何哉記學者至此以謂先王之
punctuated:
序其績也。自序其績，是誠以天自處而不以爲嫌者，其斯以爲聖人矣乎！嗚呼！三田歸而變齊，二邑墮而變魯，所謂「朞月而可」，此其徵也。使得志而行乎魯焉，則必一變至道，文武成康之治可復見也。惜也！女樂受，膰肉不至，而齊人之沮又復行其計矣。噫！魯不用孔子，「吾其東周」，雖有聖人，其奈之何哉！
禮記
夫然後足以化民易俗，近者說服而遠者懷之，此大學之道也。
王同文
同考試官敎諭張邦臣批：講「夫然後」處殊有根據，而「化民易俗」輕輕說去，尤得本旨，取之。
考試官敎諭鄭延年批：說得「足」字出。
考試官敎諭魏體謙批：不泥官使之効，良是。
記者推大成者之裕於用，因著其爲大學之道焉。夫學至大成，而其用自裕，大人之事備矣。謂非大學之道而何哉？記學者至此，以謂先王之
translation_en:
…to recount his own achievements. In recounting his own achievements, he truly placed himself on a level with Heaven without considering this objectionable. Was this not what made him a sage? Alas! The return of the three tracts of land transformed Qi; the demolition of the two fortified towns transformed Lu. Here was proof of the saying, “In a full year, something could be accomplished.” Had he been able to realize his intentions and put them into practice in Lu, surely a single transformation would have brought it to the Way, and the governance of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang could have been seen again. What a pity! The female musicians were accepted, the sacrificial meat failed to arrive, and the men of Qi once again succeeded in their scheme to thwart him. Alas! Lu would not employ Confucius. “I would make an Eastern Zhou”—even with a sage present, what could be done?
Book of Rites
“Only then is one capable of transforming the people and changing their customs: those nearby submit gladly, and those far away cherish him. This is the Way of the Great Learning.”
Wang Tongwen
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang Bangchen, Instructor: “The explanation of ‘only then’ is particularly well grounded, while ‘transforming the people and changing their customs’ is handled with a light touch that captures the original purport especially well. Accept it.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng Yannian, Instructor: “He brings out the meaning of the word ‘capable.’”
Comment by Examiner Wei Tiqian, Instructor: “He does not confine himself to the results of appointment to office and employment in service. This is very sound.”
The author of the Record develops the ample capacity for practical application possessed by one who has attained great accomplishment, thereby making clear that this is the Way of the Great Learning. For when learning reaches great accomplishment, its practical application naturally becomes ample, and all the undertakings of a great man are fully provided for. If this is not called the Way of the Great Learning, what else could it be? At this point, the author recording the process of learning means that the former kings’ …

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
於人才其教之者將以致用也其用之者將以
責效也士而視德業于九年信足以言大成矣
夫惟其大成也則素豫吾內已寓乎鼓舞變動
之術而求利吾外斯優于化民易俗之治被其
澤者則心說而誠服焉孚感之速以言乎近則
不厭也聞其風者則向慕而允懷焉綏來之妙
以言乎遠則不禦也蓋施于有政不徒能于其
官而日見于行且將不負所使者矣若此者寧
非大學教人之道也哉蓋明德新民大人之事
===
也惟學有未成則用有未裕謂之大學未也今
以大成而裕大用焉則本諸其身旣盡夫明德
之功而徵諸庶民不愧乎新民之用擴而充之
可以成位育之能內聖外王由此其選也推而
極之可以達參贊之化盛德大業於是乎畢也
否則明體不足以適用治人或歉于自淑豈古
者作人之本意哉是知士非大學無以成其材
而學非大成無以彰其盛此先王所以臻治化
之隆而非後世之所能及也歟抑考成周之世
punctuated: 於人才，其教之者將以致用也，其用之者將以責效也。士而視德業于九年，信足以言大成矣。夫惟其大成也，則素豫吾內，已寓乎鼓舞變動之術；而求利吾外，斯優于化民易俗之治。被其澤者，則心說而誠服焉；孚感之速，以言乎近，則不厭也。聞其風者，則向慕而允懷焉；綏來之妙，以言乎遠，則不禦也。蓋施于有政，不徒能于其官，而日見于行，且將不負所使者矣。若此者，寧非大學教人之道也哉？蓋明德新民，大人之事也。惟學有未成，則用有未裕，謂之大學，未也。今以大成而裕大用焉，則本諸其身，旣盡夫明德之功；而徵諸庶民，不愧乎新民之用。擴而充之，可以成位育之能，內聖外王，由此其選也；推而極之，可以達參贊之化，盛德大業，於是乎畢也。否則明體不足以適用，治人或歉于自淑，豈古者作人之本意哉？是知士非大學，無以成其材；而學非大成，無以彰其盛。此先王所以臻治化之隆，而非後世之所能及也歟？抑考成周之世，
translation_en:
…with regard to men of talent, their purpose in educating them was to prepare them for service, and their purpose in employing them was to hold them accountable for results. When a scholar’s virtue and accomplishments are examined in the ninth year, they surely warrant the designation “great attainment.” Precisely because his attainment is great, what he has long cultivated within himself already contains the means to inspire others and bring about change. When he seeks to benefit those outside himself, he therefore has ample capacity for the work of transforming the people and changing their customs. Those who receive his beneficence rejoice in their hearts and submit sincerely. Such is the swiftness with which his sincerity moves them that those nearby never tire of him. Those who hear of his influence admire him and turn toward him in true affection. Such is his marvelous ability to draw them peacefully to him that those far away cannot be kept from coming. When he applies his learning to government, he is not merely competent in his office: his ability manifests itself daily in his conduct, and he will also prove worthy of the missions entrusted to him. Is this not the way in which the Great Learning teaches people?

Manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people are the affairs of the great person. Only when learning remains incomplete does one lack ample capacity to put it into practice; to call this the Great Learning would be premature. Now, through great attainment, one gains ample capacity for great service. Grounding this in oneself, one has fully accomplished the work of manifesting luminous virtue; testing it among the common people, one proves worthy of the task of renewing them. By expanding and fully developing it, one can bring Heaven and Earth into their proper positions and nurture the myriad things. Inward sagehood and outward kingliness find their course through this [?]. By extending it to its utmost, one can participate in and assist the transforming processes of Heaven and Earth. Perfect virtue and great achievements are thereby brought to completion. Otherwise, understanding the underlying substance would not suffice for practical application, and governing others might leave one deficient in cultivating goodness within oneself. Could this have been the original intention of the ancients in nurturing men of talent?

Thus we know that without the Great Learning, scholars have no means to bring their capacities to completion, and that without great attainment, learning has no means to display its full excellence. Is this why the former kings achieved such flourishing government and moral transformation, beyond what later ages could attain? Now, if we examine the age of the fully established Zhou…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
濟濟多士文王以寧王國克生維周之楨宜若
氣化之使然矣及觀棫樸之詩乃知周王作人
之有自而又以緝煕之德先之此所以成人有
德而治化隆美也若夫過魯之祀臨雍之拜非
不知敎也而卒不能復先王之舊焉噫本之則
無如之何其不漢也
禮樂刑政四達而不悖則王道備矣
徐養大
同考試官敎諭張〔邦臣〕批鋪敘禮樂刑政四字甚有
===
關鍵程式之文也
考試官敎諭鄭〔延年〕批說備字出
考試官敎諭魏〔體謙〕批文有意味
記者舉先王治具之大行而要其爲道之全也
夫禮樂刑政所以同民心而出治也卽其大行
而王道之全在玆矣且記者之意謂夫先王之
立敎固本乎人情先王之治情實關乎治道何
也制禮樂以節和天下而政之與刑固所以行
而防之矣然合而觀之禮樂也者雖所以虔其
punctuated:
濟濟多士，文王以寧；王國克生，維周之楨。宜若氣化之使然矣。及觀《棫樸》之詩，乃知周王作人之有自，而又以緝煕之德先之，此所以成人有德而治化隆美也。若夫過魯之祀、臨雍之拜，非不知敎也，而卒不能復先王之舊焉。噫！本之則無，如之何其不漢也？

禮樂刑政四達而不悖，則王道備矣。
徐養大
同考試官敎諭張〔邦臣〕批：「鋪敘禮樂刑政四字，甚有關鍵，程式之文也。」
考試官敎諭鄭〔延年〕批：「說備字出。」
考試官敎諭魏〔體謙〕批：「文有意味。」

記者舉先王治具之大行，而要其爲道之全也。夫禮樂刑政，所以同民心而出治也。卽其大行，而王道之全在玆矣。且記者之意，謂夫先王之立敎固本乎人情，先王之治情實關乎治道。何也？制禮樂以節和天下，而政之與刑，固所以行而防之矣。然合而觀之，禮樂也者，雖所以虔其
translation_en:
…“Numerous were the worthy men; through them King Wen enjoyed tranquility.” “The royal state could bring forth men who were the pillars of Zhou.” It might seem that the transforming operations of vital energy had brought this about. Yet upon examining the ode “The Oak Trees” (Yupu), we recognize that the Zhou king’s cultivation of men had a foundation, and that he led them through his own virtue of continuous cultivation and illumination. This is why men attained maturity in virtue and why government and moral transformation flourished so splendidly. As for the sacrifice offered when passing through Lu and the obeisance performed upon visiting the Biyong ceremonial college, these did not show ignorance of education. Yet they ultimately failed to restore the institutions of the former kings. Alas! When one seeks their foundation, there is none; how could this have been anything other than the Han approach?

“When rites, music, punishments, and government operate everywhere without conflict, the Kingly Way is complete.”
By Xu Yangda.
Associate Examiner Zhang〔Bangchen〕, Instructor, comments: “The exposition of the four terms—rites, music, punishments, and government—has very effective connections. This is an essay worthy of serving as a model.”
Examiner Zheng〔Yannian〕, Instructor, comments: “It brings out the meaning of the word ‘complete.’”
Examiner Wei〔Tiqian〕, Instructor, comments: “The essay has depth of meaning.”

The compiler of the Record of Rites cites the far-reaching operation of the former kings’ instruments of government, drawing together their completeness as a Way. Rites, music, punishments, and government are the means of unifying the people’s hearts and bringing forth good governance. In their far-reaching operation lies the completeness of the Kingly Way. Moreover, the compiler’s meaning is that the former kings’ establishment of instruction was firmly rooted in human feelings, and that their regulation of those feelings was intimately connected with the Way of governing. Why is this? They instituted rites and music to regulate and harmonize all under Heaven, while government and punishments were precisely the means of putting these into effect and guarding against transgressions. Yet, considered together, rites and music, although they serve to bring reverence to their …

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
始而刑政也者實所以厚其終均之可以適乎
治也誠於是四者變通以盡利而推之必準文
德昭誕敷之休鼓舞以盡神而動之必化庶民
協歸極之應服習其敎而天下以中以和焉唯
其達而莫予違也遵守其法而天下以懲以勸
焉隨所施而無敢逾也夫如是而王道有弗備
矣乎蓋治道具而四達之未能失則偏矣治具
達而有一之或悖失則間矣要之皆不足以言
備也玆惟愼感之具旣以通行而無違則治平
===
之術自是咸正而無缺優游平中德之盛也蓋
無偏無黨而王道之蕩蕩者有以會其全天下
化中治之極也蓋無反無側而王道之平平者
有以盡其大謂之曰備信乎所過者化所存者
神上下與天地同流矣豈曰小補之哉吁此先
王之所以爲不可及也歟大抵先王之治本於
道先王之道本於心心也者道之統而治之原
也故因心以達道則禮樂刑政皆足以維治使
規規於法制之末而無本以出之雖欲言治皆
punctuated: 始，而刑政也者，實所以厚其終，均之可以適乎治也。誠於是四者，變通以盡利，而推之必準，文德昭誕敷之休；鼓舞以盡神，而動之必化，庶民協歸極之應。服習其敎，而天下以中以和焉，唯其達而莫予違也；遵守其法，而天下以懲以勸焉，隨所施而無敢逾也。夫如是，而王道有弗備矣乎？蓋治道具而四達之未能，失則偏矣；治具達而有一之或悖，失則間矣。要之，皆不足以言備也。玆惟愼感之具，旣以通行而無違，則治平之術，自是咸正而無缺。優游平中，德之盛也，蓋無偏無黨，而王道之蕩蕩者，有以會其全；天下化中，治之極也，蓋無反無側，而王道之平平者，有以盡其大。謂之曰備，信乎所過者化，所存者神，上下與天地同流矣，豈曰小補之哉？吁！此先王之所以爲不可及也歟！大抵先王之治本於道，先王之道本於心。心也者，道之統而治之原也。故因心以達道，則禮樂刑政皆足以維治；使規規於法制之末，而無本以出之，雖欲言治，皆
translation_en:
…at the beginning, while punishments and government are in fact the means of bringing their completion to fullness. All alike can conduce to good order. If, in employing these four, one truly adapts to changing circumstances so as to realize every benefit, their application will assuredly accord with the proper standard: this is the auspicious achievement of making civil virtue manifest and spreading it widely. If one inspires and animates the people so as to realize their full spiritual efficacy, every action will assuredly transform them: the response will be that the common people unite in turning toward the supreme standard. Practicing and becoming accustomed to these teachings, all under Heaven attain equilibrium and harmony; the teachings reach everywhere, and none oppose them. Observing these laws, all under Heaven are restrained from wrongdoing and encouraged toward goodness; wherever the laws are applied, none dare transgress them. With things thus, could anything be lacking in the Kingly Way?

When the means of government are complete but cannot reach in all four directions, the failing is partiality. When the instruments of government reach everywhere but even one runs counter to the others, the failing is discontinuity. In either case, one cannot speak of completeness. Once these instruments of careful influence [?] operate everywhere without opposition, the arts of governing and bringing peace will consequently all be correct and without deficiency. To dwell at ease in balance and equilibrium is the fullness of virtue: free of partiality and faction, the broad and expansive Kingly Way can thereby be realized in its entirety. For all under Heaven to be transformed toward equilibrium is the utmost achievement of government: free of perversity and deviation, the level and even Kingly Way can thereby attain its full greatness. Calling this completeness is indeed justified: wherever the sage passes, transformation follows; wherever he abides, his influence is spiritual. Above and below, he flows together with Heaven and Earth. How could this be called merely a minor contribution? Ah! Is this not what makes the former kings impossible to equal?

In general, the government of the former kings was rooted in the Way, and their Way was rooted in the heart. The heart unifies the Way and is the source of government. Thus, if one proceeds from the heart to realize the Way, ritual, music, punishments, and government are all sufficient to sustain good order. But if one confines oneself narrowly to the peripheral details of laws and institutions, without a root from which they issue, then, even if one wishes to speak of government, all …

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
淺也嗚呼有天德便可語王道其要只在謹獨
有志於先王之治者當自得之
第貳場
論
聖人至德淵微自然之應
王祖嫡
同考試官教諭何三畏批聖人之德之化本與天一
而子能以誠字發之眞達天人之蘊者宜首多士
同考試官學正劉鵬翊批規格不凡而詞氣充沛可
以占所養矣
===
考試官教諭鄭延年批立意圓融致辭暢順而淵
微之妙獨能發揮眞切宜錄以式
考試官教諭魏體謙批博學高識語意不凡且議
論正大能發天人之蘊
聖人之德天德也其脩諸已也非有所爲也其
民之化也亦非於我有所徇也機之相感而自
神者乎機者非他也誠也天下之理誠則無思
有思則非誠矣誠則無爲有爲則非誠矣誠也
punctuated:
淺也。嗚呼！有天德便可語王道，其要只在謹獨。有志於先王之治者，當自得之。

第貳場
論
聖人至德淵微自然之應
王祖嫡

同考試官教諭何三畏批：聖人之德之化，本與天一，而子能以誠字發之，眞達天人之蘊者，宜首多士。

同考試官學正劉鵬翊批：規格不凡，而詞氣充沛，可以占所養矣。

考試官教諭鄭延年批：立意圓融，致辭暢順，而淵微之妙，獨能發揮眞切，宜錄以式。

考試官教諭魏體謙批：博學高識，語意不凡，且議論正大，能發天人之蘊。

聖人之德，天德也。其脩諸已也，非有所爲也；其民之化也，亦非於我有所徇也。機之相感而自神者乎？機者非他也，誠也。天下之理，誠則無思，有思則非誠矣；誠則無爲，有爲則非誠矣。誠也
translation_en:
…is shallow. Alas! Only with Heaven’s virtue can one speak of the kingly Way; its essential requirement lies simply in vigilance when alone. Those who aspire to the government of the former kings should apprehend this for themselves.

Second Session
Discourse
“The Sage’s Supreme Virtue: Its Profundity and Subtlety, and the Spontaneous Response It Elicits”
Wang Zudi

Comment by Associate Examiner He Sanwei, Instructor: “The transforming influence of the sage’s virtue is fundamentally one with Heaven. You have elucidated it through the word ‘sincerity,’ truly penetrating the deepest workings of Heaven and humanity. You deserve to rank first among the candidates.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu Pengyi, Instructor: “The form and structure are extraordinary, and the language brims with vigor. From these one can judge the cultivation that sustains the writer.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng Yannian, Instructor: “The conception is comprehensive and harmonious, and the expression fluent and smooth. The marvel of this profundity and subtlety is expounded with exceptional clarity and precision. This should be selected as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Wei Tiqian, Instructor: “Broad learning and lofty discernment; exceptional language and ideas. Moreover, the argument is upright and grand, bringing to light the deepest workings of Heaven and humanity.”

The sage’s virtue is Heaven’s virtue. When he cultivates it within himself, he does not act with a particular end in view; when his people are transformed, neither do they seek to comply with his personal wishes. Is this not the incipient impulse of mutual responsiveness, spontaneously displaying its spiritual efficacy? This impulse is nothing other than sincerity. Such is the principle governing all under Heaven: sincerity involves no deliberate thought; where there is deliberate thought, there is no sincerity. Sincerity involves no contrived action; where there is contrived action, there is no sincerity. Sincerity…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
者天之命也性之眞也道之原也人見聖人會
天下之理于一心以爲聖人思以易天下也而
不知盡吾之所當爲曷嘗有所期哉又見其民
之遷善敏德不誡而中也以爲其民之徇上所
欲也而不知其悅聖人先得我心之同然鼓之
舞之而不自知耳一有不誠則致飾襲取上以
之而要乎下也聲音笑貌下以之而徇其上也
奚足以語自然之應哉聖人之德天德也聖人
之心天心也淵微之化亦與天同運之而已矣
===
吾嘗仰觀於天之道而有以知聖人之德矣今
夫確然上覆示人易矣人但見其秉陽而垂日
星也成象而見變化也而不知其無極之眞二
五之精於穆不已之命宰於沖漠之表而莫得
其蘊也妙於陰陽之運而莫測其機也屈伸於
往來之微而莫窺其朕也由是闔闢之爲陰陽
循其則也昭布之爲日月順其常也推遷之爲
寒暑不爽其候也星辰經緯之各合其度也飛
潛動植之各若其性也聲色象貌之不易其恒
punctuated:
者，天之命也，性之眞也，道之原也。人見聖人會天下之理于一心，以爲聖人思以易天下也，而不知盡吾之所當爲，曷嘗有所期哉？又見其民之遷善敏德，不誡而中也，以爲其民之徇上所欲也，而不知其悅聖人先得我心之同然，鼓之舞之而不自知耳。一有不誠，則致飾襲取，上以之而要乎下也；聲音笑貌，下以之而徇其上也。奚足以語自然之應哉？聖人之德，天德也；聖人之心，天心也。淵微之化，亦與天同運之而已矣。

吾嘗仰觀於天之道，而有以知聖人之德矣。今夫確然上覆，示人易矣。人但見其秉陽而垂日星也，成象而見變化也，而不知其無極之眞、二五之精、於穆不已之命，宰於沖漠之表而莫得其蘊也，妙於陰陽之運而莫測其機也，屈伸於往來之微而莫窺其朕也。由是闔闢之爲陰陽，循其則也；昭布之爲日月，順其常也；推遷之爲寒暑，不爽其候也；星辰經緯之各合其度也；飛潛動植之各若其性也；聲色象貌之不易其恒
translation_en:
…is Heaven’s mandate, the genuineness of human nature, and the source of the Way. People see the sage gathering the principles of all under Heaven into a single mind and suppose that he deliberates in order to transform the world. They do not understand that he merely fulfills what he ought to do: when has he ever sought a particular outcome? They also see his people turning toward goodness and diligently cultivating virtue, attaining what is right without admonition, and suppose that the people are complying with their ruler’s desires. They do not understand that the people delight in the sage’s having already grasped what their own hearts alike acknowledge; they are stirred and moved without themselves knowing it. Once sincerity is lacking, those above resort to embellishment and borrowed appearances [?] to exact compliance from those below, while those below use tones of voice and smiling expressions to gratify those above. How could this deserve to be called a spontaneous response? The sage’s virtue is Heaven’s virtue; the sage’s mind is Heaven’s mind. His profound and subtle transforming influence simply operates together with Heaven.

I have looked up and contemplated Heaven’s Way, and thereby come to understand the sage’s virtue. Now Heaven firmly arches over us, and what it displays is readily apparent. People see only that it holds the yang force and suspends the sun and stars, and that it forms images and manifests transformations. They do not understand its reality of the Limitless, its essence of the two forces and five phases, or its profound and unceasing mandate. It governs beyond the realm of undifferentiated stillness, yet none can grasp its depths; it works wondrously through the movements of yin and yang, yet none can fathom its workings; it contracts and expands in the subtleties of coming and going, yet none can discern its traces. Thus the closing and opening that constitute yin and yang follow their rules; the radiant display of sun and moon follows its constant course; the succession of cold and heat never misses its appointed season; the fixed positions and movements of the stars each accord with their proper measures; flying and swimming creatures, animals and plants each follow their own natures; sounds, colors, forms, and appearances do not depart from their constancy…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
也其應乎天者一出於自然也夫其應之自然
者天運之自然者感之也易曰大哉乾乎剛健
中正純粹精也夫純者至一而不二粹者至美
而不雜精則微妙難名而聲臭俱無矣非誠乎
又曰大哉乾元萬物資始誠之源也各正性命
保合太和誠斯立焉非誠之應乎聖人者法天
者也天生人而篤於聖人聖人獨得天之秀而
最靈者故其德之脩諸已者無不求與天合焉
洗心以退藏於密而無一私之累也齊戒以神
===
明其德而無一念之忽也思慮雖未起而亦臨
亦保之念恒存焉耳目雖未交而勿視勿聽之
念恒存焉事物雖未接而勿二勿三之念恒存
焉故端嚴疑重主乎一而已矣玄微澄徹守乎
靜而已矣明通靈瑩致乎虚而已矣夫主一以
待天下之賾則賾雖日至而不眩也守靜以臨
天下之動則動雖萬變而不惑也致虚以應天
下之務則務雖沓至而不乖也夫聖人議道自
已建極於民使徒於聲音形迹是脩而弗於其
punctuated:
也。其應乎天者，一出於自然也。夫其應之自然者，天運之自然者感之也。《易》曰：「大哉乾乎！剛健中正，純粹精也。」夫純者，至一而不二；粹者，至美而不雜；精則微妙難名，而聲臭俱無矣。非誠乎？又曰：「大哉乾元，萬物資始。」誠之源也。「各正性命，保合太和。」誠斯立焉。非誠之應乎？

聖人者，法天者也。天生人，而篤於聖人。聖人獨得天之秀而最靈者，故其德之脩諸已者，無不求與天合焉。洗心以退藏於密，而無一私之累也；齊戒以神明其德，而無一念之忽也。思慮雖未起，而亦臨亦保之念恒存焉；耳目雖未交，而勿視勿聽之念恒存焉；事物雖未接，而勿二勿三之念恒存焉。故端嚴疑重，主乎一而已矣；玄微澄徹，守乎靜而已矣；明通靈瑩，致乎虚而已矣。夫主一以待天下之賾，則賾雖日至而不眩也；守靜以臨天下之動，則動雖萬變而不惑也；致虚以應天下之務，則務雖沓至而不乖也。夫聖人議道自已，建極於民，使徒於聲音形迹是脩，而弗於其
translation_en:
…All that responds to Heaven does so spontaneously. This spontaneity of response arises because the spontaneous workings of Heaven move it. The Book of Changes says: “Great indeed is Qian! Firm and vigorous, central and correct, pure, unmixed, and refined.” To be pure is to be utterly one, without division; to be unmixed is to be supremely beautiful, without admixture; to be refined is to be subtle and mysterious beyond naming, without either sound or scent. Is this not sincerity? It also says: “Great indeed is the primal power of Qian! The myriad things draw upon it for their beginning.” This is the source of sincerity. “Each attains its proper nature and destiny, preserving and uniting in supreme harmony.” Here sincerity is established. Is this not the response elicited by sincerity?

The sage takes Heaven as his model. Heaven gives birth to human beings, but endows the sage especially richly. The sage alone receives Heaven’s finest and most spiritually perceptive essence; thus, in cultivating virtue within himself, he invariably seeks accord with Heaven. He cleanses his heart and withdraws into hidden stillness, unburdened by even a single selfish concern. Through purification and abstinence, he makes his virtue spiritually luminous, without a single careless thought. Though reflection has not yet arisen, the thought of Heaven’s watching over and protecting him remains constantly present. Though his ears and eyes have not yet engaged with anything, the resolve not to look or listen improperly remains constantly present. Though he has not yet encountered affairs and things, the resolve not to waver between two or three courses remains constantly present. Thus, his upright solemnity and gravity [?] consist simply in maintaining oneness; his profound subtlety and limpid clarity consist simply in preserving stillness; his luminous understanding and spiritual lucidity consist simply in attaining emptiness. By maintaining oneness to meet the complexities of the world, he is not bewildered even when they arrive daily. By preserving stillness to confront the world’s movements, he is not confused even by their myriad transformations. By attaining emptiness to respond to the world’s affairs, he does not go astray even when they come crowding upon him. The sage considers the Way beginning with himself [?] and establishes the supreme standard for the people. If he were merely to cultivate sounds and outward forms, without applying himself to what is…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
幽深玄遠者是務則天下之民亦相率而馳於
外矣其何以化成天下哉故至敬昭融則本原
培植心得旣至則見外自章由是發之爲七情
則喜怒哀懼愛惡欲之施罔不中其節也敘之
爲五典則君臣父子夫婦長幼朋友之勅罔不
若其倫也敷之爲庶政則大而朝廷宗廟之儀
細而食息起居之節莫不協于理也是豈聖人
作意而爲之哉至德積於中英華發於外聖人
不自知其然也由是天下之人見聖人情之中
===
其節也相率約其情而作好作惡者遠也見聖
人倫之敘也相率惇其典而反道敗德者遠也
見聖人庶務之協于理也相率會其極歸其極
而偏陂偏黨者遠也邇之而家一家之人無不
應也遠之而國一國之人無不應也推極之於
萬方萬方之人無不應也是非天下之求悅乎
聖人也神而化之使民宜之天下亦不自知也
是何也人心有同然之理聖人旣先得之而又
以默成之孚不言之信率先于上焉故觸之而
punctuated: 幽深玄遠者是務，則天下之民亦相率而馳於外矣，其何以化成天下哉？故至敬昭融，則本原培植；心得旣至，則見外自章。由是發之爲七情，則喜怒哀懼愛惡欲之施罔不中其節也；敘之爲五典，則君臣父子夫婦長幼朋友之勅罔不若其倫也；敷之爲庶政，則大而朝廷宗廟之儀，細而食息起居之節，莫不協于理也。是豈聖人作意而爲之哉？至德積於中，英華發於外，聖人不自知其然也。由是天下之人見聖人情之中其節也，相率約其情，而作好作惡者遠也；見聖人倫之敘也，相率惇其典，而反道敗德者遠也；見聖人庶務之協于理也，相率會其極、歸其極，而偏陂偏黨者遠也。邇之而家，一家之人無不應也；遠之而國，一國之人無不應也；推極之於萬方，萬方之人無不應也。是非天下之求悅乎聖人也，神而化之，使民宜之，天下亦不自知也。是何也？人心有同然之理，聖人旣先得之，而又以默成之孚、不言之信率先于上焉，故觸之而
translation_en:
…what is deep, subtle, mysterious, and far-reaching, then the people throughout the world will likewise follow one another in pursuing externals. How could the sage thereby transform and perfect the world? Thus, when utmost reverence shines forth in its fullness, the roots are nourished; when inward understanding reaches its utmost, its outward manifestation naturally becomes evident. Expressed as the seven emotions, joy, anger, sorrow, fear, love, hatred, and desire are invariably appropriate in their measure. Ordered as the five constant relationships, the regulation of relations between ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friend and friend invariably accords with their proper order. Extended to the various affairs of government, everything accords with principle, from the great ceremonies of the court and ancestral temple to the small observances of eating, resting, rising, and retiring. Does the sage accomplish this through deliberate effort? Supreme virtue accumulates within, and its brilliance manifests without; the sage himself is unaware of how it comes about.

Consequently, when people throughout the world see that the sage’s emotions attain their proper measure, they follow one another in restraining their own emotions, and arbitrary likes and dislikes recede. When they see the order of the sage’s human relationships, they follow one another in giving due weight to those constant relationships, and conduct that contravenes the Way and corrupts virtue recedes. When they see that the sage’s many affairs accord with principle, they follow one another in assembling around his supreme standard and returning to it, and partiality and factionalism recede. Close at hand, within the family, everyone responds; farther afield, within the state, everyone responds; extended to all regions, everyone everywhere responds. This is not because the world seeks to please the sage. Through a wondrous transformation, he brings the people into fitting accord, and the world itself is unaware of how this happens. Why is this so? Human hearts share principles that they alike acknowledge. The sage has apprehended these first and, moreover, leads from above through the trust engendered by silent accomplishment and the confidence inspired without words. Thus, when he touches them …

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
即感作之而即興不戒以孚也不疾而速也不
行而至也非天下之至誠其孰能與於此哉易
之觀曰大觀在上順而巽中正以觀天下又曰
下觀而化也咸曰聖人感人心而天下和平夫
順巽中正聖人之至德也固足以致下觀之化
矣然必感人心而後天下和平焉是可以知淵
微之德之應矣推而極之以至德而祀天則天
神可格以至德而事地則地祇可感所謂天不
愛道地不愛寶河出馬圖山出器車而諸福之
===
物可致之祥者畢至也以至德而曲成乎萬物
也則天時有生地利有養胎生者不殰卵生者
不殈而無一物不得其所者可致也何莫而非
自然之應哉向使涵養之未極其純充積之未
極其盛則一間未達難以語神形迹尚存難以
語化而其應亦朋從之思耳夫淵微之德一真
內融萬境俱徹求之而無方即之而無體恍惚
而莫可為象者也而自然之應則言乎遠不禦
也言乎邇靜而正也言乎天地之間則備焉是
punctuated:
即感，作之而即興，不戒以孚也，不疾而速也，不行而至也。非天下之至誠，其孰能與於此哉？《易》之《觀》曰：「大觀在上，順而巽，中正以觀天下。」又曰：「下觀而化也。」《咸》曰：「聖人感人心而天下和平。」夫順巽中正，聖人之至德也，固足以致下觀之化矣。然必感人心而後天下和平焉，是可以知淵微之德之應矣。

推而極之，以至德而祀天，則天神可格；以至德而事地，則地祇可感。所謂「天不愛道，地不愛寶，河出馬圖，山出器車」，而諸福之物、可致之祥者畢至也。以至德而曲成乎萬物也，則天時有生，地利有養，胎生者不殰，卵生者不殈，而無一物不得其所者可致也。何莫而非自然之應哉？向使涵養之未極其純，充積之未極其盛，則一間未達，難以語神；形迹尚存，難以語化；而其應亦朋從之思耳。

夫淵微之德，一真內融，萬境俱徹，求之而無方，即之而無體，恍惚而莫可為象者也。而自然之應，則言乎遠，不禦也；言乎邇，靜而正也；言乎天地之間，則備焉。是
translation_en:
…they respond at once; when stirred, they rise at once. Trust is secured without admonition; there is speed without haste and arrival without travel. Who but one possessed of the utmost sincerity under Heaven could participate in this? The Book of Changes says of the hexagram Guan (Contemplation): “The great spectacle is above; compliant and yielding, central and correct, he displays himself to all under Heaven.” It also says: “Those below look upon him and are transformed.” Of Xian (Influence), it says: “The sage moves people’s hearts, and all under Heaven becomes peaceful and harmonious.” Compliance, yielding, centrality, and correctness constitute the sage’s supreme virtue, which is certainly sufficient to bring about the transformation of those below who look upon him. Yet only after people’s hearts have been moved does all under Heaven become peaceful and harmonious. From this we may understand the response evoked by profound and subtle virtue.

Extend this to its fullest reach: when one sacrifices to Heaven with supreme virtue, the celestial spirits can be brought to approach; when one serves Earth with supreme virtue, the terrestrial spirits can be moved. This is what is meant by “Heaven does not withhold its Way; Earth does not withhold its treasures; the river brings forth the horse diagram, and the mountains bring forth vessels and carriages.” All things bearing blessings, and all auspicious signs that can be elicited, arrive together. When supreme virtue brings the myriad things to fulfillment in all their particulars, Heaven’s seasons provide for their birth and Earth’s resources provide for their nourishment. Those born from the womb do not perish before birth, and those born from eggs do not perish before hatching. A condition in which every single thing finds its proper place can thus be attained. Which of these is not a spontaneous response? If cultivation had not reached the utmost purity, and the accumulation of virtue had not reached its fullest abundance, then even a single gap left unpenetrated would make it difficult to speak of spiritual efficacy. If outward forms and traces still remained, it would be difficult to speak of transformation. The response evoked would then amount merely to the thought that draws one’s companions to follow.

Profound and subtle virtue is a single genuine reality, inwardly integrated, through which all realms are fully penetrated. Seek it, and it has no location; approach it, and it has no form. Elusive and indistinct, it cannot be represented by an image. As for its spontaneous response: speaking of what is distant, nothing checks it; speaking of what is near, it is still and correct; speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, it encompasses everything. This is…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
之謂發微不可見充周不可窮聖道之所以爲
神也然此豈聖人之絕德哉天下雷行物與無
妄誠敬之賦途人與聖人同也性以情動情以
物遷而昏昧放逸自喪其良者衆也豈惟夫人
賢者能存之矣然功未造於精純德未入於玄
妙此淵微之至所以獨歸於聖人歟知夫人之
所以失則知聖人之所以得矣然聖人亦豈能
外至誠以爲之本哉雖然未至於聖者如之何
曰爲己其始也知幾其要也謹獨其功也根之
===
以勉強行道之心馴習於日進有功之域則淵
微之德在我而自然之應日臻矣苟憚力行黽
勉之勞而求徑超頓悟之術卒流於猖狂自恣
之歸而去道遠矣善學者尚鑒兹哉
表
擬
賀
西苑瑞穀表
李際春
punctuated:
之謂發微不可見，充周不可窮，聖道之所以爲神也。然此豈聖人之絕德哉？天下雷行，物與無妄，誠敬之賦，途人與聖人同也。性以情動，情以物遷，而昏昧放逸、自喪其良者衆也。豈惟夫人？賢者能存之矣，然功未造於精純，德未入於玄妙，此淵微之至所以獨歸於聖人歟？知夫人之所以失，則知聖人之所以得矣。然聖人亦豈能外至誠以爲之本哉？雖然，未至於聖者如之何？曰：爲己，其始也；知幾，其要也；謹獨，其功也。根之以勉強行道之心，馴習於日進有功之域，則淵微之德在我，而自然之應日臻矣。苟憚力行黽勉之勞，而求徑超頓悟之術，卒流於猖狂自恣之歸，而去道遠矣。善學者尚鑒兹哉！

表

擬賀西苑瑞穀表
李際春
translation_en:
…is what is meant by manifestation so subtle that it cannot be seen, and an all-pervading fullness that cannot be exhausted: this is what makes the Way of the sage numinous. Yet how could this virtue belong exclusively to sages? Thunder moves beneath heaven, and all things partake of freedom from falsity; the ordinary passerby and the sage are alike endowed with sincerity and reverence. Human nature is stirred by feelings, and feelings shift in response to things; many become benighted and unrestrained, themselves forfeiting their innate goodness. But why speak only of ordinary people? The worthy can preserve it, yet their efforts have not attained perfect refinement and purity, nor has their virtue entered the realm of profound subtlety. Is this why the utmost depth and subtlety belong to sages alone? If we understand how ordinary people lose it, we understand how sages attain it. Yet how could even sages take anything other than utmost sincerity as their foundation?

Nevertheless, what should those who have not attained sagehood do? The answer is: learning for oneself is the beginning; discerning the first subtle signs is the essential point; vigilance when alone is the work required. Root these in a determination to exert oneself in practicing the Way, and cultivate them steadily until daily progress brings results. Then profound and subtle virtue will reside within oneself, and its spontaneous responses will arrive day by day. If one fears the toil of strenuous practice and diligent effort, seeking instead techniques for leaping straight ahead to sudden enlightenment, one will ultimately lapse into reckless self-indulgence and stray far from the Way. May those who would learn well take heed of this!

Memorial

Draft Memorial Congratulating the Emperor on Auspicious Grain in the Western Park (Xiyuan)
By Li Jichun

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭王敬賓批體裁莊重造語峻切其於
我
皇上敬天勤民之應頌揚得出亦四六之最佳者錄之
同考試官教諭熊彥臣批典則而麗懇至而文敬服
敬服
同考試官教諭張旆批思深詞婉能揄揚我
皇上仁孝盛心可以占忠愛矣錄之
考試官教諭鄭延年批稱頌有體辭氣謹嚴是文
表之優者
===
考試官教諭魏體謙批駢麗典雅鏗鏘可誦錄式
多士允宜允宜
嘉靖三十七年某月某日具官臣某等恭
遇
西苑進瑞穀一本三穗者一雙穗五十五謹
奉
表稱
賀者伏以貺錫
皇穹紫極介無前之慶瑞呈
punctuated:
同考試官教諭王敬賓批：體裁莊重，造語峻切，其於我皇上敬天勤民之應，頌揚得出，亦四六之最佳者，錄之。

同考試官教諭熊彥臣批：典則而麗，懇至而文，敬服，敬服。

同考試官教諭張旆批：思深詞婉，能揄揚我皇上仁孝盛心，可以占忠愛矣，錄之。

考試官教諭鄭延年批：稱頌有體，辭氣謹嚴，是文表之優者。

考試官教諭魏體謙批：駢麗典雅，鏗鏘可誦，錄式多士，允宜，允宜。

嘉靖三十七年某月某日，具官臣某等，恭遇西苑進瑞穀一本三穗者一，雙穗五十五，謹奉表稱賀者。伏以貺錫皇穹，紫極介無前之慶；瑞呈
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang Jingbin, Instructor: Its form is dignified and its phrasing forceful and apt. It successfully praises the auspicious response to our Emperor’s reverence for Heaven and diligent care for the people. This is also among the finest examples of four-and-six parallel prose. Include it.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiong Yanchen, Instructor: It follows classical standards yet is beautiful; it is deeply earnest yet polished. I admire it, I admire it.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang Pei, Instructor: Its thought is profound and its language graceful. It extols our Emperor’s abundant benevolence and filial devotion, revealing the writer’s loyalty and love. Include it.

Comment by Examiner Zheng Yannian, Instructor: Its praise observes the proper forms, and its language and tone are reverent and restrained. This composition is an outstanding memorial.

Comment by Examiner Wei Tiqian, Instructor: Its parallel phrasing is beautiful, classical, and elegant; its resonant cadences invite recitation. It is most fitting, most fitting, to include it as a model for the many scholars.

On an unspecified day of an unspecified month in the thirty-seventh year of Jiajing, your servants, so-and-so and others, holding the duly stated offices, reverently mark the presentation from the Western Park of auspicious grain: one stalk bearing three ears and fifty-five bearing two ears. We respectfully submit this memorial of congratulation. We humbly consider: blessings are bestowed by August Heaven, and the imperial court receives unprecedented felicity; auspicious signs appear …

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
帝畝瑤符徵有道之昌
節將届於流虹
禎遂同於舒筴頌聲雷動喜氣天開臣等誠
懽誠忭稽首頓首上言竊惟王業以稼穡
爲艱明神非粢盛不享豳風教遠宜賡七
月之篇周制禮洽斯受百靈之祐睠玆仙
種植自
天田
帝耒昔荷於三推農扈玆欣於首
===
獻飽
明廷之渥露孕毓瓊膏挹
太液之清塵光生玉顆三岐竝峙畫應乾爻
二穎交芳數占坤偶準河圖生成之策秉
五分雙協太極動靜之元函三爲一迎眸
而山川薦爽觸手則
殿閣生香巧若天成
麻真神授彼合懽連理會何補於民生曁竹
實杉花詎有資於國用猶且一時歆動奄
punctuated: 帝畝，瑤符徵有道之昌。節將届於流虹，禎遂同於舒筴。頌聲雷動，喜氣天開。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首上言：竊惟王業以稼穡爲艱，明神非粢盛不享。豳風教遠，宜賡七月之篇；周制禮洽，斯受百靈之祐。睠玆仙種，植自天田。帝耒昔荷於三推，農扈玆欣於首獻。飽明廷之渥露，孕毓瓊膏；挹太液之清塵，光生玉顆。三岐竝峙，畫應乾爻；二穎交芳，數占坤偶。準河圖生成之策，秉五分雙；協太極動靜之元，函三爲一。迎眸而山川薦爽，觸手則殿閣生香。巧若天成，麻真神授。彼合懽連理，會何補於民生？曁竹實杉花，詎有資於國用？猶且一時歆動，奄
translation_en:
…in the imperial fields; precious tokens attest to the flourishing of a reign possessing the Way. As the festival of the flowing rainbow approaches [the imperial birthday], this auspicious sign accords with the unfolding of the divining stalks [?]. Acclamations thunder forth, and joyful radiance fills the heavens. We, your servants, truly rejoice and exult; bowing our heads to the ground and repeatedly kowtowing, we submit these words:
We humbly reflect that the royal enterprise regards sowing and reaping as arduous, and that the luminous spirits accept no offerings without sacrificial grain. The instruction conveyed by the Airs of Bin reaches far: fittingly should we continue the song of the Seventh Month. The ritual institutions of Zhou are comprehensive: thus are blessings received from the hundred spirits. Behold this wondrous seed, planted in the fields of Heaven. In former days Your Majesty took up the imperial plough for the three ritual pushes; now the agricultural officers rejoice in presenting the first offering. Sated with the rich dew of the illustrious court, it nurtures a jade-like richness within; drawing upon the pure dust of Taiye Pool [?], its jade-like kernels shine. Three branches stand side by side, their configuration corresponding to the lines of Qian; two ears mingle their fragrance, their number betokening the paired lines of Kun. It conforms to the River Chart’s numerical scheme of generation and completion, taking five and dividing into pairs [?]; it accords with the Supreme Ultimate’s source of movement and stillness, embracing three as one. At its appearance, mountains and rivers offer refreshing purity; at its touch, halls and pavilions give forth fragrance. Its ingenuity seems fashioned by Heaven; the hemp is truly bestowed by spirits [?]. What benefit, after all, do those joined blossoms and interlocking branches bring to the people’s livelihood? And how could bamboo fruit and fir blossoms contribute to the needs of the state? Yet even these stirred admiration in their own time and forthwith…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
致異代流傳寧如
秘苑之嘉生真爲
熈朝之上瑞時如有待物豈無知恭惟
皇帝陛下
體合重玄
心涵太始
中和建極敬
天法
祖勤民
===
作述成能議禮考文制度萃道孚而饗
親饗
帝乾綱運而克長克
君八政弘宣五兵靜戢肆
沖和之融液上及
太清下及太寧聿
景祜之昭垂天不愛道地不愛寳期當應
聖熒光合而黄河清徵在
延齡雲馭來而白鹿見丹芝燁燁產屬名山
punctuated: 致異代流傳，寧如秘苑之嘉生，真爲熈朝之上瑞？時如有待，物豈無知？恭惟皇帝陛下，體合重玄，心涵太始，中和建極，敬天法祖勤民，作述成能，議禮考文制度萃。道孚而饗親饗帝，乾綱運而克長克君。八政弘宣，五兵靜戢。肆沖和之融液，上及太清，下及太寧。聿景祜之昭垂，天不愛道，地不愛寳。期當應聖，熒光合而黄河清；徵在延齡，雲馭來而白鹿見。丹芝燁燁，產屬名山。
translation_en:
… brought them renown transmitted to later ages. Yet how could they compare with this auspicious growth in the imperial garden, truly a supreme auspice of this illustrious reign? If the time seemed to await its arrival, could the thing itself have been unaware?

We reverently consider Your Majesty the Emperor: your person accords with the profound mystery, and your mind embraces the primordial beginning. Through equilibrium and harmony you establish the supreme standard; you revere Heaven, emulate your ancestors, and diligently care for the people. In creating and transmitting, you fulfill your capacities; in deliberating on rites and examining cultural forms, you bring institutions to perfection. Your Way inspires trust, and you offer sacrifices to your ancestors and to the Lord on High; the sovereign authority operates, and you prove capable as leader and ruler. The eight concerns of government are broadly attended to, and the five kinds of weapons lie quietly stored away. Thus the permeating influence of your perfect harmony reaches upward to the highest heavens and downward to the realm of great peace. Thereupon great blessings visibly descend: Heaven does not withhold its Way, nor Earth its treasures.

At the time appointed to respond to the sage ruler, luminous celestial influences unite [?], and the Yellow River runs clear. As a portent of lengthened life, a cloud-borne carriage arrives and a white deer appears. Brilliant red numinous fungi grow upon renowned mountains.

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
甘露瀼瀼降從琪樹瑞麥呈於齊甸寶兎
貢自巴川由載籍以來古今稀遘非
聖人不出造化奚私四表方沸康謠
九重尚勤周穡日成月要計頻質於司徒秋
報春祈禋更虔於
上帝是生神物式相
昌辰煥
璇極以迎祥應金方而擢秀將擬同玄珠而
上
===
萬壽吉應
天壇豈特豐赤穰而兆三登氣先
禁籞邁唐封之同穎陋漢代之雙岐是宜倣
神雀以紀年按芝房而度曲薦諸
郊廟彌彰
明德之馨播在裔夷共識太平之象臣等忭
承
鈞造幸接清班對
丹扆而慶
punctuated:
甘露瀼瀼，降從琪樹；瑞麥呈於齊甸，寶兎貢自巴川。由載籍以來，古今稀遘，非聖人不出，造化奚私？四表方沸康謠，九重尚勤周穡。日成月要，計頻質於司徒；秋報春祈，禋更虔於上帝。是生神物，式相昌辰。煥璇極以迎祥，應金方而擢秀。將擬同玄珠而上萬壽，吉應天壇；豈特豐赤穰而兆三登，氣先禁籞？邁唐封之同穎，陋漢代之雙岐。是宜倣神雀以紀年，按芝房而度曲。薦諸郊廟，彌彰明德之馨；播在裔夷，共識太平之象。
臣等忭承鈞造，幸接清班，對丹扆而慶
translation_en:
…Sweet dew falls abundantly from jeweled trees; auspicious wheat appears in the fields of Qi, and a precious hare is offered as tribute from Bachuan. Since written records began, such things have seldom been encountered, in antiquity or today. They do not appear unless a sage reigns: how could the powers of creation show partiality? While songs of well-being resound throughout the four quarters, within the ninefold palace Your Majesty still diligently attends to agriculture, as did the Zhou. Daily accounts and monthly summaries are repeatedly checked with the Minister of Education; in autumn thanksgiving and spring supplication, pure sacrifices are offered with ever greater reverence to the Lord on High. Thus divine things are born to assist this flourishing age. They illuminate the jeweled celestial pole to welcome auspicious blessings, answering the quarter of Metal as they put forth exceptional growth. They shall be likened to the mysterious pearl and presented with wishes for boundless longevity, their auspicious portent answering at the Altar of Heaven. Could they merely promise abundant ‘red stalks’ [?] and foretell three harvests, their vital force first appearing in the imperial gardens? They surpass the ears of grain joined together in the fief of Tang and put to shame the double-branched grain of the Han dynasty. It is fitting to follow the precedent of ‘Divine Bird’ in naming a reign era, and to compose a melody after ‘The Fungus Chamber.’ Presented at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, they further reveal the fragrance of luminous virtue; made known among distant foreign peoples, they enable all to recognize the signs of great peace.
We, your servants, joyfully receive your nurturing beneficence and are fortunate to stand among the honored ranks of officials. Facing the vermilion throne screen, we celebrate…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
元良懽均獸舞載彤管而書大有才謝麟編
一飯敢忘祗效嵩呼之
祝寸衷欲
獻載歌天保之章伏願
念切民依
功超玄化
播茲百穀水火金木土惟脩
協用庶徵雨暘燠寒風時若敷
皇極而錫福心和氣氣和形形和兩儀
===
握瑤圖而凝神一生二二生三三生萬物四
靈畢集八蜡咸通川至日升
聖筭益綿於
寶籙天長地久
國祚永保於金甌臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖忭躍慶戴之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
punctuated: 元良，懽均獸舞；載彤管而書大有，才謝麟編。一飯敢忘？祗效嵩呼之祝；寸衷欲獻，載歌天保之章。伏願念切民依，功超玄化，播茲百穀，水火金木土惟脩；協用庶徵，雨暘燠寒風時若。敷皇極而錫福，心和氣，氣和形，形和兩儀；握瑤圖而凝神，一生二，二生三，三生萬物。四靈畢集，八蜡咸通，川至日升，聖筭益綿於寶籙；天長地久，國祚永保於金甌。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、忭躍慶戴之至，謹奉表稱賀以
translation_en:
…the heir apparent, our joy shared equally with the dancing beasts. Taking up the vermilion brush to record this great abundance, our talents fall short of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Dare we forget the kindness of even a single meal? We can only offer blessings like the acclamations at Mount Song. Wishing to present our humble devotion, we sing the ode “Heaven Protects You” (Tianbao).

We humbly wish that Your Majesty may cherish deeply the people's means of livelihood, and that your achievements may surpass the mysterious workings of creation. May the hundred grains be sown, and water, fire, metal, wood, and earth be duly regulated. May the various signs be brought into accord, with rain, sunshine, warmth, cold, and wind arriving in their proper seasons. May you extend the August Norm and bestow blessings: the heart harmonizing vital energy, vital energy harmonizing bodily form, and bodily form harmonizing Heaven and Earth. May you hold the precious chart of sovereignty and concentrate your spirit: the One generates the Two, the Two generate the Three, and the Three generate the myriad things. May the four numinous creatures all assemble, and the eight year-end agricultural sacrifices all achieve communion with the spirits. Like the river's flow and the rising sun, may your sacred lifespan extend ever further in the precious registers. As enduring as Heaven and Earth, may the dynasty's fortune remain forever secure within its golden vessel.

We, your servants, look toward Heaven and gaze up at Your sagely Majesty, unable to contain our utmost rejoicing, celebration, and reverent allegiance. We respectfully submit this memorial of congratulation in order to…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
聞
第叄塲
策五道
第一問
劉奮庸
同考試官教諭王敬賓批我
皇上孝兼舜武制備明聖天下實涵泳其中而不知也子能揄揚殆盡
是留心於典章者
同考試官教諭熊藎臣批以功德明聖揄揚我
===
皇上之孝而且本之於敬一是亦用心於
明倫大典而究其深者取冠多士允宜允宜
同考試官教諭張旆批舜武之孝其大與達處古
今莫能分辨子能以功德言之亦獨得之見也
取之
考試官教諭鄭延年批揄揚我
皇上兼舜武殆盡是懷忠愛者也錄之
考試官教諭魏體謙批博學强識是能敬揚我
皇上功德之盛者
punctuated:
聞。

第叄塲。策五道。第一問。劉奮庸。

同考試官教諭王敬賓批：我皇上孝兼舜武，制備明聖，天下實涵泳其中而不知也。子能揄揚殆盡，是留心於典章者。

同考試官教諭熊藎臣批：以功德明聖揄揚我皇上之孝，而且本之於敬一，是亦用心於《明倫大典》而究其深者。取冠多士，允宜允宜。

同考試官教諭張旆批：舜武之孝，其大與達處，古今莫能分辨。子能以功德言之，亦獨得之見也。取之。

考試官教諭鄭延年批：揄揚我皇上兼舜武殆盡，是懷忠愛者也。錄之。

考試官教諭魏體謙批：博學强識，是能敬揚我皇上功德之盛者。
translation_en:
…for Your Majesty’s information.

Third Session. Five Policy Questions. First Question. Liu Fenyong.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang Jingbin, Instructor: Our Emperor combines the filial piety of Shun and King Wu; his institutions embody both enlightenment and sageliness. All under Heaven are immersed in their benefits without realizing it. You have praised these qualities almost exhaustively: you are someone who attends closely to institutions and statutes.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiong Jinchen, Instructor: You praise our Emperor’s filial piety in terms of achievements and virtue, enlightenment and sageliness, and moreover ground it in reverent concentration on the One. You have thus also applied yourself to the Great Compendium on Clarifying Human Relations (Minglun dadian) and fathomed its depths. Selecting this essay to rank first among the many candidates is most fitting, most fitting.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang Pei, Instructor: As for the filial piety of Shun and King Wu, no one, past or present, has been able to distinguish wherein lay its greatness and its universal recognition. Your ability to explain it in terms of achievements and virtue represents an insight uniquely your own. Accept it.

Comment by Examiner Zheng Yannian, Instructor: Your praise of how our Emperor combines the qualities of Shun and King Wu is nearly exhaustive. You are someone who cherishes loyalty and love for the sovereign. Accept it.

Comment by Examiner Wei Tiqian, Instructor: Broad learning and a strong memory: here is someone capable of reverently extolling the magnificence of our Emperor’s achievements and virtue.

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
至哉
聖人之孝乎貫帝王而會其全合明聖而臻其
盛者乎夫行帝道而帝行王道而王帝王
者功德之謂也作之者曰聖述之者曰明
明聖者述作之謂也然聖造同而性反自
異治化一而常變或殊則功德必至於相
掩述作不能以兼盡矣集大成以神參賛
之能妙時出而極功化之大盡善而盡美
丕顯而丕承自生民以來孰有如我
===
皇上者乎請敬陳之夫自天地定位殽倫理之
原圖書呈象洩綱常之秘三五元聖率由
是矣矧典謨所載訓誥所紀者皆古聖人
也而孔子獨賛舜武何哉蓋或處人倫之
常未極尊饗之典則雖功德之盛而未可
與於斯也孔門師弟論孝至詳孔子曰通
於神明曾子曰橫於四海故精微廣大孝
之德也孔子曰加於百姓曾子曰斷一樹
不以其時非孝故仁民愛物孝之功也舜
punctuated: 至哉，聖人之孝乎！貫帝王而會其全，合明聖而臻其盛者乎！夫行帝道而帝，行王道而王，帝王者功德之謂也。作之者曰聖，述之者曰明，明聖者述作之謂也。然聖造同而性反自異，治化一而常變或殊，則功德必至於相掩，述作不能以兼盡矣。集大成以神參賛之能，妙時出而極功化之大，盡善而盡美，丕顯而丕承，自生民以來，孰有如我皇上者乎？請敬陳之。夫自天地定位，殽倫理之原，圖書呈象，洩綱常之秘，三五元聖率由是矣。矧典謨所載、訓誥所紀者，皆古聖人也，而孔子獨賛舜武，何哉？蓋或處人倫之常，未極尊饗之典，則雖功德之盛，而未可與於斯也。孔門師弟論孝至詳。孔子曰：「通於神明。」曾子曰：「橫於四海。」故精微廣大，孝之德也。孔子曰：「加於百姓。」曾子曰：「斷一樹不以其時，非孝。」故仁民愛物，孝之功也。舜
translation_en:
How consummate is the sage’s filial piety! Does it not unite the achievements of emperors and kings in their fullness, and combine illumination and sagehood at their height? One becomes an emperor by practicing the Way of emperors, and a king by practicing the Way of kings: emperorship and kingship refer to achievement and virtue. One who creates is called a sage; one who carries on is called illuminated: illumination and sagehood refer to carrying on and creating. Yet although their attainment of sagehood is the same, some possess it by nature and others return to it through cultivation. Although their transforming governance is one, their circumstances may differ between the ordinary and the exceptional. Thus achievement and virtue inevitably overshadow one another, and carrying on and creating cannot both be fully realized. Who, since humankind first came into being, has equaled Our Emperor in gathering all excellences into a consummate whole, exercising with divine mastery the capacity to assist Heaven and Earth, responding wondrously to the demands of the time, and bringing achievement and transforming influence to their utmost greatness—perfect in goodness and beauty, gloriously manifesting and gloriously continuing the ancestral legacy? Allow me respectfully to set this forth.

Ever since Heaven and Earth assumed their positions, the source of ethical relationships was patterned forth [?]; the River Chart and the Luo Writing displayed their images, revealing the mysteries of the cardinal bonds and constant virtues. The great sages—the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors—all followed these principles. Moreover, those recorded in the Canons and Counsels, and chronicled in the Instructions and Announcements, were all ancient sages. Why, then, did Confucius single out Shun and King Wu for praise? Presumably, some lived amid the ordinary circumstances of human relationships and did not bring to their fullest extent the rites of honoring their parents and presenting offerings to them. Thus, despite the greatness of their achievements and virtue, they could not be included in this praise.

The master and disciples of Confucius’s school discussed filial piety in the greatest detail. Confucius said, “It communicates with the spirits.” Zengzi said, “It extends across the Four Seas.” Thus subtlety and vastness constitute the virtue of filial piety. Confucius said, “It reaches the common people.” Zengzi said, “To cut down a single tree at an improper season is unfilial.” Thus benevolence toward the people and care for living things constitute the achievements of filial piety. Shun…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
處父子之變致底豫之化尊富則至保饗
則備矣以之齊政輯瑞同律脩禮肇州咨
牧莫非功也而德則大武遭君臣之變舉
順應之事繼述則善追王則遠矣以之釋
囚表閭興絕舉廢致遠展親莫非德也而
功則勝邵堯夫曰堯禪舜以德武王下舜
一等則入於功矣故大以德言達以功言
各自其孝之所至者言之而豈有二哉由
舜之後千有餘年而有武王焉由武王而
===
後則貞元未合光岳久渙矣洪惟我
皇上應五百之期撫一統之運纘膺
丕緒光握
瑤符蓋遵
太祖兄終弟及之訓承
純皇子燕孫貽之謀所謂
聖作而物睹天與而人歸者也
踐阼之初首
詔廷臣議舉
punctuated:
處父子之變，致底豫之化，尊富則至，保饗則備矣。以之齊政輯瑞，同律脩禮，肇州咨牧，莫非功也，而德則大。武遭君臣之變，舉順應之事，繼述則善，追王則遠矣。以之釋囚表閭，興絕舉廢，致遠展親，莫非德也，而功則勝。邵堯夫曰：「堯禪舜以德，武王下舜一等，則入於功矣。」故大以德言，達以功言，各自其孝之所至者言之，而豈有二哉？由舜之後千有餘年而有武王焉，由武王而後，則貞元未合，光岳久渙矣。
洪惟我皇上，應五百之期，撫一統之運，纘膺丕緒，光握瑤符，蓋遵太祖兄終弟及之訓，承純皇子燕孫貽之謀，所謂聖作而物睹、天與而人歸者也。踐阼之初，首詔廷臣議舉
translation_en:
…Faced with an extraordinary rupture in the relationship between father and son, [Shun] brought about a transformation that ultimately made his father content. His honor and wealth reached their utmost extent, and his preservation of these and enjoyment of sacrificial offerings were complete. Through this filial devotion, he regulated the celestial governing powers, collected the jade credentials, harmonized pitch standards, revised ritual, established provinces, and consulted the regional governors. All these were achievements, yet his virtue was the greater. King Wu encountered an extraordinary rupture in the relationship between ruler and minister and acted in accord with Heaven and in response to the people. He excelled in continuing his predecessors’ purposes and undertakings, and his retrospective bestowal of royal titles reached far back. Through this filial devotion, he released prisoners, honored worthy men at their neighborhood gates, restored extinguished lines, revived discontinued institutions, attracted those far away, and extended affection to his kin. All these were acts of virtue, yet his achievements predominated. Shao Yaofu said: “Yao abdicated in favor of Shun on account of virtue. King Wu stood one degree below Shun and thus belonged to the realm of achievement.” Thus, “great” refers to virtue, and “universally recognized” refers to achievement. Each expression describes what their filial devotion attained: how could these be two different things? More than a thousand years after Shun, King Wu arose. After King Wu, however, the cosmic cycle of completion and renewal failed to come together, and the realm had long remained divided.
We reverently consider how Our Emperor has answered the five-hundred-year cycle and presided over the destiny of a unified realm, succeeding to the great imperial inheritance and gloriously holding the jade token of heavenly authority. He has followed Taizu’s injunction that, upon an elder brother’s death, the younger brother should succeed, and carried forward Emperor Chun’s plan to bring repose to his sons and provide for his grandsons. This is what is meant by “the sage arises, and all beings behold him,” and “Heaven grants it to him, and the people turn to him.” At the beginning of his accession, his first edict commanded the court ministers to deliberate on undertaking…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
尊親大典夫何昧禮者據人後之疑泥古者持
漢宋之謬仰惟
皇上濬哲天縱愛敬性成
英悟睿斷引聖經以折羣疑
離明乾剛觀會通而行典禮乃崇
尊號而名實以稱爰立
世廟而追饗以伸一本之義萬世之經粲然
著矣於是揭始末之故而要其是詳異同
之言而歸於一下之史局編摩成書
===
綸音凡三頒而更名曰
明倫大典焉首列帝王之統則正變以别次
詳
祖宗之系則正閏以分析統嗣之義而人後之
疑始决申世及之文而大人之禮攸定漢
宋本其預養則濮議自廢曹叡發其援立
則魏詔斯悖古先聖賢之訓所當尊則上
稽孔孟之敎旁采歐陽之議衆言殽而折
諸聖也末世弊陋之說所當斥則遠破師
punctuated:
尊親大典。夫何昧禮者據人後之疑，泥古者持漢宋之謬？仰惟皇上濬哲天縱，愛敬性成，英悟睿斷，引聖經以折羣疑；離明乾剛，觀會通而行典禮。乃崇尊號而名實以稱，爰立世廟而追饗以伸。一本之義、萬世之經，粲然著矣。於是揭始末之故而要其是，詳異同之言而歸於一，下之史局，編摩成書。綸音凡三頒，而更名曰《明倫大典》焉。
首列帝王之統，則正變以别；次詳祖宗之系，則正閏以分。析統嗣之義，而人後之疑始决；申世及之文，而大人之禮攸定。漢宋本其預養，則濮議自廢；曹叡發其援立，則魏詔斯悖。古先聖賢之訓所當尊，則上稽孔孟之敎，旁采歐陽之議，衆言殽而折諸聖也。末世弊陋之說所當斥，則遠破師
translation_en:
…the great rites for honoring his parents. Yet why did those ignorant of ritual base their objections on doubts about becoming another man's heir, while those bound to antiquity upheld the errors of the Han and Song? We reverently consider that His Majesty possesses profound wisdom bestowed by Heaven, with love and reverence inherent in his nature. Brilliant in understanding and sagacious in judgment, he invoked the canonical writings of the sages to resolve the many doubts. With the brightness of the trigram Li and the firmness of Qian, he discerned how principles converge and apply to changing circumstances, and carried out the prescribed rites. He accordingly exalted the honorific title, bringing name and reality into accord, and established the Temple of the Imperial Father (Shimiao), thereby giving full expression to retrospective sacrificial worship. The principle that one has a single source of descent, the enduring norm for ten thousand generations, thus became manifest in all its brilliance. Thereupon, the circumstances from beginning to end were set forth to establish what was right; agreeing and dissenting statements were examined in detail and brought to a single conclusion. The material was sent down to the Historiography Office to be compiled into a book. Imperial pronouncements were issued three times in all, and the work was renamed the Great Compendium on Clarifying Human Relationships (Minglun dadian).
First, it sets out the succession of emperors and kings, distinguishing regular succession from exceptional cases. Next, it details the genealogy of the imperial ancestors, distinguishing legitimate from irregular lines. By analyzing the distinction between succeeding to the imperial line and succeeding as a filial heir, it finally resolves doubts about becoming another man's heir; by expounding the texts concerning succession from father to son and from elder brother to younger brother, it establishes the rites due to one's parents. The Han and Song cases rested on prior adoptive upbringing, so the arguments concerning the Prince of Pu fall away of themselves. Cao Rui's case reveals his invocation of enthronement by others' support [?], thereby exposing the error of the Wei edict. As for the teachings of the ancient sages and worthies that ought to be honored, the work consults the teachings of Confucius and Mencius and also draws upon Ouyang's arguments: amid the confusion of competing statements, it takes the sages as its arbiters. As for the defective and narrow doctrines of latter ages that ought to be rejected, it refutes, among the more distant examples, the arguments of Shi…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
丹之論近折司馬光之疏異論息而大義
明矣
崇諡獨斷純得乎天理之正
世饗專舉深即乎人心之安伏讀
聖諭曰各官所奏一一直書以明是非以見邪
正又曰先儒所論幷魏詔漢宋之事其於禮
合則褒進之使後人有所守謬而否則斥之
亦使後人無所惑大哉
皇言蓋是非直書褒貶自見其春秋之義乎
===
御製序曰王天下者皆本奉天命承宗祀立人
極建綱常作民之主未有舍是而外求諸道
以能化行四海澤被生民者也又曰上承乎
天奉宗祀於億萬斯年下勤乎民務盡君人
師長之道期於禮樂之興刑罰是中大哉
皇言蓋肇於親睦及於協和其尚書之旨乎稽
之孝經則本一行而兼三才之道質諸中
庸則操三重而兼六事之善至哉
聖人之孝乎一孝立而萬善從之矣是故以之
punctuated:
丹之論，近折司馬光之疏，異論息而大義明矣。崇諡獨斷，純得乎天理之正；世饗專舉，深即乎人心之安。伏讀聖諭曰：「各官所奏，一一直書，以明是非，以見邪正。」又曰：「先儒所論，幷魏詔、漢宋之事，其於禮合，則褒進之，使後人有所守；謬而否，則斥之，亦使後人無所惑。」大哉皇言！蓋是非直書，褒貶自見，其《春秋》之義乎！

御製序曰：「王天下者，皆本奉天命、承宗祀、立人極、建綱常、作民之主，未有舍是而外求諸道，以能化行四海、澤被生民者也。」又曰：「上承乎天，奉宗祀於億萬斯年；下勤乎民，務盡君人師長之道，期於禮樂之興，刑罰是中。」大哉皇言！蓋肇於親睦，及於協和，其《尚書》之旨乎！稽之《孝經》，則本一行而兼三才之道；質諸《中庸》，則操三重而兼六事之善。至哉聖人之孝乎！一孝立而萬善從之矣。是故以之
translation_en:
…the arguments of Shi Dan, and, nearer our own time, refutes the memorial of Sima Guang. Dissenting arguments are silenced, and the great principle is made clear. The sovereign’s sole decision to confer an exalted posthumous title accords wholly with the rectitude of Heaven’s principle; his particular provision for perpetual sacrificial honors accords profoundly with what brings peace to human hearts. I reverently read the sacred instruction: “Record plainly, one by one, what each official submitted, to clarify right and wrong and reveal perversity and rectitude.” It further says: “As for the discussions of earlier Confucian scholars, together with the Wei edict and the affairs of the Han and Song dynasties, wherever they accord with ritual, commend and promote them, so that later generations have something to uphold. Wherever they are mistaken and do not accord with it, reject them, so that later generations likewise remain free of confusion.” How great are these imperial words! By recording right and wrong plainly, praise and blame become apparent of themselves. Is this not the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals?

The imperially composed preface says: “Those who rule all under Heaven invariably take as their foundation reverent obedience to Heaven’s Mandate, the continuation of ancestral sacrifices, the establishment of the highest human standard and the cardinal bonds and constant virtues, and service as the people’s sovereign. Never has anyone abandoned these and sought the Way elsewhere, yet succeeded in extending moral transformation throughout the Four Seas and bestowing blessings upon the people.” It further says: “Above, obey Heaven and maintain the ancestral sacrifices for countless millions of years; below, labor diligently for the people, striving to fulfill the Way of acting as their ruler, teacher, and leader, with the aim that rites and music flourish and punishments attain due measure.” How great are these imperial words! Beginning with affection and concord among kin and extending to universal harmony—is this not the purport of the Book of Documents? Examined against the Classic of Filial Piety, this takes one form of conduct as its foundation while encompassing the Way of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity. Tested against the Doctrine of the Mean, it embraces the three weighty responsibilities and encompasses the excellence of the six duties. How consummate is the sage’s filial piety! Once filial piety is established, all virtues follow from it. Thus, through it…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
而明天經則
圜丘有祀
祈穀有祀
欽天有頌焉以之而正地義則
方澤有祀
嶽瀆有祀
籍田有典焉以之而植民行則辟雍之
幸養老之
詔
===
釐先師之儀黜夷族之享
蠲租憫疫賑饑勸農之
令行焉孝心融徹和氣充塞於兩儀之間禮
制通行濊澤漸被於八埏之外是故天不
愛道地不愛寶禎符疊應景貺洊至甘露
屢降嘉禾茂產芝草充
廷醴泉湧地黄河
薦瑞白鹿協靈可致之祥無不畢集
成功巍乎莫及
punctuated: 而明天經，則圜丘有祀，祈穀有祀，欽天有頌焉；以之而正地義，則方澤有祀，嶽瀆有祀，籍田有典焉；以之而植民行，則辟雍之幸、養老之詔、釐先師之儀、黜夷族之享、蠲租憫疫賑饑勸農之令行焉。孝心融徹，和氣充塞於兩儀之間；禮制通行，濊澤漸被於八埏之外。是故天不愛道，地不愛寶，禎符疊應，景貺洊至。甘露屢降，嘉禾茂產，芝草充廷，醴泉湧地，黄河薦瑞，白鹿協靈，可致之祥，無不畢集。成功巍乎莫及，
translation_en: …and thereby make manifest Heaven’s constant order, there are sacrifices at the Circular Mound, sacrifices for a fruitful grain harvest, and hymns revering Heaven. Through filial piety, the proper order of Earth is established: there are sacrifices at the Square Marsh altar, sacrifices to the sacred peaks and waterways, and ceremonies of plowing the imperial field. Through it, proper conduct is fostered among the people: the imperial visit to the Biyong, the edict on caring for the aged, the revision of rites for the First Teacher, the exclusion of barbarian clans from sacrificial honors [?], and orders remitting taxes, showing compassion to victims of epidemics, relieving famine, and encouraging agriculture—all are put into effect. The filial heart permeates everything, and harmonious vital energy fills the space between Heaven and Earth. Ritual institutions prevail everywhere, and abundant beneficence gradually extends beyond the eight extremities of the world. Thus Heaven does not withhold its Way, nor Earth its treasures; auspicious signs respond one after another, and glorious blessings arrive repeatedly. Sweet dew frequently descends; auspicious grain grows luxuriantly; numinous mushrooms fill the court; sweet springs gush from the earth. The Yellow River presents auspicious signs, and white deer attest to numinous harmony. Every auspicious portent that could be summoned gathers here. These towering accomplishments are beyond all comparison…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
至德蕩乎難名何莫非孝之所至哉故明倫理
於羣迷雖非帝舜之遇而其大則同焉極
尊養以天下雖非武王之遇而其達則同焉先
聖後聖不一揆耶雖然此自明問言及之
而言爾乃愚生睹日而測天飲澗而遡海
將不可揄揚於萬一乎夫恭己無爲而聲
色之俱泯我伐用張而盡美之未遑則雖
舜武之功德相掩矣端南面之治非述也
紹南巢之舉非作也則雖舜武之述作不
===
兼矣惟我
皇上帝德廣運
聖神文武兼體而無遺功盛矣而備舜之德
王道顯行禮樂刑政四達而不悖德盛矣而
總武之功故曰貫帝王而會其全本衷綏
猷先
天地開闢之仁視虞之作而愈光緣法建治後
天地制作之義軼周之述而爲烈故曰合明聖
而臻其盛猗歟休哉然豈無其本乎粵自
punctuated:
至德蕩乎難名，何莫非孝之所至哉？故明倫理於羣迷，雖非帝舜之遇，而其大則同焉；極尊養以天下，雖非武王之遇，而其達則同焉。先聖後聖，不一揆耶？

雖然，此自明問言及之而言爾。乃愚生睹日而測天，飲澗而遡海，將不可揄揚於萬一乎？夫恭己無爲而聲色之俱泯，我伐用張而盡美之未遑，則雖舜武之功德相掩矣；端南面之治，非述也；紹南巢之舉，非作也。則雖舜武之述作不兼矣。

惟我皇上，帝德廣運，聖神文武兼體而無遺，功盛矣而備舜之德；王道顯行，禮樂刑政四達而不悖，德盛矣而總武之功。故曰：貫帝王而會其全。本衷綏猷，先天地開闢之仁，視虞之作而愈光；緣法建治，後天地制作之義，軼周之述而爲烈。故曰：合明聖而臻其盛。猗歟休哉！然豈無其本乎？粵自
translation_en:
…His supreme virtue is so vast that it defies naming. What among these things is not brought about by filial piety? Thus, in making human relationships clear to the bewildered multitude, although his circumstances differ from those of Emperor Shun, his greatness is the same. In bringing honor and nurture to their utmost through possession of all under Heaven, although his circumstances differ from those of King Wu, the reach of his filial devotion is the same. Do not earlier and later sages follow a single standard?

Yet these remarks merely address what your illuminating question has raised. Might I, an ignorant student, by observing the sun and gauging Heaven, by drinking from a mountain stream and tracing it back to the sea, offer praise equal to even one ten-thousandth of his greatness? Shun held himself reverently and governed without action, dispensing altogether with stern words and expressions; King Wu proclaimed, “Our campaign is now set forth,” yet had no leisure to attain perfection in beauty. Thus, even with Shun and Wu, achievement and virtue overshadowed one another. Shun’s establishing government while facing south was not a transmission of earlier deeds; Wu’s following the precedent of the undertaking at Nanchao—the banishment of Jie—was not an original creation. Thus, even Shun and Wu did not each unite transmission and creation.

Our Emperor alone extends his imperial virtue far and wide, embodying sageliness, spiritual insight, civil refinement, and martial prowess, with nothing omitted. His achievements are flourishing, yet he also possesses Shun’s virtue in full. The kingly Way is manifestly practiced; rites, music, punishments, and government reach everywhere without discord. His virtue is flourishing, yet he also encompasses Wu’s achievements. Hence we say: he unites the traditions of the emperors and kings and brings together their full excellence. Rooting himself in inner sincerity and bringing repose through his plans [?], he gives precedence to the benevolence by which Heaven and Earth opened forth; compared with the creations of Shun of Yu, his work shines still more brightly. Following established models to institute government, he follows the righteousness by which Heaven and Earth fashion and order things; his accomplishments surpass the transmission undertaken by Wu of Zhou. Hence we say: he joins illumination and sageliness and brings them to their fullest flourishing. Ah, how splendid! Yet could this be without a foundation? From the time when…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
精一授受開萬世心學之原敬義敷陳綿
八百王業之久二聖人之孝統於是矣我
皇上敬一之學蓋異世而共貫焉一者純乎理
而不雜即精一之旨而敬者存其心而無
忽即敬義之訓也然舜之紹堯得之乎見
知武之繼文無異於師資我
皇上則心領神會獨悟乎化育之妙
建極錫民自得於見聞之表直與二帝三王
默契於數千載之外三十登庸乃承帝堯
===
之咨旣陟太耄始聞丹書之誡我
皇上則生知夙成匪藉啓翼之力
閎謨駿烈不假閲歷之功直與
二祖
列聖潛孚於二百載之上是故本源澄徹採之
無際元機充滿施之不匱功德崇隆並羣
聖而有赫述作昌明冠百王而大備至哉
聖人之孝乎雍熙太和之治將與
天地爲悠久而生斯世者沐浴
punctuated: 精一授受，開萬世心學之原；敬義敷陳，綿八百王業之久。二聖人之孝統於是矣。我皇上敬一之學，蓋異世而共貫焉。一者，純乎理而不雜，即精一之旨；而敬者，存其心而無忽，即敬義之訓也。然舜之紹堯，得之乎見知；武之繼文，無異於師資。我皇上則心領神會，獨悟乎化育之妙，建極錫民，自得於見聞之表，直與二帝三王默契於數千載之外。三十登庸，乃承帝堯之咨；旣陟太耄，始聞丹書之誡。我皇上則生知夙成，匪藉啓翼之力；閎謨駿烈，不假閲歷之功，直與二祖列聖潛孚於二百載之上。是故本源澄徹，採之無際；元機充滿，施之不匱。功德崇隆，並羣聖而有赫；述作昌明，冠百王而大備。至哉，聖人之孝乎！雍熙太和之治，將與天地爲悠久，而生斯世者沐浴
translation_en:
