…the transmission of refinement and single-mindedness opened the source of the learning of the mind for all ages; the exposition of reverent attentiveness and righteousness prolonged the royal enterprise for eight hundred years. In these lay the unifying principle of the two sages’ filial piety. Our Emperor’s learning of reverent single-mindedness follows the same thread as theirs, though in a different age. Single-mindedness means being pure in principle, without admixture: this is precisely the purport of refinement and single-mindedness. Reverent attentiveness means preserving the mind without negligence: this is precisely the teaching of reverent attentiveness and righteousness.

Yet Shun, in succeeding Yao, acquired his understanding through seeing and knowing him; King Wu, in succeeding King Wen, stood in a relationship no different from that of pupil and teacher. Our Emperor, however, grasps these things in his heart and comprehends them in his spirit, independently awakening to the mysteries of transformation and nurture. He establishes the supreme standard and bestows it upon the people, attaining understanding for himself beyond what is seen and heard. He thus accords silently with the Two Emperors and Three Kings across several thousand years. Only when called to service at thirty did Shun receive Emperor Yao’s counsel; only after reaching advanced old age did King Wu hear the admonitions of the Cinnabar Writing. Our Emperor, however, was born with understanding and attained perfection early, without relying on others’ guidance and assistance. His grand plans and magnificent achievements do not depend on knowledge gained through long experience. He thus accords inwardly with the Two Founding Ancestors and the successive sage emperors across more than two hundred years.

Therefore his fountainhead is clear and limpid, and what may be drawn from it is boundless; the primal workings are abundant within him, and their application is inexhaustible. His achievements and virtue are lofty, shining alongside those of all the sages. His continuation of inherited institutions and creation of new ones are flourishing and enlightened, surpassing those of the hundred kings in their completeness. How consummate is the sage’s filial piety! His harmonious, prosperous rule of supreme concord will endure as long as Heaven and Earth, while those born into this age bathe in…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
膏澤涵泳
聖化相忘於
道德之中而不知矣愚也雖欲操觚翰以形容
竭心力而賛述殆若聽簫韶而知舜之難
名歌下武而識武之莫及也何能揄揚於
萬一哉謹對
第二問
尹來師
同考試官教諭何〔崇貴〕批經以言明亦以言晦子能
===
剖析諸儒而根極要領能自得師錄之
同考試官學正劉〔鶴翔〕批辨析明盡以之致用必有
實効不可以經生目子也
考試官教諭鄭〔延年〕批折衷詳確
考試官教諭魏〔體謙〕批評品得宜
存六經難矣未若明之之難也明六經難
矣未若行之之難也夫經以載道道不明
則所存者器數之末爾道以經世用不適
則所明者章句之義爾如是而聖人作經
punctuated:
膏澤，涵泳聖化，相忘於道德之中而不知矣。愚也雖欲操觚翰以形容，竭心力而賛述，殆若聽簫韶而知舜之難名，歌下武而識武之莫及也。何能揄揚於萬一哉？謹對。
第二問
尹來師
同考試官教諭何〔崇貴〕批：「經以言明，亦以言晦。子能剖析諸儒而根極要領，能自得師，錄之。」
同考試官學正劉〔鶴翔〕批：「辨析明盡，以之致用，必有實効，不可以經生目子也。」
考試官教諭鄭〔延年〕批：「折衷詳確。」
考試官教諭魏〔體謙〕批：「評品得宜。」
存六經難矣，未若明之之難也；明六經難矣，未若行之之難也。夫經以載道，道不明，則所存者器數之末爾；道以經世，用不適，則所明者章句之義爾。如是而聖人作經
translation_en:
…the bounty of imperial grace, immersed in the sage emperor’s transforming influence, forgetting themselves amid the Way and its virtue without even knowing it. Foolish though I am, even if I wished to take up writing tablet and brush to describe this, exhausting my mind and strength in praise, it would be like hearing the Shao music and realizing how difficult Shun is to describe, or singing “Following in the Footsteps of the Martial King” (Xia Wu) and recognizing that King Wu cannot be equaled. How could I extol even one ten-thousandth of it? Respectfully submitted in reply.
Second Question
Yin Laishi
Associate Examiner He Chonggui, Instructor, comments: “Words illuminate the Classics, but words also obscure them. You can analyze the various Confucian scholars and probe the essentials to their roots. You can find a teacher for yourself [?]. I select this essay.”
Associate Examiner Liu Hexiang, School Director, comments: “Your distinctions and analyses are clear and exhaustive. Applied to practical affairs, they will assuredly produce real results. You cannot be regarded as merely a student of the Classics.”
Examiner Zheng Yannian, Instructor, comments: “Your weighing of differing views is detailed and precise.”
Examiner Wei Tiqian, Instructor, comments: “Your assessments and rankings are appropriate.”
Preserving the Six Classics is difficult, but not as difficult as understanding them; understanding the Six Classics is difficult, but not as difficult as putting them into practice. The Classics convey the Way. If the Way is not understood, what is preserved amounts merely to the minutiae of ritual objects and numerical prescriptions. The Way serves to order the world. If its application is unsuitable, what is understood amounts merely to the meaning of textual sections and sentences. If this is so, then the sages’ intention in composing the Classics…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
之意不其息哉執事以經學策諸生愚豈
其人顧窮居所習謂何而可虛明問乎蓋
自秦兼天下燔詩書捐業士六學從此缺
矣而漢興孝惠除挾書之條武帝行藏書
之策明帝下購書之詔章帝舉白虎之儀
於是文學之士雝雝然言易者田何以授
丁寛由田王孫至於高相可勝紀也而最
著者曰田何之易焦贛之易費直之易然
或離爲十二篇或專指災異或雜入彖象
===
不免捃摭而皆稱易之學言書者伏生口
授張生與鼂錯由歐陽生至於歐陽高可
勝紀也而最著者曰歐陽之書大夏侯之
書小夏侯之書或辯析乎簡編或取信於
字跡或湊泊於女子所獻不免執泥而皆
稱書之學詩則申公爲魯詩轅固爲齊詩
韓嬰爲韓詩三家竝立厥後毛萇之詩盛
興而三家廢矣蓋其書穿先秦如釋鴟鴞
與金縢合釋北山與孟子合烏得而不傳
punctuated: 之意不其息哉？執事以經學策諸生，愚豈其人？顧窮居所習謂何，而可虛明問乎？蓋自秦兼天下，燔詩書，捐業士，六學從此缺矣。而漢興，孝惠除挾書之條，武帝行藏書之策，明帝下購書之詔，章帝舉白虎之儀。於是文學之士雝雝然。言易者，田何以授丁寛，由田王孫至於高相，可勝紀也？而最著者，曰田何之易、焦贛之易、費直之易。然或離爲十二篇，或專指災異，或雜入彖象，不免捃摭，而皆稱易之學。言書者，伏生口授張生與鼂錯，由歐陽生至於歐陽高，可勝紀也？而最著者，曰歐陽之書、大夏侯之書、小夏侯之書。或辯析乎簡編，或取信於字跡，或湊泊於女子所獻，不免執泥，而皆稱書之學。詩則申公爲魯詩，轅固爲齊詩，韓嬰爲韓詩，三家竝立。厥後毛萇之詩盛興，而三家廢矣。蓋其書穿先秦，如釋鴟鴞與金縢合，釋北山與孟子合，烏得而不傳？
translation_en:
…would not the sages’ purpose in composing the Classics thereby come to an end? You, honored examiners, have posed a policy question on classical learning to the candidates. Am I, in my ignorance, fit to answer it? Yet what would my studies in humble retirement amount to if I left your discerning question unanswered?

When Qin unified All-under-Heaven, it burned the Odes and Documents and cast aside learned scholars; from then onward, the six branches of classical learning were impaired. With the rise of Han, however, Emperor Xiaohui abolished the statute against possessing books; Emperor Wu implemented a policy of collecting books; Emperor Ming issued an edict to purchase books; and Emperor Zhang convened the deliberations at the White Tiger Hall. Scholars of textual learning consequently gathered in harmony.

Among those who expounded the Changes, Tian He transmitted his learning to Ding Kuan. From Tian Wangsun down to Gao Xiang, could they all be enumerated? The most prominent traditions were the Changes of Tian He, of Jiao Gan, and of Fei Zhi. Yet some divided the text into twelve sections, some focused exclusively on calamities and anomalies, and some interspersed the Judgments and Images commentaries. They could not avoid piecing together collected materials, yet all were called studies of the Changes.

Among those who expounded the Documents, Master Fu orally instructed Master Zhang and Chao Cuo. From Master Ouyang down to Ouyang Gao, could they all be enumerated? The most prominent traditions were the Documents of Ouyang, of the Elder Xiahou, and of the Younger Xiahou. Some made minute distinctions in the written texts, some relied on the written characters as evidence, and some cobbled together what a woman had presented. They could not avoid rigid attachment to particulars, yet all were called studies of the Documents.

As for the Odes, Master Shen established the Lu tradition, Yuan Gu the Qi tradition, and Han Ying the Han tradition; the three schools stood side by side. Later, Mao Chang’s tradition of the Odes flourished, and the three schools fell into disuse. His text apparently reached back into pre-Qin times [?]: for example, its explanation of “The Owl” accords with “The Metal-bound Coffer,” and its explanation of “Northern Mountain” accords with the Mencius. How could it fail to be transmitted?

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
春秋則有公羊氏穀梁氏鄒氏夾氏四家
並立厥後左氏之書始出而鄒夾廢矣蓋
其親見孔子如湛露諸詩合於專對南蒯
之事有功名教烏得而不傳至於諸侯惡
害已而去籍策士附私見以紊聖樂已不
傳而禮制散佚久矣大小二戴共氏而分
門王鄭兩家同經而異註於是高堂生極
力探討而學庸樂記賴之以不墜當其時
傅師之所授受非經不談朝廷之所揚搉
===
惟古是程賈捐之請勿擊朱厓王育則曰
經義何以據龔勝之奏王嘉公孫祿則曰
君議一無所援自周末以還玆其盛矣綴
簡册於煨燼尊聖訓如蓍龜蓋皆曰存經
也夫存之謂其明之也乃有以伯益之事
疑書月令之非疑禮卜筮之數疑易醜亂
之跡疑詩讀周禮未訖篇謂爲戰國之書
讀春秋未識十二巳議三傳之失如是而
曰存經可乎傳註及於三折補綴盡乎百
punctuated: 春秋則有公羊氏、穀梁氏、鄒氏、夾氏四家並立，厥後左氏之書始出，而鄒、夾廢矣。蓋其親見孔子，如湛露諸詩合於專對，南蒯之事有功名教，烏得而不傳？至於諸侯惡害已而去籍，策士附私見以紊聖，樂已不傳，而禮制散佚久矣。大小二戴共氏而分門，王、鄭兩家同經而異註，於是高堂生極力探討，而學、庸、樂記賴之以不墜。當其時，傅師之所授受，非經不談；朝廷之所揚搉，惟古是程。賈捐之請勿擊朱厓，王育則曰：「經義何以據？」龔勝之奏王嘉、公孫祿，則曰：「君議一無所援。」自周末以還，玆其盛矣。綴簡册於煨燼，尊聖訓如蓍龜，蓋皆曰存經也。夫存之，謂其明之也。乃有以伯益之事疑書，月令之非疑禮，卜筮之數疑易，醜亂之跡疑詩；讀周禮未訖篇，謂爲戰國之書；讀春秋未識十二，巳議三傳之失。如是而曰存經，可乎？傳註及於三折，補綴盡乎百
translation_en: As for the Spring and Autumn Annals, the four schools of Gongyang, Guliang, Zou, and Jia stood side by side. Later, when Zuo’s book appeared, the Zou and Jia schools fell into disuse. Since Zuo had personally seen Confucius, his treatment of such poems as “Heavy Dew” accorded with the practice of independently answering diplomatic inquiries, and his account of Nan Kuai served the moral teachings governing human relationships. How could his work fail to be transmitted? As for the feudal lords, they removed records because they feared these would harm themselves; political persuaders introduced private opinions that confused the sages’ teachings. The Classic of Music ceased to be transmitted, and the institutions of ritual had long been scattered and lost. The Elder and Younger Dai shared a surname but established separate schools; Wang and Zheng treated the same classic but supplied different commentaries. Thereupon Master Gaotang exerted himself in investigation, and the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, and the Record of Music depended on him for their preservation. At that time, in what teachers transmitted and received, they discussed nothing but the classics; in the court’s deliberations, antiquity alone supplied the standard. When Jia Juanzhi requested that Zhuya not be attacked, Wang Yu said, “On what meaning in the classics do you base this?” Of Gong Sheng’s memorial concerning Wang Jia and Gongsun Lu, it was said, “Your proposal cites no authority whatsoever.” Since the end of the Zhou, this was the flourishing age of classical learning. They pieced together bamboo slips and books from the ashes and revered the sages’ instructions like divinatory milfoil and tortoise shells. All this, they said, was preserving the classics. Yet preserving them means understanding them. Some, however, doubted the Book of Documents because of the affair of Bo Yi; doubted the Record of Rites because of errors in the “Monthly Ordinances”; doubted the Book of Changes because of its calculations for tortoise-shell and milfoil divination; and doubted the Book of Odes because of its accounts of depravity and disorder. Before finishing a section of the Rites of Zhou, they declared it a book of the Warring States period; before understanding even a tenth or two of the Spring and Autumn Annals, they were already discussing the faults of its Three Commentaries. Can conduct like this be called preserving the classics? The commentaries and annotations went through three successive turns [?], and the patching extended to a hundred …

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
孔蓋皆曰明經也夫明之謂其行之也乃
魏相明易屢上災異之疏匡衡明詩不聞
無邪之義明書若歐陽歙而身以賄累明
禮若戴聖而子有盜行雖以仲舒之賢著
春秋決獄二百餘條而其徒呂步舒等因
之窮驗深刻如是而曰明經可乎蓋非有
明道覺世之心各尊祖習互相詆訾枝葉
日繁根本隱矣非有任道輔世之心徒積
虛名獵都貴顯青紫旣得弁髦委矣夫旣
===
有師之責則當時信之至於流行而不廢
自其不廢之說足以惑後世之心曰明經
之說不廢夫既有世之責則當時尊之至
於推行而不効自其不効之學足以阻後
世之心曰明經之學不効此王通所以致
譏而鄭樵為之興嘆乎是故六經之文已
晦而不終晦者漢諸儒之功而六經之道
可明而不大明者則漢諸儒之責不可辭
矣迄於有宋周茂叔倡不傳之學二程引
punctuated:
孔，蓋皆曰明經也。夫明之，謂其行之也。乃魏相明易，屢上災異之疏；匡衡明詩，不聞無邪之義；明書若歐陽歙，而身以賄累；明禮若戴聖，而子有盜行。雖以仲舒之賢，著春秋決獄二百餘條，而其徒呂步舒等因之窮驗深刻。如是而曰明經，可乎？蓋非有明道覺世之心，各尊祖習，互相詆訾，枝葉日繁，根本隱矣；非有任道輔世之心，徒積虛名，獵都貴顯，青紫旣得，弁髦委矣。夫旣有師之責，則當時信之，至於流行而不廢，自其不廢之說，足以惑後世之心，曰明經之說不廢。夫既有世之責，則當時尊之，至於推行而不効，自其不効之學，足以阻後世之心，曰明經之學不効。此王通所以致譏，而鄭樵為之興嘆乎？是故六經之文已晦，而不終晦者，漢諸儒之功；而六經之道可明，而不大明者，則漢諸儒之責不可辭矣。
迄於有宋，周茂叔倡不傳之學，二程引
translation_en:
…holes—all this, they claimed, was elucidating the Classics. Yet to elucidate them means to put them into practice. Wei Xiang understood the Book of Changes, but repeatedly submitted memorials concerning calamities and anomalies. Kuang Heng understood the Book of Odes, but showed no awareness of the meaning of “no wayward thoughts.” Ouyang Xi understood the Book of Documents, yet was himself implicated in bribery; Dai Sheng understood the rites, yet his son committed theft. Even the worthy Dong Zhongshu compiled more than two hundred rulings in Deciding Judicial Cases through the Spring and Autumn Annals, but his followers, Lü Bushu and others, used them to pursue exhaustive investigations with harsh severity. Can conduct like this be called elucidating the Classics?
They lacked the resolve to clarify the Way and awaken the world. Each revered the teachings he had inherited, and they disparaged one another: branches and leaves multiplied daily, while the roots became obscured. They lacked the resolve to shoulder responsibility for the Way and aid the world. They merely amassed empty reputations and hunted for high office and distinction [?]. Once they obtained the blue and purple insignia of rank, they cast the Classics aside like a discarded ceremonial cap and childhood hair.
Since they bore the responsibilities of teachers, their contemporaries trusted them. Their teachings consequently circulated without falling into disuse; precisely through their continued currency, these doctrines were sufficient to mislead later generations into saying, “The doctrines that elucidate the Classics endure.” Since they bore responsibilities in the world [?], their contemporaries esteemed them. Yet when their learning was put into practice, it proved ineffective; precisely through its ineffectiveness, it was sufficient to discourage later generations into saying, “Learning that elucidates the Classics is ineffective.” Was this why Wang Tong voiced criticism and Zheng Qiao heaved a sigh?
Thus, although the texts of the Six Classics had become obscure, they did not remain obscure forever: this was the achievement of the Han scholars. But the Way of the Six Classics, though capable of being made clear, was never fully clarified: for this the Han scholars cannot evade responsibility.
When the Song dynasty arrived, Zhou Maoshu championed the learning whose transmission had been broken, and the two Cheng brothers carried forward…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
其緒楊中立載道南之宗朱仲晦集其成
朱程之傳出而易明矣蔡沉之註行而書
明矣詩研於集傳禮定於集解春秋折衷
乎程胡於是漢儒之穿鑿諸家之分裂始
振刷矣蓋至是而後可言存經焉濂溪明
冕帶於司理伊川揭正道以說書龜山壽
靖康之脉安國扶紹興之業南軒濟淳熈
之治文公堅誠正之對雖其遭逢不偶未
究厥用而小試輒効矣蓋至是而後可言
===
明經焉彼其時雖不免拘數觀易新義僭
古蘇陳驚辭子韶耽寂紛然出矣朱子蓋
嘗患之然譬諸揚爝火於日中奏俚曲於
雅庭抑何損哉合而言之漢人監秦之失
者也過焉則亦漢之失也宋人懲漢之弊
者也過焉則亦宋之弊也何以言之荀子
曰欲觀先王之迹則於其粲然者矣自秦
焚籍壁簡僅存周官之制度已不可見漢
儒慨慕紆鬱不得已而稽之於稗小採之
punctuated:
其緒，楊中立載道南之宗，朱仲晦集其成。朱程之傳出而《易》明矣，蔡沉之註行而《書》明矣。《詩》研於《集傳》，《禮》定於《集解》，《春秋》折衷乎程胡，於是漢儒之穿鑿、諸家之分裂始振刷矣。蓋至是而後可言存經焉。濂溪明冕帶於司理，伊川揭正道以說書，龜山壽靖康之脉，安國扶紹興之業，南軒濟淳熈之治，文公堅誠正之對。雖其遭逢不偶，未究厥用，而小試輒効矣。蓋至是而後可言明經焉。
彼其時，雖不免拘數觀《易》，《新義》僭古，蘇陳驚辭，子韶耽寂，紛然出矣，朱子蓋嘗患之。然譬諸揚爝火於日中，奏俚曲於雅庭，抑何損哉？合而言之，漢人監秦之失者也，過焉則亦漢之失也；宋人懲漢之弊者也，過焉則亦宋之弊也。何以言之？荀子曰：「欲觀先王之迹，則於其粲然者矣。」自秦焚籍，壁簡僅存，周官之制度已不可見。漢儒慨慕紆鬱，不得已而稽之於稗小，採之
translation_en:
…their intellectual thread; Yang Zhongli carried the lineage of the Way southward, and Zhu Zhonghui brought it to completion. With the appearance of Zhu’s and Cheng’s commentaries, the Book of Changes became clear; with the circulation of Cai Chen’s annotations, the Book of Documents became clear. The Book of Odes was investigated in the Collected Commentaries, and the Book of Rites was settled in the Collected Explanations; the Spring and Autumn Annals was interpreted by weighing the views of Cheng and Hu. Thus the strained interpretations of Han scholars and the fragmentation among the various schools at last began to be swept away. Only at this point, indeed, could one speak of preserving the Classics. Lianxi illuminated the ceremonial cap and girdle [?] while serving as a prefectural judge; Yichuan set forth the correct Way as an Expositor-in-waiting; Guishan prolonged the lifeblood of the Jingkang reign; Anguo supported the enterprise of the Shaoxing reign; Nanxuan aided the government of the Chunxi reign; and Master Wen firmly upheld sincerity of intention and rectification of the mind in his replies to the throne. Although their circumstances were unfavorable and they never fully realized their abilities in office, even their limited opportunities invariably produced results. Only at this point, indeed, could one speak of elucidating the Classics.
In their time, admittedly, there arose in profusion those who interpreted the Book of Changes through a restrictive numerology, those whose New Interpretations usurped the authority of antiquity, the startling language of Su and Chen, and Zishao’s absorption in quietude. Master Zhu was indeed once troubled by these things. Yet they were like raising a torch at midday or playing rustic tunes in a court of refined music: what harm could they do? Taken together, the men of Han learned from Qin’s failures; but when they went too far, this became Han’s own failing. The men of Song sought to remedy Han’s defects; but when they went too far, this became Song’s own defect. How can this be explained? Xunzi said: “If you wish to observe the traces of the former kings, look to those that are clearly manifest.” After Qin burned the books, only the bamboo slips hidden in walls survived, and the institutional arrangements of the Offices of Zhou could no longer be seen. Han scholars yearned for them with anguished frustration. Having no alternative, they sought evidence in minor writings and gathered it from …

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
於故老歲積月累心力勤矣庸詎知其考
索之過詳尋章摘句支分節解而經之㫖
裂矣遂至徼纒文義豐蔀性靈烏得而不
流於訓詁宋則反是周子揭無欲之要程
子昭定性之說微辭奧㫖粹然一出於正
乃不善學者捐棄往昔著意精微喜徑約
則曰六經註我便脫畧則曰何書可讀自
謂懲漢之弊而不知其弊之流于斯也故
曰鹵莽之患甚於黨伐高闊之病深於訓
===
詁拘攣之見慘於煨燼蓋指漢宋人云雖
然漢人之學持引繩墨然而近著已矣擇
地而蹈行不踰閑所少者通方之見爾故
多節義之士而自高尚宋人之弊侈辯析
迂談闊眂不鏡事機乃其末季多議論而
少成功夫論儒先之造詣則宋得其精漢
則粗矣論世代之習尚則漢得其實宋則
虛矣嗚呼玆世教所由係歟故必經世者
而後可明經必反經者而後可正經不知
punctuated:
於故老，歲積月累，心力勤矣。庸詎知其考索之過詳，尋章摘句，支分節解，而經之㫖裂矣！遂至徼纒文義，豐蔀性靈，烏得而不流於訓詁？宋則反是。周子揭無欲之要，程子昭定性之說，微辭奧㫖，粹然一出於正。乃不善學者，捐棄往昔，著意精微，喜徑約則曰「六經註我」，便脫畧則曰「何書可讀」。自謂懲漢之弊，而不知其弊之流于斯也。故曰：「鹵莽之患甚於黨伐，高闊之病深於訓詁，拘攣之見慘於煨燼。」蓋指漢宋人云。

雖然，漢人之學，持引繩墨，然而近著已矣。擇地而蹈，行不踰閑，所少者通方之見爾。故多節義之士而自高尚。宋人之弊，侈辯析，迂談闊眂，不鏡事機，乃其末季多議論而少成功。夫論儒先之造詣，則宋得其精，漢則粗矣；論世代之習尚，則漢得其實，宋則虛矣。嗚呼！玆世教所由係歟？故必經世者而後可明經，必反經者而後可正經。不知
translation_en:
…from elderly men. Year upon year and month upon month, they labored diligently in mind and strength. Yet how could they have known that their investigations were excessively minute—that by searching out passages and plucking out phrases, dividing limbs and dissecting joints, they fragmented the meaning of the Classics? Eventually they became entangled in textual meanings [?] and thickly obscured their innate spiritual understanding. How could they avoid lapsing into mere philological exegesis? The Song scholars took the opposite course. Master Zhou set forth the essential principle of freedom from desire, and Master Cheng elucidated the teaching of stabilizing one’s nature. Their subtle words and profound meanings issued entirely from what was correct. Yet those who learned poorly abandoned the past and concentrated on abstruse subtleties. Delighting in shortcuts, they declared, “The Six Classics annotate me”; finding careless omission convenient, they asked, “What books are worth reading?” They claimed to be correcting the failings of Han scholarship, unaware that their own failings had reached this point. Thus it is said: “The harm of careless crudity exceeds that of partisan attacks; the sickness of lofty abstraction runs deeper than philological exegesis; constricted understanding does more damage than burning books to ashes.” This presumably refers to the scholars of the Han and Song.

Nevertheless, Han scholarship adhered to guiding lines and standards, though it remained confined to what was close at hand and manifest [?]. Its scholars chose where to tread, and their conduct did not overstep proper bounds. What they lacked was only a comprehensive understanding. Thus there were many men of integrity and righteousness who held themselves to lofty ideals. The failings of Song scholars lay in excessive disputation and analysis, impractical talk and sweeping views, and failure to discern the circumstances of affairs. Consequently, in the dynasty’s final years there was much discussion but little accomplishment. If we consider the attainments of earlier Confucian masters, the Song grasped the essence, while the Han remained at the level of the crude. If we consider the prevailing habits of their respective ages, however, the Han attained substance, while the Song embraced emptiness. Alas! Is this not what the moral teaching of an age depends upon? Thus only those who can put the world in order can elucidate the Classics; only those who return to the Classics can rectify their interpretation. I wonder…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
執事以為何如
第三問
陳所蘊
同考試官學正段〔文綺〕批師古救今之說鑿鑿可行
經濟之學也
考試官教諭鄭〔延年〕批籌畫詳盡
考試官教諭魏〔體謙〕批抱濟時之畧者取之
執事舉積貯之法下詢乎承學顧愚生何
足以辨此雖然蓋嘗誦王制矣曰國無九
===
年之蓄曰不足無六年之蓄曰急無三年
之蓄曰國非其國也三年耕必有一年之
食九年耕必有三年之食以三十年之通
雖有凶旱水溢民無菜色而又有遺人掌
縣都之委積以待凶荒有廩人掌九穀之
數以治年之凶豐以令邦移民就穀有鄉
師以歲時賙民有司救以王命施惠載在
周官不一而足是故春頒秋斂國富公蓄
比櫛崇墉民多私積懷襄之災九年而民
punctuated:
執事以為何如？

第三問
陳所蘊

同考試官學正段〔文綺〕批：師古救今之說，鑿鑿可行，經濟之學也。
考試官教諭鄭〔延年〕批：籌畫詳盡。
考試官教諭魏〔體謙〕批：抱濟時之畧者，取之。

執事舉積貯之法，下詢乎承學，顧愚生何足以辨此？雖然，蓋嘗誦《王制》矣，曰：「國無九年之蓄曰不足，無六年之蓄曰急，無三年之蓄曰國非其國也。三年耕，必有一年之食；九年耕，必有三年之食。以三十年之通，雖有凶旱水溢，民無菜色。」而又有遺人掌縣都之委積，以待凶荒；有廩人掌九穀之數，以治年之凶豐，以令邦移民就穀；有鄉師以歲時賙民；有司救以王命施惠。載在《周官》，不一而足。是故春頒秋斂，國富公蓄；比櫛崇墉，民多私積。懷襄之災九年，而民
translation_en:
…what does Your Honor think?

Third Policy Question
Chen Suoyun

Comment by Associate Examiner Duan Wenqi, School Director: “His proposals for emulating antiquity to remedy present difficulties are definite and practicable. This is learning directed toward governing the realm and aiding its people.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng Yannian, Instructor: “His planning is thorough and detailed.”
Comment by Examiner Wei Tiqian, Instructor: “He possesses strategies for meeting the needs of the age. Select him.”

Your Honor has raised the methods of accumulating reserves and deigned to question us students about them. How could an ignorant student such as I be competent to explain this? Nevertheless, I have read the ‘Royal Regulations’ (Wang zhi), which says: ‘A state without reserves sufficient for nine years is said to be inadequately supplied; without reserves for six years, it is said to be in straits; without reserves for three years, it is said to be no longer a state. Three years of cultivation must yield food sufficient for one year in reserve; nine years of cultivation must yield food sufficient for three years in reserve. Balancing resources over thirty years, even if severe droughts and overflowing waters occur, the people will show no signs of hunger.’

There were also Officers of Reserves (yiren), who managed the stores of the districts and domains against famine; Granary Officers (linren), who managed the quantities of the nine grains to provide for years of scarcity and abundance and instructed the states to move people to where grain was available; District Preceptors (xiangshi), who provided relief to the people according to the seasons; and Relief Officers (sijiu), who distributed aid at the king’s command. The provisions recorded in the Offices of Zhou (Zhou guan) are too numerous to enumerate.

Thus, with distributions in spring and collections in autumn, the state had abundant public reserves. With grain piled like comb teeth and high walls, the people had ample private stores. The overwhelming floods lasted nine years, yet the people…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
自嬉食桑林之旱七年而民自允殖是則
經常之制也上也自井田之法廢而兼幷
之害興道德之化微而管晏之術熾先王
之制蕩然矣而因時創法足濟當時則有
平糴之法熟則斂之於官饑則散之於民
而大小異宜行之於魏者李悝也常平之
法穀賤則增價以糴穀貴則減價以糶而
民農兼利行之於漢者耿壽昌也社倉之
制自民而出自民而入以置於社行之於
===
隋者長孫平也義倉之法斂散有權貧富
相濟行之於唐者戴冑也是則權宜之法
也次也由是而下宋之亮臣孰與范仲淹
耶而其在兩浙祗假營造而賙活又孰與
富弼耶其在青州不過饘粥以療饑豈其
知有不給所遭之時異也蓋預備之法行
於豐年則易而講於年饑之後則難行於
無事則易而舉於有兵之日則難故軍旅
饑饉必子路之才勇而後足賈誼之告文
punctuated:
自嬉食；桑林之旱七年，而民自允殖。是則經常之制也，上也。

自井田之法廢，而兼幷之害興，道德之化微，而管晏之術熾，先王之制蕩然矣。而因時創法，足濟當時，則有平糴之法：熟則斂之於官，饑則散之於民，而大小異宜，行之於魏者李悝也。常平之法：穀賤則增價以糴，穀貴則減價以糶，而民農兼利，行之於漢者耿壽昌也。社倉之制：自民而出，自民而入，以置於社，行之於隋者長孫平也。義倉之法：斂散有權，貧富相濟，行之於唐者戴冑也。是則權宜之法也，次也。

由是而下，宋之亮臣孰與范仲淹耶？而其在兩浙，祗假營造而賙活。又孰與富弼耶？其在青州，不過饘粥以療饑。豈其知有不給？所遭之時異也。蓋預備之法，行於豐年則易，而講於年饑之後則難；行於無事則易，而舉於有兵之日則難。故軍旅饑饉，必子路之才勇而後足。賈誼之告文
translation_en:
…the people still ate contentedly; during the seven-year drought associated with Sanglin, the people still continued to thrive. These were enduring institutions, the highest order of provision.

Once the well-field system was abolished, the evils of land engrossment arose; as moral transformation through virtue waned, the techniques of Guan Zhong and Yan Ying flourished. The institutions of the former kings disappeared entirely. Yet measures devised to suit the times could adequately meet contemporary needs. There was the system of equitable grain purchasing: in abundant harvests, grain was collected by the government; in famine, it was distributed to the people, with measures adjusted to the scale of the harvest. Li Kui implemented this in Wei. Under the ever-normal granary system, when grain was cheap, the purchase price was raised; when grain was dear, the selling price was lowered, benefiting both consumers and farmers. Geng Shouchang implemented this under the Han. Under the community granary system, contributions came from the people and receipts returned to the people, with grain stored within the community. Zhangsun Ping implemented this under the Sui. Under the charitable granary system, collection and distribution were managed flexibly, and rich and poor supported one another. Dai Zhou implemented this under the Tang. These were expedient measures, ranking second.

Coming down to later times, which worthy minister of the Song could compare with Fan Zhongyan? Yet in Liangzhe, he relied only on construction projects to provide relief and sustain lives. And who could compare with Fu Bi? In Qingzhou, he did no more than relieve hunger with gruel. Was their understanding somehow inadequate? The circumstances they encountered were different. Measures for advance provision are easy to implement in abundant years, but difficult to devise once famine has begun; easy to implement in peaceful times, but difficult to introduce when warfare is underway. Thus, facing warfare and famine requires the ability and courage of Zilu to meet the task. Jia Yi’s admonition to Emperor Wen…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
帝縣有急兵方數千里旱民方狼顧而文
帝且憂之夫宋正坐此於是乎爲無策然
亦可以監矣夫考之先王驗之後世何嘗
有一定之法哉時之異則異焉勢之異則
異焉地之異則異焉委任權力之異則異
焉夫舉井田之制於今日則有司議之矣
何也時也青苗行於鄞則足而推之天下
則否何也勢也趙抃知越州增米價而民
不病文彥博之在成都減之亦不病何也
===
地也朱仲晦之賢豈但十倍長孫平請于
孝宗行社倉而竟不效何也委任權力之
異也是故法不足恃而酌本末之宜達損
益之權可恃也執事知河南之民乎敝也
極矣地瘠而賦重益以轉徙之多則無常
業矣塲工甫畢輒貿易焉以苟旦夕之便
則蓋藏鮮矣起土播種仰聽於天時一不
登則棄之矣而籍猶存鬻產者利乎直之
多而不割則虛額懸矣吏人胥人皂輿之
punctuated:
帝，縣有急兵，方數千里旱，民方狼顧，而文帝且憂之。夫宋正坐此，於是乎爲無策，然亦可以監矣。夫考之先王，驗之後世，何嘗有一定之法哉？時之異則異焉，勢之異則異焉，地之異則異焉，委任權力之異則異焉。夫舉井田之制於今日，則有司議之矣。何也？時也。青苗行於鄞則足，而推之天下則否。何也？勢也。趙抃知越州，增米價而民不病；文彥博之在成都，減之亦不病。何也？地也。朱仲晦之賢，豈但十倍長孫平？請于孝宗行社倉，而竟不效。何也？委任權力之異也。是故法不足恃，而酌本末之宜、達損益之權可恃也。
執事知河南之民乎？敝也極矣！地瘠而賦重，益以轉徙之多，則無常業矣。塲工甫畢，輒貿易焉，以苟旦夕之便，則蓋藏鮮矣。起土播種，仰聽於天，時一不登則棄之矣，而籍猶存；鬻產者利乎直之多而不割，則虛額懸矣。吏人、胥人、皂輿之
translation_en:
…Emperor Wen: a county faced an urgent military threat, drought extended over several thousand li, and the people looked about in alarm; even Emperor Wen was troubled by this. The Song suffered precisely from this predicament and consequently had no remedy. Yet this, too, can serve as a warning. Examining the practices of the former kings and testing them against later ages, when has there ever been a single fixed method? Methods must differ as the times differ, as circumstances differ, as places differ, and as the authority conferred on those entrusted with their implementation differs. Were someone to propose the well-field system today, the responsible officials would take issue with it. Why? Because of the times. The Green Sprouts scheme was adequate when implemented in Yin, but not when extended throughout the empire. Why? Because of the circumstances. When Zhao Bian was prefect of Yuezhou, he raised rice prices without harming the people; when Wen Yanbo was in Chengdu, he lowered them, likewise without harming the people. Why? Because of the locality. Was Zhu Zhonghui’s worth merely ten times that of Zhangsun Ping? He petitioned Emperor Xiaozong to institute community granaries, yet ultimately the proposal proved ineffective. Why? Because of differences in the authority conferred on those entrusted with implementation. Thus, fixed methods cannot be relied upon; what can be relied upon is judging what is appropriate in both fundamentals and particulars, and understanding how to adjust measures by weighing what should be reduced or increased.
Do you, sir, know the condition of the people of Henan? Their impoverishment has reached an extreme! The land is barren and taxes are heavy; with frequent migration added to these burdens, they have no stable livelihoods. As soon as threshing is finished, they sell their produce to scrape by from day to day, leaving little in reserve. They till the soil and sow, relying entirely on Heaven. Whenever a harvest fails, they abandon the land, yet it remains on the tax registers. Those who sell their property seek a higher price and do not transfer its tax liability, leaving outstanding assessments with no corresponding holdings. Clerks, petty functionaries, livery servants, and sedan-chair bearers …

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
人鱗鱗在庭舉待哺乎官則游食多矣戴
白無褐脫粟不充乃富子美服鮮食有山
坻之積則盛兼并之徒俗尚侈矣天下之
中五方具焉土著之羨歲運而之他則利
去矣此六者民之所由以瘠也然而非其
大也
天潢之派其麗不億皆食土之力以相滋挹顧
壤地有限而祿制無紀民力將竭矣夫民
也者固
===
藩封之所恃以安者也南之征北之戍裹糗
于邁輸輓邊鎮歲且百萬持符使者項背
在道孰非朘民之脂血哉夫棘一體之誼
固也目睫先疾遑遐矚耶夫五者耗財之
源其在民十之七八二者決財之流非民
致之也然猶冀萬一於歲焉則庶乎可也
邇者伊洛之溢田廬蕩析濁河潰決瀰漫
千里南陽之墟汝墳之間積數十州縣不
登老弱溝壑壯者四方獷悍之徒揮刃在
punctuated:
人鱗鱗在庭，舉待哺乎官，則游食多矣。戴白無褐，脫粟不充；乃富子美服鮮食，有山坻之積，則盛兼并之徒，俗尚侈矣。天下之中，五方具焉，土著之羨，歲運而之他，則利去矣。此六者，民之所由以瘠也。然而非其大也。
天潢之派，其麗不億，皆食土之力以相滋挹。顧壤地有限，而祿制無紀，民力將竭矣。夫民也者，固藩封之所恃以安者也。南之征，北之戍，裹糗于邁，輸輓邊鎮，歲且百萬；持符使者，項背在道，孰非朘民之脂血哉？夫棘一體之誼，固也；目睫先疾，遑遐矚耶？夫五者，耗財之源，其在民十之七八；二者，決財之流，非民致之也。然猶冀萬一於歲焉，則庶乎可也。
邇者伊洛之溢，田廬蕩析；濁河潰決，瀰漫千里。南陽之墟，汝墳之間，積數十州縣不登。老弱溝壑，壯者四方，獷悍之徒揮刃在
translation_en:
…personnel crowd the courtyards, all looking to the government for their sustenance: thus there are many who eat without producing. The white-haired lack even coarse clothing and cannot get their fill of roughly husked grain, while the sons of the wealthy wear fine clothes, eat choice foods, and possess stores piled like hills. Thus those who engross others’ property flourish, and extravagance becomes the prevailing custom. Here at the center of the realm, people from all five regions gather; the surplus of the settled inhabitants is transported elsewhere each year, and the profits depart. These six things are what impoverish the people. Yet they are not the greatest burdens.
The branches of the imperial lineage are beyond counting, and all live upon the produce of the land to sustain themselves. Yet the land is finite, while the system of stipends knows no bounds: the people’s resources are about to be exhausted. It is precisely upon the people that the princely fiefs depend for their security. For campaigns in the south and garrison duty in the north, men pack dry provisions and set out; transport to the frontier garrisons costs nearly a million each year. Envoys bearing credentials follow one another along the roads. Which of these does not drain the people’s lifeblood? The obligation of belonging to one body is certainly binding [?]; but when one’s eyes and lashes are already afflicted, how can one find leisure to gaze into the distance? Those five things [the text earlier says six] are sources of financial depletion, seven or eight tenths of which lie among the people themselves; these two things open the floodgates through which wealth drains away, and are not caused by the people. Even so, if there were still some slight hope of a good harvest, matters might perhaps remain manageable.
Recently the Yi and Luo rivers overflowed, sweeping away fields and homes; the turbid Yellow River burst its banks, inundating a thousand li. Around Nanyang and along the banks of the Ru, several dozen subprefectures and counties have suffered crop failures. The old and weak perish in ditches and gullies; the able-bodied scatter in every direction. Violent, lawless men brandish blades in…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
道白晝大都之中剽吏而奪之金環視莫
敢誰何者有之矣而不講積貯之法可乎
執事之言及之也將起民之骨而肉之瘠
而潤之使腴也已幸甚傳曰君者代天理
物者也臣者行君之令而致之民者也今
外服之臣則藩臬與守令爾藩臬去民遠
雖有承宣之責不得不下諸守令蓋守令
則朝發而夕可達矣是故舉積貯則當責
守令行積貯之法在使民自生而上生之
===
使民自生其說莫如荀卿曰田野縣鄙者
財之本也垣窌倉廩者財之末也百姓時
和事業得叙者貨之源也等賦府庫者貨
之流也上生之其說莫如曾鞏曰病而後
圖之與夫先事而爲計者則有間矣不習
而有爲與夫素得之者則有間矣斯二說
皆行法之意也而法不與焉夫
宗藩徵發非守令所得爲也不曰於斯二者
之外乎賦之重則河南郡矣災之重則南
punctuated:
道，白晝大都之中，剽吏而奪之金，環視莫敢誰何者，有之矣。而不講積貯之法，可乎？執事之言及之也，將起民之骨而肉之，瘠而潤之使腴也已，幸甚！傳曰：「君者，代天理物者也；臣者，行君之令而致之民者也。」今外服之臣，則藩臬與守令爾。藩臬去民遠，雖有承宣之責，不得不下諸守令。蓋守令則朝發而夕可達矣。是故舉積貯，則當責守令。行積貯之法，在使民自生而上生之。
使民自生，其說莫如荀卿曰：「田野縣鄙者，財之本也；垣窌倉廩者，財之末也；百姓時和，事業得叙者，貨之源也；等賦府庫者，貨之流也。」上生之，其說莫如曾鞏曰：「病而後圖之，與夫先事而爲計者，則有間矣；不習而有爲，與夫素得之者，則有間矣。」斯二說，皆行法之意也，而法不與焉。夫宗藩、徵發，非守令所得爲也，不曰於斯二者之外乎？賦之重，則河南郡矣；災之重，則南
translation_en:
…on the roads. There have even been cases of men robbing officials and taking their money in broad daylight in great cities, while all who looked on dared not challenge them. Can we then fail to consider methods of building reserves? Your raising this subject will put flesh back on the people's bones and nourish the emaciated until they are well fed. What a great blessing! A transmitted text says: “The ruler orders all things on Heaven's behalf; ministers carry out the ruler's commands and convey them to the people.” Now, officials serving outside the capital are the provincial administration and surveillance commissioners, prefects, and county magistrates. The provincial commissioners are distant from the people. Though charged with receiving and promulgating imperial commands, they must pass these down to the prefects and magistrates. With prefects and magistrates, an order issued in the morning can reach the people by evening. Thus, responsibility for building reserves should be assigned to them. To implement methods of building reserves requires enabling the people to sustain themselves and having those above sustain them.
On enabling the people to sustain themselves, no explanation surpasses that of Xun Qing: “Fields and outlying rural districts are the root of wealth; walled storehouses, underground storage pits, and granaries are its branches. When the common people live in harmony with the seasons and their occupations are properly ordered, this is the source of goods; graded tax assessments and treasuries are their downstream flow.” On those above sustaining the people, no explanation surpasses that of Zeng Gong: “There is a difference between devising measures only after distress has arisen and making plans beforehand. There is a difference between undertaking something without practice and having long mastered it.” These two explanations express the intent behind implementing methods, but do not include the methods themselves. Now, expenditure on the imperial princes and requisitions are beyond the control of prefects and magistrates. Are we not speaking of matters apart from these two? As for the severity of taxation, Henan Prefecture stands foremost; as for the severity of disaster, it is Nan…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
陽矣請於監司多撥閭布輕則以示恤可
乎民之少蓋藏也俗之侈也兼幷者導之
也有司躬羔羊之節則闤市歌蟋蟀矣矧
僭擬條所具可按而理也地不失畔糧不
失額則丈量庶幾矣使分布得人復譏察
之民將安所奸哉樹藝無法農之惰不勸
也詢水之源委爲利而教以播耨之時淺
深之方勞之董之民自勸於農矣五方之
赴啖吾利也俗旣儉則逐末寡矣省約騶
===
===
從旣仰食者少而民免乎魚肉此在有司
猶振落爾此六者有取於荀卿之說也皆
所以使民自生也夫民旣知自生而儲蓄
之法可行宜於平糴宜於常平則以李悝
耿壽昌之意行之宜於社倉宜於義倉則
以長孫平戴胄之意行之不得已而處兩
浙之難則出以文正之意不得已而有青
州之役則出以鄭公之意譬之於醫察其
標本之因審其虛實之宜然後從而劑砭
punctuated:
陽矣。請於監司，多撥閭布，輕則以示恤，可乎？民之少蓋藏也，俗之侈也，兼幷者導之也。有司躬羔羊之節，則闤市歌蟋蟀矣。矧僭擬條所具，可按而理也。地不失畔，糧不失額，則丈量庶幾矣。使分布得人，復譏察之，民將安所奸哉？樹藝無法，農之惰不勸也。詢水之源委爲利，而教以播耨之時、淺深之方，勞之董之，民自勸於農矣。五方之赴啖吾利也，俗旣儉，則逐末寡矣。省約騶從，旣仰食者少，而民免乎魚肉，此在有司猶振落爾。此六者，有取於荀卿之說也，皆所以使民自生也。
夫民旣知自生，而儲蓄之法可行。宜於平糴，宜於常平，則以李悝、耿壽昌之意行之；宜於社倉，宜於義倉，則以長孫平、戴胄之意行之。不得已而處兩浙之難，則出以文正之意；不得已而有青州之役，則出以鄭公之意。譬之於醫，察其標本之因，審其虛實之宜，然後從而劑砭
translation_en:
…Nanyang. Might one petition the surveillance officials to allocate more funds from household levies and lighten the assessments, thereby showing compassion [?]? The people have few reserves because their customs are extravagant, and those who engross wealth and property lead them in this direction. If the responsible officials personally embody the integrity celebrated in “The Lamb’s Fur,” then even the marketplaces will sing “The Cricket.” Moreover, the provisions against arrogating the privileges of one’s superiors are fully set out and can be consulted and enforced. If no land escapes its recorded boundaries and no grain tax falls outside its assessed quota, land measurement will have largely achieved its purpose. If suitable men are assigned throughout the area and their work is further inspected, where will the people find room for fraud? Cultivation lacks proper methods because farmers are idle and receive no encouragement. Investigate the sources and courses of waterways to put them to beneficial use; teach the proper seasons for sowing and hoeing and the methods of working shallow or deep; encourage and supervise the people, and they will of themselves apply themselves to farming. As for those who come from all regions to feed upon our profits, once customs become frugal, fewer will pursue the secondary occupations of commerce. Reduce mounted attendants and retinues: with fewer people dependent upon such maintenance, the common people will escape being preyed upon. For the responsible officials, this would be as easy as shaking down falling leaves. These six measures draw upon the teachings of Xun Qing; all enable the people to provide for themselves.
Once the people know how to provide for themselves, methods of building reserves can be put into practice. Where equitable grain purchasing or ever-normal granaries are appropriate, implement them in the spirit of Li Kui and Geng Shouchang. Where community granaries or charitable granaries are appropriate, implement them in the spirit of Zhangsun Ping and Dai Zhou. If compelled to confront difficulties like those of Liangzhe, act in the spirit of Wenzheng; if compelled to undertake an effort like that at Qingzhou, act in the spirit of the Duke of Zheng. It is like practicing medicine: investigate the causes underlying both the symptoms and the root disorder, determine what is appropriate to conditions of deficiency or excess, and only then administer medicines and stone-needle treatment…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
之則循方可也損益之可也自爲方可也
要在不失乎倉扁之意此六者有取於曾
鞏之言也皆所以爲上生之也夫如是雖
有災沴吾不患矣或曰才力之强弱知識
之敏鈍弗可齊也而槩責諸守令可乎愚
嘗渡河洛矣三老在柁長年鼓枻睹其氣
嶽嶽然聞其聲登登然其心則矢其力共
戮已而濟矣何也共濟之心也嘗觀御於
大梁之墟矣其所御也非御者有也然暄
===
之則思覆之雨之則思蔽之疾徐高下酌
而行之惴惴惟恐失何也受直故也夫所
貴乎守令者非才智之難而不實心之爲
患苟實心矣則自有灼事之智任事之才
而良法出焉即弗齊達之有遲速耳而其
於人必濟愚願守令以舟楫視
國家之事而以御視其民則吾河南之民將
阜以生乎執事甚盛惠也
第四問
punctuated:
之，則循方可也，損益之可也，自爲方可也，要在不失乎倉扁之意。此六者有取於曾鞏之言也，皆所以爲上生之也。夫如是，雖有災沴，吾不患矣。或曰：「才力之强弱，知識之敏鈍，弗可齊也，而槩責諸守令，可乎？」愚嘗渡河洛矣，三老在柁，長年鼓枻，睹其氣嶽嶽然，聞其聲登登然，其心則矢，其力共戮，已而濟矣。何也？共濟之心也。嘗觀御於大梁之墟矣，其所御也，非御者有也。然暄之則思覆之，雨之則思蔽之，疾徐高下，酌而行之，惴惴惟恐失。何也？受直故也。夫所貴乎守令者，非才智之難，而不實心之爲患。苟實心矣，則自有灼事之智、任事之才，而良法出焉。即弗齊，達之有遲速耳，而其於人必濟。愚願守令以舟楫視國家之事，而以御視其民，則吾河南之民將阜以生乎！執事甚盛惠也。
第四問
translation_en:
…in treating it, one may follow an established prescription, modify it, or devise one’s own. What matters is not departing from the intent of Cang Gong and Bian Que. These six measures draw upon the words of Zeng Gong; all are ways for those above to sustain the people’s livelihood. If matters are handled thus, even when calamities strike, I shall have no concern.
Someone may ask: “People differ in the strength of their abilities and the keenness of their understanding. Is it right to demand the same of all prefects and magistrates?” I once crossed the Yellow and Luo Rivers. The boatmaster stood at the rudder, and the boatmen plied their oars. I saw their imposing bearing and heard their resounding calls. Their resolve was firm, and they exerted their strength together; before long, we had crossed. Why? Because they shared the determination to make the crossing.
I once watched a driver at the site of Daliang. What he drove did not belong to him. Yet when the sun grew hot, he thought to provide a covering; when it rained, he thought to provide shelter. Whether moving swiftly or slowly, uphill or downhill, he proceeded with deliberation, anxiously fearing any mishap. Why? Because he received wages.
What matters in prefects and magistrates is this: the difficulty is not obtaining talent and intelligence; the danger lies in a lack of sincere dedication. Given sincere dedication, they will naturally possess the intelligence to understand affairs and the ability to undertake them, and sound methods will emerge. Even if their abilities differ, this means only that some achieve results sooner and others later; they will assuredly bring relief to the people. I humbly wish that prefects and magistrates would regard the affairs of the state as a boatman regards his boat and oars, and regard their people as a driver regards his charge. Then surely the people of our Henan would prosper in their livelihoods! This would be a most generous benefaction on your part.
Fourth Question

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
王來潤
同考試官學正張介批敷答詳盡而深識遠見舉
切時宜似有經緯之蘊者取之
考試官教諭鄭延年批條答精詳
考試官教諭魏體謙批足占所養
將也者國之衞也識也者擇將之基也度
也者任將之地也公也者勵將之典也何
謂識立之而不問其方拔之而不惑于衆
是也何謂度誠信而不使之疑含弘而不
===
使之忌是也何謂公賞不至於遐遺罰不
至於潰逸是也夫人才之伏無盡而將之
才又非可以繩墨矩度言者是非有高世
之識曷能拔之於庸衆之中哉拔之矣必
假之以機宜使進止得以敷其猷任之矣
又必稽之於衆論使誅賞有以適其節則
恩施而莫不忘其生威震而莫不忘其死
蓋無不可用之將無不可成之功矣若夫
奮軀以建績先國家之急而忘其私此則
punctuated:
王來潤

同考試官學正張介批：敷答詳盡，而深識遠見，舉切時宜，似有經緯之蘊者，取之。
考試官教諭鄭延年批：條答精詳。
考試官教諭魏體謙批：足占所養。

將也者，國之衞也；識也者，擇將之基也；度也者，任將之地也；公也者，勵將之典也。何謂識？立之而不問其方，拔之而不惑于衆，是也。何謂度？誠信而不使之疑，含弘而不使之忌，是也。何謂公？賞不至於遐遺，罰不至於潰逸，是也。夫人才之伏無盡，而將之才又非可以繩墨矩度言者，是非有高世之識，曷能拔之於庸衆之中哉？拔之矣，必假之以機宜，使進止得以敷其猷；任之矣，又必稽之於衆論，使誅賞有以適其節。則恩施而莫不忘其生，威震而莫不忘其死，蓋無不可用之將，無不可成之功矣。若夫奮軀以建績，先國家之急而忘其私，此則
translation_en:
Wang Lairun

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang Jie, School Instructor: His exposition is thorough and exhaustive, displaying profound understanding and far-reaching insight. Every point addresses the needs of the time. He seems to possess the capacity to order affairs of state. Accept him.
Comment by Examiner Zheng Yannian, Instructor: His answers to the individual points are incisive and detailed.
Comment by Examiner Wei Tiqian, Instructor: This amply reveals his cultivation.

Generals are the defenders of the state. Discernment is the foundation for selecting generals; magnanimity is the basis for employing them; impartiality is the rule for encouraging them. What is meant by discernment? Appointing a man without asking where he comes from, and promoting him without being swayed by the multitude. What is meant by magnanimity? Being sincere and trustworthy so that he harbors no doubts, and being tolerant and broad-minded so that he feels no apprehension. What is meant by impartiality? Ensuring that rewards do not overlook those far away, and that punishments do not allow offenders to slip away.

The talents latent among men are inexhaustible, and a general’s abilities, moreover, cannot be assessed by fixed rules and measures. Without discernment surpassing that of one’s age, how could one raise such a man from among the ordinary multitude? Once he has been promoted, he must be granted discretion to act as circumstances require, so that, whether advancing or halting, he can carry out his plans. Once he has been entrusted with command, his conduct must also be examined against the judgments of others, so that punishments and rewards are properly proportioned. Then, when favor is bestowed, none will cling to life; when authority strikes awe, none will heed death. There will thus be no general who cannot be put to use, and no achievement that cannot be accomplished. As for exerting oneself to win distinction, putting the urgent needs of the state first and forgetting one’s private interests, this is …

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
為將者之所當自懷又奚俟上之敺之哉
嘗稽孫武子曰將者人之司命國家安危
之主也太史公曰且欲興聖統惟在擇任
將相司馬法曰輔周則國强輔隙則國弱
蓋甚言將之當擇耳夫悉國家之力兵甲
之衆寄之於一夫之手决機於兩陣之間
國之安危衆之存殁胥於此焉繫欲無慎
得乎故三代盛王雖隆仁義禮樂以化天
下之俗而常求天下之奇才以待不測之
===
患以銷伏其悖戾好爭之心而其法則寓
於六遂之間蓋戡定禍亂之謨即孝友睦
姻者之所習卒乗車徒之制皆公卿大夫
之素所講求也是其寵綏抜擢儲之於閒
暇之時授鉞臨戎任之於有事之日法備
而旨微卓乎不可尚矣自時厥後古制不
存戰伐日尋而將帥之名始紛紛於天下
然簡擇之審亦有可言者焉自其君之抜
擢者言之樂毅假節自魏迹何疎也而燕
punctuated: 為將者之所當自懷，又奚俟上之敺之哉？嘗稽孫武子曰：「將者，人之司命，國家安危之主也。」太史公曰：「且欲興聖統，惟在擇任將相。」司馬法曰：「輔周則國强，輔隙則國弱。」蓋甚言將之當擇耳。夫悉國家之力、兵甲之衆，寄之於一夫之手，决機於兩陣之間，國之安危、衆之存殁，胥於此焉繫，欲無慎得乎？故三代盛王，雖隆仁義禮樂以化天下之俗，而常求天下之奇才，以待不測之患，以銷伏其悖戾好爭之心。而其法則寓於六遂之間，蓋戡定禍亂之謨，即孝友睦姻者之所習；卒乗車徒之制，皆公卿大夫之素所講求也。是其寵綏抜擢，儲之於閒暇之時；授鉞臨戎，任之於有事之日。法備而旨微，卓乎不可尚矣！自時厥後，古制不存，戰伐日尋，而將帥之名始紛紛於天下。然簡擇之審，亦有可言者焉。自其君之抜擢者言之，樂毅假節自魏，迹何疎也，而燕
translation_en:
…is what a commander ought to cherish of his own accord. Why should he wait for his sovereign to urge him on?

I have examined Master Sun Wu’s statement: “The commander controls the lives of the people and determines the security or peril of the state.” The Grand Astrologer said: “If one wishes to revive the sagely succession, everything depends on selecting and appointing generals and chief ministers.” The Methods of the Minister of War (Sima fa) states: “When assistance is comprehensive, the state is strong; when assistance has gaps, the state is weak.” These sayings emphatically stress the need to choose commanders carefully. When the entire strength of the state and its mass of armed troops are entrusted to a single man, and the decisive moment comes between two opposing armies, the security or peril of the state and the survival or death of the multitude all hinge upon this. Can one possibly dispense with caution?

Thus, although the flourishing kings of the Three Dynasties exalted benevolence, righteousness, rites, and music to transform the customs of the realm, they constantly sought exceptional talent throughout the world to prepare for unforeseen calamities and to quell the people’s rebellious and contentious impulses. Their methods were embodied in the institutions of the six rural districts. Plans for suppressing disorder were precisely what those practicing filial devotion, brotherly affection, and harmony with their kin and relatives by marriage studied. The organization of soldiers, chariots, and infantry was what the dukes, ministers, and grand masters habitually investigated. They therefore favored, fostered, and promoted such men, keeping them in reserve during times of peace; when troubles arose, they bestowed the battle-axe of command and entrusted them with facing the enemy. Their methods were comprehensive and their intent subtle—so outstanding that nothing could surpass them!

Thereafter, the ancient institutions ceased to endure, warfare followed warfare daily, and men bearing the titles of general and commander began to proliferate throughout the realm. Nevertheless, there are still instances worth recounting of care in their selection. To speak of those promoted by their rulers: Yue Yi came from Wei bearing an envoy’s credential; how tenuous his ties were! Yet Yan…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
昭與圖國政卒成破齊之功韓信返自追
亡名未著也漢高以為大將遂奏滅楚之
績李靖出自囚繫身何辱也太宗與謀大
計竟開唐室之基是非識之精者能然乎
自其臣之薦進者言之晉侯擇尉中軍祁
奚以子午對君子與其能趙簡子擇守上
黨而狐解以伯栁稱當世稱其美符堅入
冦江左危矣謝安舉兄子玄拒之淝水之
捷符氏傾焉是非心之公者能然乎又嘗
===
稽古之為將者矣李牧備邊軍功爵賞皆
决於外李廣為將人人自便幕府省文書
李漢超守關南屬州錢悉以資軍猶規免
商筭夫迹之以行師之道則三子為否臧
律之以治吏之規則三子為干紀然當時
以閫外寄之也悉無所問焉故牧竟大破
諸胡廣能使匈奴不犯而漢超則漢遼聾
服不敢窺焉是三子皆能建非常之烈酬
不制之知而三君乃皆錄其功而不計其
punctuated:
昭與圖國政，卒成破齊之功。韓信返自追亡，名未著也，漢高以為大將，遂奏滅楚之績。李靖出自囚繫，身何辱也，太宗與謀大計，竟開唐室之基。是非識之精者能然乎？自其臣之薦進者言之，晉侯擇尉中軍，祁奚以子午對，君子與其能；趙簡子擇守上黨，而狐解以伯栁稱，當世稱其美；符堅入冦，江左危矣，謝安舉兄子玄拒之，淝水之捷，符氏傾焉。是非心之公者能然乎？
又嘗稽古之為將者矣。李牧備邊，軍功爵賞皆决於外；李廣為將，人人自便，幕府省文書；李漢超守關南，屬州錢悉以資軍，猶規免商筭。夫迹之以行師之道，則三子為否臧；律之以治吏之規，則三子為干紀。然當時以閫外寄之也，悉無所問焉。故牧竟大破諸胡，廣能使匈奴不犯，而漢超則漢遼聾服，不敢窺焉。是三子皆能建非常之烈，酬不制之知，而三君乃皆錄其功而不計其
translation_en:
…King Zhao consulted him on affairs of state, and ultimately achieved the defeat of Qi. Han Xin returned after being pursued as a deserter, his reputation still unestablished; Emperor Gao of Han appointed him general-in-chief, and he subsequently accomplished the destruction of Chu. Li Jing emerged from imprisonment—how abased his circumstances were! Yet Emperor Taizong consulted him on great plans, and he ultimately helped lay the foundations of the Tang ruling house. Could anyone without penetrating discernment have acted thus? As for recommendations made by ministers: when the lord of Jin sought a commandant for the central army, Qi Xi proposed his own son Wu, and gentlemen commended his ability. When Zhao Jianzi sought a governor for Shangdang, Hu Jie recommended Bo Liu, and his contemporaries praised his virtue. When Fu Jian invaded, the lands south of the Yangzi were in peril; Xie An recommended his elder brother’s son Xuan to resist him, and the victory at the Fei River brought down the Fu house. Could anyone without an impartial heart have acted thus?
I have also examined the generals of antiquity. When Li Mu defended the frontier, he decided in the field all grants of rank and rewards for military merit. When Li Guang commanded, everyone enjoyed freedom of action, and his headquarters reduced its paperwork. When Li Hanchao defended Guannan, all revenues from the subordinate prefectures went to support his army, and he also sought exemption from commercial taxes. Judged by the principles of conducting military operations, these three were subject to censure or praise [?]; measured against the rules for administering officials, all three violated established regulations. Yet, because they had been entrusted with command beyond the capital, their rulers questioned none of these matters. Thus Li Mu ultimately inflicted a crushing defeat on the various Hu peoples; Li Guang kept the Xiongnu from invading; and under Li Hanchao, Han and Liao submitted in fear [?], not daring to cast covetous eyes on his territory. All three were therefore able to accomplish extraordinary feats and repay the discerning trust that left them unfettered. Their three rulers, in turn, all recorded their achievements without reckoning their…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
過誠所謂將將之道宜然也洪惟我
皇上神武布昭
玄威遐暢往以小醜匪茹赫然討罪敷求將帥
拔擢側微有出自幽囚而建節有起自休廢
而秉麾者撻伐用張海宇寧謐視格苗薄
伐之師已超軼之漢宋諸君無復論矣而
執事尤欲求必勝之將何哉毋亦天下雖
安必當擇將意耶自昔擇將之道求之也
貴廣任之也貴專賞罰之也貴審以速而
===
已矣夫倜儻非常之士豈可以一端求哉
推舉必於世官則自奮之途沮矣任用必
於條格則逸駕之俊遺矣綺紈世胄充位
握符孰若廣簡技能遴選奇傑之為得耶
跅弛不羈者多負俗之累細廉曲謹者乏
濟世之規矧介胄之士取其能斬將搴旗
已矣能橫行朔漠已矣使詐使貪使智使
過期以集吾之事已矣何必追其旣往耶
故曰求之宜廣也將貴專謀兵在畏將軍
punctuated:
過，誠所謂將將之道宜然也。洪惟我皇上神武布昭，玄威遐暢。往以小醜匪茹，赫然討罪，敷求將帥，拔擢側微，有出自幽囚而建節，有起自休廢而秉麾者。撻伐用張，海宇寧謐，視格苗薄伐之師，已超軼之，漢宋諸君無復論矣。而執事尤欲求必勝之將，何哉？毋亦天下雖安，必當擇將意耶？自昔擇將之道，求之也貴廣，任之也貴專，賞罰之也貴審以速而已矣。
夫倜儻非常之士，豈可以一端求哉？推舉必於世官，則自奮之途沮矣；任用必於條格，則逸駕之俊遺矣。綺紈世胄，充位握符，孰若廣簡技能，遴選奇傑之為得耶？跅弛不羈者，多負俗之累；細廉曲謹者，乏濟世之規。矧介胄之士，取其能斬將搴旗已矣，能橫行朔漠已矣。使詐，使貪，使智，使過，期以集吾之事已矣，何必追其旣往耶？故曰求之宜廣也。將貴專謀，兵在畏將。軍
translation_en:
…their faults. This is indeed how the art of commanding commanders ought to be practiced. We reverently reflect that our Emperor’s divine martial prowess shines everywhere, and his august might extends afar. Formerly, when petty villains failed to reckon with their own strength, he rose in wrath to punish their offenses, sought commanders far and wide, and promoted men from obscure and humble circumstances. Some emerged from imprisonment to receive the commander’s staff; others were recalled from retirement or dismissal to wield the command banner. Punitive operations thus gained force, and all within the seas enjoyed peace. Compared with the campaigns that brought the Miao to submission and chastised the invaders, his achievements have already surpassed them; the rulers of Han and Song need not even be discussed. Yet you, honored examiners, still wish to seek commanders certain of victory. Why is this? Is it perhaps your view that, even when the realm is at peace, commanders must nevertheless be carefully selected? Since antiquity, the principles of selecting commanders have been simply these: seek them broadly, entrust them with undivided authority, and administer rewards and punishments with careful judgment and speed.
How could bold and extraordinary men be sought by a single criterion? If recommendations must come exclusively from families holding hereditary office, the path of those who advance through their own efforts will be obstructed. If appointments must conform strictly to established regulations, men of exceptional talent will be overlooked. How could filling posts and placing command tallies in the hands of silk-clad hereditary scions compare with searching widely for skill and ability and selecting outstanding men? Unrestrained and independent men often bear the burden of society’s censure; those scrupulous in petty matters and punctilious in minor observances lack plans for setting the world in order. All the more so with men in armor: it is enough to choose them for their ability to slay enemy commanders and seize their banners, enough that they can range unhindered across the northern deserts. Employ the deceitful, the greedy, the wise, and those who have committed faults, expecting only that they accomplish our undertaking. Why must their past be pursued? Thus I say that the search should be broad. What matters for a commander is independent planning; what matters for soldiers is that they stand in awe of their commander. Military…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
機牽制則失筭戎帥摧沮則不威古者選
將而任之授之以鉞俾專斷也分之以閫
俾樹威也其於委任之體豈不博大哉乃
或制於大吏而號令莫可施束於繁文而
勇畧莫可奮是雖韓白有作奚由自見哉
又或以指麾順旨爲良以奔走服勞爲敬
木强稍見疵類旋加矣夫委之以身先士
卒之寄而奪其服衆之威責之以肝腦塗
地之忠而復拘之以局促轅下之態不亦
===
難哉故曰任之宜專也三軍之衆百萬之
師以一將臨之而能使之帖然順靡然聽
者以賞罰之典在也故賞不踰時欲人速
得爲善之利也罰不旋踵欲人知討罪之
嚴也其或賞以遠遺則爲善者懼矣罰以
倖避則爲惡者興矣又或奏報之間淹延
時日推勘之久蔓引枝連慢令稽誅亦非
所以勵衆也故曰賞罰之宜審而速也雖
然擇將之道則然矣而將可無所自擇乎
punctuated:
機牽制則失筭，戎帥摧沮則不威。古者選將而任之，授之以鉞，俾專斷也；分之以閫，俾樹威也。其於委任之體，豈不博大哉？乃或制於大吏而號令莫可施，束於繁文而勇畧莫可奮，是雖韓白有作，奚由自見哉？又或以指麾順旨爲良，以奔走服勞爲敬，木强稍見，疵類旋加矣。夫委之以身先士卒之寄，而奪其服衆之威；責之以肝腦塗地之忠，而復拘之以局促轅下之態，不亦難哉？故曰任之宜專也。

三軍之衆，百萬之師，以一將臨之，而能使之帖然順、靡然聽者，以賞罰之典在也。故賞不踰時，欲人速得爲善之利也；罰不旋踵，欲人知討罪之嚴也。其或賞以遠遺，則爲善者懼矣；罰以倖避，則爲惡者興矣。又或奏報之間，淹延時日；推勘之久，蔓引枝連。慢令稽誅，亦非所以勵衆也。故曰賞罰之宜審而速也。

雖然，擇將之道則然矣，而將可無所自擇乎？
translation_en:
…When military operations are constrained, calculations go awry; when commanders are thwarted and discouraged, they lose their authority. In antiquity, generals were selected and entrusted with command. They were given the battle-axe so that they could decide independently, and assigned authority beyond the threshold so that they could establish their prestige. Was this not a broad and generous conception of entrusting command? Yet some are controlled by high officials, so that they cannot put their orders into effect, or bound by elaborate formalities, so that they cannot exercise their courage and strategic skill. Even if Han Xin and Bai Qi were to arise again, how could they show their abilities? Some, moreover, consider a commander good only when his directions conform to his superiors’ wishes, and respectful only when he runs about performing their errands. Let the slightest stubbornness appear, and accusations of faults immediately follow [?]. To entrust him with leading his officers and soldiers in person, yet strip him of the authority to command their obedience; to demand loyalty unto a death that leaves his brains and liver strewn upon the ground, yet confine him to the cramped posture of a subordinate beneath the command carriage—is this not asking too much? Thus I say that those entrusted with command should have undivided authority.

That a single general can command the hosts of the Three Armies, a force of a million men, and make them submit peaceably and obey without resistance is due to the established system of rewards and punishments. Rewards therefore must not be delayed, so that people may quickly obtain the benefits of doing good; punishments must follow without an instant’s delay, so that people may understand the severity with which offenses are punished. If rewards are omitted because their recipients are far away, those who do good will become apprehensive; if punishment is escaped through good fortune, evildoers will flourish. Sometimes, too, days are wasted while reports are submitted to the throne, and protracted investigations spread like vines, implicating one person after another. Lax enforcement of orders and delayed punishment are likewise no means of inspiring the troops. Thus I say that rewards and punishments should be carefully judged and swiftly administered.

Yet although these are the principles for choosing generals, can a general himself dispense with making his own choices?

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
本之以忠貞出之以果敢是非有見於外
利害無怵於中雖惡而無怒也雖喜而無
悅也予之而不驚也奪之而不怨也威之
而不屈也其自治如此故行通於神明而
可爲天下之將矣然非知道之君子其孰
能之哉方今
聖天子悠久成物壽考作人行將有若人者出
以副
側席之求矣草茅之見執事奚辱聽焉
===
第五問
王同文
同考試官教諭張〔邦臣〕批 待用之器理會自别執此
以往可收平倭之績矣
考試官教諭鄭〔延年〕批 深切時宜
考試官教諭魏〔體謙〕批 甚有識見
愚聞攘夷之道在治内而其要在責實何
也事變出於無窮而機宜伏於至微非有
昭曠之識則其端日陳於吾前且將忽焉
punctuated:
本之以忠貞，出之以果敢，是非有見於外，利害無怵於中。雖惡而無怒也，雖喜而無悅也，予之而不驚也，奪之而不怨也，威之而不屈也。其自治如此，故行通於神明，而可爲天下之將矣。然非知道之君子，其孰能之哉？方今聖天子悠久成物，壽考作人，行將有若人者出，以副側席之求矣。草茅之見，執事奚辱聽焉？

第五問
王同文
同考試官教諭張〔邦臣〕批：待用之器，理會自别。執此以往，可收平倭之績矣。
考試官教諭鄭〔延年〕批：深切時宜。
考試官教諭魏〔體謙〕批：甚有識見。

愚聞攘夷之道在治内，而其要在責實。何也？事變出於無窮，而機宜伏於至微，非有昭曠之識，則其端日陳於吾前，且將忽焉。
translation_en:
He must ground himself in loyalty and steadfastness and express these through resolve and courage, discerning right and wrong in external affairs while remaining inwardly unshaken by advantage or harm. Though he dislikes something, he does not become angry; though he likes something, he does not become delighted. When granted something, he is not startled; when deprived of something, he does not resent it; when threatened, he does not yield. With such mastery of himself, his conduct reaches the spirits, and he can serve as a general for all under Heaven. Yet who but a gentleman who understands the Way could accomplish this? Now our sagely Son of Heaven brings things to fulfillment through enduring constancy and nurtures men of talent throughout his long life. Soon men such as these will emerge to answer his eager quest for worthy men. These are the views of an obscure commoner; why should you, honored officials, deign to hear them?

Fifth Question
Wang Tongwen
Associate Examiner Zhang Bangchen, Instructor, comments: “A man of talent awaiting employment, whose understanding is distinctive. Proceeding on this basis, he could achieve success in pacifying the Japanese raiders.”
Examiner Zheng Yannian, Instructor, comments: “Closely addresses the needs of the times.”
Examiner Wei Tiqian, Instructor, comments: “Shows considerable discernment.”

I have heard, in my ignorance, that the way to repel the barbarians lies in ordering affairs at home, and that its essential point lies in demanding actual results. Why is this? Changing circumstances arise without limit, while the opportunities for appropriate action lie hidden in the subtlest details. Without clear and comprehensive discernment, even when their first signs appear before us daily, we shall overlook them …

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
而莫之知旣知矣而欲舉之非一人之力
旦夕焉可必也非一人之力則獨任乎不
可期之功者罕矣而復伺以歲月之積鮮
不從中阻者故知之未必舉舉之未必實
也法密而實則疎名存而實則亡天下之
事往往坐此弊矣而况以制難窮之變握
不測之機者乎是故責實要矣方今東南
之患非倭耶執事策豫士而及此豈不以
豫天下之中而淮南西鄰焉邇者焚掠至
===
淮矣震鄰之戒可晏然也乎天下大勢强
弱在西北虛實在東南而虛實則强弱之
本也故以形勢論則吳浙閩廣輕然而
京師公私所仰給乎東南者豈少也故以氣
脉論則吳浙閩廣重而可使之困乎宜執
事之惓焉及之也愚請悉言之夫自有倭
之役議臣發言策士畫計大約有二言守
者則議城寨議兵舩議團練議招募不特
此也曰調兵曰積餉曰賞罰曰守令曰將
punctuated:
而莫之知。旣知矣，而欲舉之，非一人之力，旦夕焉可必也。非一人之力，則獨任乎不可期之功者罕矣；而復伺以歲月之積，鮮不從中阻者。故知之未必舉，舉之未必實也。法密而實則疎，名存而實則亡，天下之事往往坐此弊矣，而况以制難窮之變、握不測之機者乎？是故責實要矣。
方今東南之患，非倭耶？執事策豫士而及此，豈不以豫天下之中，而淮南西鄰焉，邇者焚掠至淮矣，震鄰之戒，可晏然也乎？天下大勢，强弱在西北，虛實在東南，而虛實則强弱之本也。故以形勢論，則吳浙閩廣輕；然而京師公私所仰給乎東南者，豈少也？故以氣脉論，則吳浙閩廣重，而可使之困乎？宜執事之惓焉及之也。愚請悉言之。
夫自有倭之役，議臣發言，策士畫計，大約有二。言守者，則議城寨，議兵舩，議團練，議招募。不特此也，曰調兵，曰積餉，曰賞罰，曰守令，曰將
translation_en:
…and fail to recognize them. Even once they are recognized, putting measures into effect is beyond one person’s power; how could success be assured overnight? Since this exceeds one person’s power, few will undertake sole responsibility for an achievement whose realization cannot be assured. If, moreover, one must wait through accumulating months and years, scarcely any undertaking escapes obstruction along the way. Thus, recognizing a problem does not necessarily lead to action, and action does not necessarily produce actual results. Regulations are meticulous, yet implementation is lax; the name remains, yet the substance disappears. Affairs throughout the realm repeatedly founder on this failing. How much more is this so when dealing with endlessly varying circumstances and grasping unpredictable opportunities? Hence the essential thing is to demand actual results.
Are not the Japanese raiders the present scourge of the southeast? In putting policy questions to the candidates of Henan, have you not raised this matter because Henan lies at the center of the realm and is Huainan’s western neighbor? Recently, burning and pillaging have reached the Huai region. With this warning of thunder striking one’s neighbor, can we remain at ease? In the overall configuration of the realm, military strength or weakness lies in the northwest, and material scarcity or abundance in the southeast; scarcity or abundance is the foundation of strength or weakness. Thus, judged by strategic position, Wu, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong carry little weight. Yet are the resources on which both public institutions and private households in the capital depend upon the southeast at all slight? Judged, therefore, by the realm’s vital circulation, Wu, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong carry great weight. Can we allow them to be reduced to distress? It is fitting that you should raise this matter with such concern. Permit me to explain fully.
Ever since the campaigns against the Japanese raiders began, deliberating ministers have voiced their views, and strategists have devised plans. Broadly speaking, these fall into two approaches. Those advocating defense discuss fortified cities and strongholds, warships, local militia training, and recruitment. Nor do they stop there: they speak of troop deployments, stockpiling military provisions, rewards and punishments, prefects and magistrates, and military commanders…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
領主於征討明中國之體者也言撫者則
歸咎于海禁之太嚴而曰互市曰招降急
於輯靖安瘡痍之民者也蓋皆忠國之猷
焉而自愚生言之則主守者是而撫之者
其說非也夫互市不可也非我族類其心
叵測我之需彼者非急而彼之仰資乎我
者十之八九方峻防之猶竊窺焉而可自
啓其釁復誘之使啖利乎利源旣開一不
厭其所欲絕之則信不行縱之則害方蔓
===
不聞勝國時乎舸艘絡繹戈矛森具輒燔
燬剽掠爲州縣害我
太祖高皇帝明燭其狡絕却貢獻載在
祖訓者可考也故互市不可也夫言招降者非
也兵之道可守而後可戰可勦而後可撫
旣深入矣而其所啖在是又未嘗受吾挫
焉而欲馳虛詞使之納欵也得乎矧介命
者持之以射彼巳之利褻尊甚矣故招降
不可也而治內急焉則主守者其說近矣
punctuated:
領，主於征討，明中國之體者也。言撫者則歸咎于海禁之太嚴，而曰互市，曰招降，急於輯靖，安瘡痍之民者也。蓋皆忠國之猷焉，而自愚生言之，則主守者是，而撫之者其說非也。
夫互市不可也。非我族類，其心叵測。我之需彼者非急，而彼之仰資乎我者十之八九。方峻防之，猶竊窺焉，而可自啓其釁，復誘之使啖利乎？利源旣開，一不厭其所欲，絕之則信不行，縱之則害方蔓。不聞勝國時乎？舸艘絡繹，戈矛森具，輒燔燬剽掠，爲州縣害。我太祖高皇帝明燭其狡，絕却貢獻，載在《祖訓》者可考也。故互市不可也。
夫言招降者非也。兵之道，可守而後可戰，可勦而後可撫。旣深入矣，而其所啖在是，又未嘗受吾挫焉，而欲馳虛詞使之納欵也，得乎？矧介命者持之以射彼巳之利，褻尊甚矣！故招降不可也。而治內急焉，則主守者其說近矣。
translation_en:
…commanders: these proposals give priority to punitive campaigns and uphold the dignity of the Central Kingdom. Those who advocate pacification, however, blame the excessive severity of the maritime prohibitions. They speak of opening trade and inviting surrender, urgently seeking to restore peace and bring security to a people wounded by war. All these are plans born of loyalty to the state. Yet in my humble judgment, those who advocate defense are right, while the arguments of those who favor pacification are mistaken.
Opening trade is unacceptable. They are not of our people, and their intentions cannot be fathomed. Our need for their goods is not urgent, whereas eight or nine tenths of what they require depends on supplies from us. Even while we maintain strict defenses against them, they secretly watch for opportunities. How could we ourselves open a breach and further entice them with profits? Once this source of profit is opened, should we fail to satisfy their desires, cutting them off would undermine our credibility, while indulging them would allow the harm to spread. Have you not heard what happened under the preceding dynasty? Ships came in an unending stream, bristling with spears and lances; they repeatedly burned and plundered, bringing devastation upon the prefectures and counties. Our Emperor Taizu Gao clearly perceived their cunning and rejected their tribute offerings. This can be verified in the Ancestral Instructions. Thus opening trade is unacceptable.
Those who advocate inviting surrender are also mistaken. The way of warfare is to secure the ability to defend before fighting, and the ability to destroy the enemy before offering pacification. They have already penetrated deep into our territory; the spoils they covet are here, and they have never yet suffered a defeat at our hands. Can we expect to dispatch empty words and thereby induce them to submit? Moreover, those entrusted with such commissions use them to seek profit for the enemy and themselves [?], gravely debasing imperial dignity! Thus inviting surrender is unacceptable. Putting our internal affairs in order is urgent; in this respect, the arguments of those who advocate defense come close to the mark.

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
今州縣非無城也頃者憲臣復增築之非
無寨也關隘棊置烽堠星羅則列城寨矣
衞所連絡分署戰舸大者艨艟便於衝突
小者艓艦捷於探望官以備倭爲職兵以
出海爲名則備兵船矣保甲壯丁列戶而
居郡縣健兒按籍而食則嚴團練矣請纓
借箸者駢足待次投石超乘者輻輳傳飧
則行招募矣羽檄紛馳疾若轉圜籍名應
徵盛同積楚則調兵矣歲輸額運盡報罷
===
以給軍需鹽餘贖羨悉蒐發以供犒具則
積餉矣分符郡庭舉自夙望綰章州縣取
諸甲榜則急守令矣報功之典卽小卒罔
遺玩寇之誅雖大將不貸則信賞罰矣建
牙之寄拔自儔伍推轂之任不聞中制則
重將領矣斯數者未嘗不舉而卒未蕩滌
妖氛收廓清之効何哉豈竒策秘計將出
於數者之外乎而歷考古今兵家之所尚
者要不出此執事慨乎實効之未臻而復
punctuated: 今州縣非無城也，頃者憲臣復增築之；非無寨也，關隘棊置，烽堠星羅，則列城寨矣。衞所連絡，分署戰舸，大者艨艟便於衝突，小者艓艦捷於探望；官以備倭爲職，兵以出海爲名，則備兵船矣。保甲壯丁列戶而居，郡縣健兒按籍而食，則嚴團練矣。請纓借箸者駢足待次，投石超乘者輻輳傳飧，則行招募矣。羽檄紛馳，疾若轉圜；籍名應徵，盛同積楚，則調兵矣。歲輸額運盡報罷，以給軍需；鹽餘贖羨悉蒐發，以供犒具，則積餉矣。分符郡庭，舉自夙望；綰章州縣，取諸甲榜，則急守令矣。報功之典，卽小卒罔遺；玩寇之誅，雖大將不貸，則信賞罰矣。建牙之寄，拔自儔伍；推轂之任，不聞中制，則重將領矣。斯數者未嘗不舉，而卒未蕩滌妖氛，收廓清之効，何哉？豈竒策秘計將出於數者之外乎？而歷考古今兵家之所尚者，要不出此。執事慨乎實効之未臻，而復
translation_en:
Today the subprefectures and counties are hardly without walls: recently the censorial officials have further enlarged and strengthened them. Nor are they without stockades: fortified passes are arrayed like pieces on a chessboard, and beacon towers scattered like stars. Thus walled defenses and stockades have been deployed. The guards and battalions are linked together, with warships assigned among them. The larger armored vessels are suited to charging the enemy, while the smaller craft are nimble at reconnaissance. Officials have defense against the Japanese pirates as their duty, and troops are designated for service at sea. Thus troops and ships have been provided. Able-bodied men of the baojia household organization reside in ordered household groupings, and the fighting men of the prefectures and counties receive provisions according to their registers. Thus local militia training has been rigorously organized. Men volunteering for service or offering military counsel stand shoulder to shoulder awaiting their turn; warriors capable of hurling stones and leaping into chariots converge from all directions and receive their meals. Thus recruitment has been undertaken. Feather-marked military dispatches speed to and fro, swift as a rolling ball; men registering their names and answering the summons are as numerous as piled brushwood. Thus troops have been mobilized. The annual quota shipments have all been reported suspended so that the resources may meet military needs; surplus salt revenues and excess proceeds from redemption payments have all been collected and disbursed to provide rewards and refreshments for the troops. Thus military provisions have been accumulated. Those entrusted with the tally of prefectural authority are selected from men of established reputation; those bearing the seals of subprefectural and county office are drawn from the ranks of metropolitan graduates. Thus priority has been given to appointing prefects and magistrates. In rewarding merit, not even an ordinary soldier is overlooked; in punishing those who take the enemy lightly, not even a senior general is spared. Thus rewards and punishments have been made dependable. Those entrusted with raising the commander's standard are promoted from among their fellows in the ranks; those commissioned to command armies are not, so far as one hears, constrained by interference from the court. Thus military commanders have been accorded weight.

All these measures have indeed been undertaken, yet in the end the baleful atmosphere has not been swept away, nor has the realm been cleared of the enemy. Why is this? Could extraordinary strategies and secret plans lie outside these measures? Yet a survey of what military experts have valued throughout history shows that, in essentials, it goes no further than these. You, sir, lament that tangible results have not yet been achieved, and again …

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
欲求常勝常安至當至要之策愚也舍是
則無以復矣無亦曰實効之未臻由於不
責實乎蓋是數者非不舉之也舉之而未
責實焉者也夫自淮海而南至於漳潮城
寨錯列兵船接屬道里犬牙連亘互制不
專責不可也蘇松淮揚福建各統之乎撫
臣而浙江則總督在焉總督者總之爾至
於信地非撫臣責乎精嚴號令明慎烽堠
勝筭夙定不動如山薙獮捷發勢同建瓴
===
假令賊至按其由入而付諸理則將何辭
也畫地而守聯營而戍卽延袤萬里指顧
目前矣故宜專責任彼此分疆則觀望顧
忌將驅盜於鄰矣宜特嚴其法諸路撫臣
訓練遊兵而以正兵守信地遊兵援鄰境
擊東則西應勢單則力併夫然後心同而
勇自奮勢合而氣自揚故宜恊心力旣招
募且調兵矣餉未甞不足也然而不捷者
何蓋狼廣則貪川土則悍鎗手洞丁則猾
punctuated: 欲求常勝常安、至當至要之策，愚也舍是則無以復矣。無亦曰實効之未臻，由於不責實乎？蓋是數者，非不舉之也，舉之而未責實焉者也。夫自淮海而南，至於漳潮，城寨錯列，兵船接屬，道里犬牙，連亘互制，不專責不可也。蘇松淮揚福建各統之乎撫臣，而浙江則總督在焉。總督者，總之爾；至於信地，非撫臣責乎？精嚴號令，明慎烽堠，勝筭夙定，不動如山；薙獮捷發，勢同建瓴。假令賊至，按其由入而付諸理，則將何辭也？畫地而守，聯營而戍，卽延袤萬里，指顧目前矣。故宜專責任。彼此分疆，則觀望顧忌，將驅盜於鄰矣，宜特嚴其法。諸路撫臣訓練遊兵，而以正兵守信地，遊兵援鄰境；擊東則西應，勢單則力併。夫然後心同而勇自奮，勢合而氣自揚，故宜恊心力。旣招募且調兵矣，餉未甞不足也，然而不捷者何？蓋狼廣則貪，川土則悍，鎗手洞丁則猾
translation_en:
…you wish to seek measures that will ensure constant victory and lasting peace, measures supremely fitting and essential. Foolish as I am, I can offer no answer apart from these. Might we not say that practical results have not been achieved because no one is held accountable for producing them? These measures have indeed been undertaken, but without accountability for actual results.

From Huaihai southward to Zhangzhou and Chaozhou, walled towns and forts stand interspersed, and warships follow one another in succession. Routes and distances interlock like dogs’ teeth, extending continuously and providing mutual support. Specific responsibility must therefore be assigned. Suzhou, Songjiang, Huai’an, Yangzhou, and Fujian are each under their respective grand coordinators, while the supreme commander is stationed in Zhejiang. The supreme commander exercises overall command; but are not the assigned defense sectors the responsibility of the grand coordinators? Commands must be precise and strict, beacon posts vigilantly and carefully managed, and plans for victory settled in advance. Standing firm, the troops should be immovable as mountains; striking swiftly to cut down the enemy, they should have the force of water pouring from a roof. If bandits arrive, investigate the route by which they entered and hand those responsible over for judicial proceedings: what excuse could they offer? Divide the territory into areas to be defended and link the camps into a connected garrison system. Even a stretch of ten thousand li would then lie before one’s eyes, ready to be directed with a gesture. Thus responsibility should be specifically assigned.

If each merely has a separate jurisdiction, they will wait and watch, constrained by misgivings, and drive the bandits into neighboring territory. The rules governing this must be particularly strict. The grand coordinators of the various regions should train mobile troops, using regular troops to defend their assigned sectors and mobile troops to reinforce neighboring territory. When the east is attacked, the west should respond; where strength is insufficient, forces should unite. Only then, with minds united, will courage naturally rise; with forces combined, morale will naturally soar. Thus their resolve and efforts should be coordinated.

Troops have already been recruited and others transferred, and provisions and pay have never been insufficient. Why, then, has victory not been achieved? The Lang and Guang troops [?] are greedy, the indigenous troops from Sichuan are unruly, and the spearmen and cave-district levies are crafty…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
不我用容美之兵足賴矣而其難御又兼
諸兵飽則颺饑則怨行則剽劫居則橫肆
而其食之也一可當土兵之十賞之也十
可當土兵之百夫方寇之猝至民不識兵
不得不數徵調今旣久而見聞且習矣孰
不懷憤激哉因而練之州縣之隸保甲之
籍比其什伍時其簡閱精其器械訓之步
伐人自爲兵家各爲衞則調兵招募可免
而餉自足矣故宜練土兵夫我之應寇嘗
===
墮於計中而寇之伺我反出於意外者以
我之人導之也嚴比閭之稽申覺察之令
飭連坐之法開首訐之門則勾引之情必
露而嘯聚之羣潛消矣故宜嚴接濟兩軍
相對間諜爲先故懸不貲之賞則機警者
至矣或用間以離其黨或張疑以誘其來
或乘其懈而擊之或伺其出而制之或潛
置火而焚之或陰鑿舟而沉之彼之虛實
作止吾得而盡知之知之而徐待之而我
punctuated:
不我用。容美之兵足賴矣，而其難御又兼諸兵：飽則颺，饑則怨，行則剽劫，居則橫肆。而其食之也，一可當土兵之十；賞之也，十可當土兵之百。夫方寇之猝至，民不識兵，不得不數徵調。今旣久而見聞且習矣，孰不懷憤激哉？因而練之，州縣之隸，保甲之籍，比其什伍，時其簡閱，精其器械，訓之步伐，人自爲兵，家各爲衞，則調兵招募可免，而餉自足矣。故宜練土兵。
夫我之應寇，嘗墮於計中，而寇之伺我，反出於意外者，以我之人導之也。嚴比閭之稽，申覺察之令，飭連坐之法，開首訐之門，則勾引之情必露，而嘯聚之羣潛消矣。故宜嚴接濟。
兩軍相對，間諜爲先。故懸不貲之賞，則機警者至矣。或用間以離其黨，或張疑以誘其來，或乘其懈而擊之，或伺其出而制之，或潛置火而焚之，或陰鑿舟而沉之。彼之虛實作止，吾得而盡知之，知之而徐待之，而我
translation_en:
…do not serve our purposes. The troops of Rongmei may be relied upon, yet their resistance to control combines the failings of all the other troops: when well fed they run off, when hungry they complain, on the march they plunder, and when quartered they behave outrageously. Feeding one of them costs as much as feeding ten local soldiers; rewarding ten costs as much as rewarding a hundred local soldiers. When the raiders first arrived suddenly, the people knew nothing of warfare, and repeated levies and troop transfers were unavoidable. Now that this has continued for so long, people have become familiar with what they have seen and heard. Who does not harbor anger and indignation? Build upon this and train them: take those under prefectural and county jurisdiction and those entered in the baojia household registers, organize them into tens and fives, inspect and muster them at appropriate times, improve their weapons, and drill them in marching and maneuvering. If each person becomes a soldier and each household defends itself, troop transfers and recruitment can be dispensed with, and military provisions will naturally suffice. Thus local soldiers should be trained.
When we respond to the raiders, we repeatedly fall into their schemes, while their moves against us come unexpectedly, because our own people guide them. Make neighborhood inspections stringent, reiterate orders for vigilance and detection, enforce the laws of collective liability, and open channels for informing and accusation. Then collusion with the raiders will surely be exposed, and the bands that gather at their call will quietly dissolve. Thus the provision of aid and supplies to them should be strictly checked.
When two armies confront each other, espionage comes first. Offer rewards of immense value, and alert, resourceful men will come forward. One may use agents to divide their faction, deploy deceptive appearances to lure them forward, strike when they are off guard, watch for their departure and intercept them, secretly set fires to burn them, or covertly bore holes in their boats to sink them. We can learn all their weaknesses and strengths, their movements and halts. Knowing these, we can calmly await them, while our…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
之事則彼不知也如是則闔闢張弛惟吾
意爾故宜通間諜夫賞當則志士死義罰
重則懦夫倍氣今賞格非不厚也而或賞
矣未著報効之實罰條非不嚴也而或罰
矣不懷奮激之志况有非功而妄報有罪
而不聞者乎故宜核功罪夫張官以爲民
則捍禦先之矣雲中樂安獨非郡縣乎愚
不敢謂今無其人也乃有詘情於豪右濡
跡乎富腴勾番主逋漫不一問甚至幸倭
===
之來因以爲利分寶取盈起官倭之謡者
矣愚以爲部使者宜按條寘憲不少假借
庶幾內治順矣故宜謹官常是數者治內
者也非出於前數者之外特責其實焉爾
而其綱領則在將古之將入不謀家出不
顧身興處卧起敵儼在前精神心志士相
爲命身冒矢石獨先三軍忠貫金石誓不
與賊俱生故將愛主而不愛身則士畏將
而不畏敵千萬一心闘氣自倍有將如此
punctuated: 之事則彼不知也。如是，則闔闢張弛惟吾意爾，故宜通間諜。夫賞當則志士死義，罰重則懦夫倍氣。今賞格非不厚也，而或賞矣，未著報効之實；罰條非不嚴也，而或罰矣，不懷奮激之志。况有非功而妄報、有罪而不聞者乎？故宜核功罪。夫張官以爲民，則捍禦先之矣。雲中、樂安獨非郡縣乎？愚不敢謂今無其人也。乃有詘情於豪右，濡跡乎富腴，勾番主逋，漫不一問，甚至幸倭之來，因以爲利，分寶取盈，起官倭之謡者矣。愚以爲部使者宜按條寘憲，不少假借，庶幾內治順矣，故宜謹官常。是數者，治內者也，非出於前數者之外，特責其實焉爾。而其綱領則在將。古之將，入不謀家，出不顧身；興處卧起，敵儼在前；精神心志，士相爲命；身冒矢石，獨先三軍；忠貫金石，誓不與賊俱生。故將愛主而不愛身，則士畏將而不畏敵，千萬一心，闘氣自倍。有將如此
translation_en:
…our affairs, however, remain unknown to them. Thus, whether to close or open, tighten or relax, will depend entirely on our own wishes. Hence we should maintain channels of espionage. When rewards are fitting, men of resolve will die for righteousness; when punishments are severe, even cowards will redouble their courage. The present scale of rewards is certainly generous, yet some who have received rewards have shown no actual service in return. The provisions for punishment are certainly strict, yet some who have been punished harbor no resolve to exert themselves. How much worse are those who falsely report achievements where none exist, or whose offenses go unreported! Hence we should scrutinize achievements and offenses.

Offices are established for the people, so defense must come first. Were Yunzhong and Le’an alone not commanderies and counties? I would not presume to say that men of their caliber no longer exist today. Yet there are officials who bend their judgment to powerful local families and immerse themselves in wealth and luxury. Collusion with foreigners and the harboring of fugitives go entirely unquestioned. Some even welcome the arrival of the Japanese pirates and use it to profit, dividing the treasure and taking their fill, giving rise to popular talk of “official pirates.” I believe that the regional inspecting commissioners should apply the statutes and impose the prescribed penalties, allowing not the slightest indulgence. Internal administration might then be put in order. Hence we should strictly uphold the regular duties of officials.

These several measures concern internal governance. They do not lie outside the measures previously discussed; they simply demand actual results from them. Their guiding principle, however, rests with the generals. The generals of antiquity, when at home, did not scheme for their households; when in the field, they gave no thought to their own safety. Whether active or at rest, lying down or rising, they saw the enemy as though standing before them. In spirit, heart, and purpose, they and their soldiers entrusted their lives to one another. They personally braved arrows and stones, taking the lead before the entire army. Their loyalty could pierce metal and stone, and they swore never to live alongside the bandits. Thus, when a general loves his sovereign more than his own life, his soldiers fear their general rather than the enemy. Thousands and tens of thousands become of one mind, and their fighting spirit naturally doubles. With generals such as these…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
而數事皆可責實矣而今之將者果能是
乎故終之責將領或者曰海洋之中屹然
而峙者在吳浙則馬蹟揚山大衢也陳錢
三山也在閩則彭湖海壇也蓋天造之險
寇所必由者也
國初巨艦悉此艤焉至正統則防稍弛矣宜
選發健丁計口分地且耕且守不責其賦
給以舟械統以材官飭器閑藝遠哨近探
無事則扼塞有警則捍蔽峙糧不費而緩
===
急得力矣則守要害之說也曰我
太祖高皇帝戡定之初嘗遣行人楊載趙秩宣
諭日本宣德間亦嘗遣使矣擬
請於
朝下
詔切責其國王之罪南則琉球北則朝鮮令
其遣使轉奉宣
諭收緝其部落而盡返中國之人離堅渙羣是
或一策則宣
punctuated:
而數事皆可責實矣。而今之將者果能是乎？故終之責將領。或者曰：「海洋之中屹然而峙者，在吳浙則馬蹟、揚山、大衢也，陳錢、三山也；在閩則彭湖、海壇也。蓋天造之險，寇所必由者也。國初巨艦悉此艤焉，至正統則防稍弛矣。宜選發健丁，計口分地，且耕且守，不責其賦，給以舟械，統以材官，飭器閑藝，遠哨近探。無事則扼塞，有警則捍蔽，峙糧不費，而緩急得力矣。」則守要害之說也。
曰：「我太祖高皇帝戡定之初，嘗遣行人楊載、趙秩宣諭日本，宣德間亦嘗遣使矣。擬請於朝，下詔切責其國王之罪。南則琉球，北則朝鮮，令其遣使轉奉宣諭，收緝其部落，而盡返中國之人。離堅渙羣，是或一策。」則宣
translation_en:
…and actual results can be demanded in all these matters. But can today’s commanders truly achieve this? Thus I conclude with holding commanders accountable. Someone says: “Among the islands rising steeply from the sea, those off Wu and Zhe are Maji, Yangshan, Daqu, Chenqian, and Sanshan; those off Min are Penghu and Haitan. These are naturally created strongholds through which the raiders must pass. At the beginning of the dynasty, great warships were all moored here, but by the Zhengtong reign the defenses had grown somewhat lax. We should select and dispatch able-bodied men, allot land according to their numbers, and have them both farm and defend it, without exacting taxes from them. Supply them with boats and weapons, place them under capable officers, put their equipment in order, and train them in military skills. Send patrols far afield and scouts nearby. When all is quiet, they would hold the strategic passes; when an alarm arises, they would provide protection. Grain could be stockpiled without expense, and they would render effective service in emergencies.” This is the proposal to defend strategic points.
Another says: “When our Emperor Taizu Gao first pacified the realm, he sent the Messengers Yang Zai and Zhao Zhi to proclaim imperial instructions to Japan. Envoys were also sent during the Xuande reign. I propose petitioning the court to issue an edict sternly censuring that country’s king for his offenses. Have Liuqiu to the south and Chaoxian to the north dispatch envoys to convey the imperial instructions, requiring him to round up his bands and return all the people of China.
