Breaking up their solid alliances and dispersing their groups might be one useful strategy.” This is the proposal for proclaiming…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
論之說也内治旣密羣策畢舉變制於我機握
自中何守不固何堅不瑕何暴亂之不可
定哉治内之道海禁寓焉執事所謂
祖宗成法昭然具在者也果責實矣浮議奚恤
哉雖然繙據載籍
天將輔有道之國使之固結延綿堅不抜之基
如磐石泰山之安者則必篤生
聖神之主内順治而外威嚴揚武張罰聲靈震
疊薄伐梗化而垂底定謐寧之治於無疆
===
盍觀之周乎武王定鼎之初肅慎氏貢楛
矢石砮王乃昭其令德之致將以示後人
至于宣王蠻荆淮南叛背匪茹王命方叔
召虎征之至于南海遂延八百靈長之業
我
成祖文皇帝北征振旅幕南無王庭矣乃日本
國王源道義効順剿捕對馬壹之寇
成祖御製銘文表其鎮國之山肆我
皇上聖神中興非周宣可彷彿其萬一蠢茲醜
punctuated:
論之說也。内治旣密，羣策畢舉，變制於我，機握自中，何守不固？何堅不瑕？何暴亂之不可定哉？治内之道，海禁寓焉，執事所謂祖宗成法昭然具在者也。果責實矣，浮議奚恤哉？雖然，繙據載籍，天將輔有道之國，使之固結延綿，堅不抜之基，如磐石泰山之安者，則必篤生聖神之主，内順治而外威嚴，揚武張罰，聲靈震疊，薄伐梗化，而垂底定謐寧之治於無疆。
盍觀之周乎？武王定鼎之初，肅慎氏貢楛矢石砮，王乃昭其令德之致，將以示後人。至于宣王，蠻荆淮南叛背匪茹，王命方叔、召虎征之，至于南海，遂延八百靈長之業。
我成祖文皇帝北征振旅，幕南無王庭矣。乃日本國王源道義効順，剿捕對馬壹之寇。成祖御製銘文，表其鎮國之山。肆我皇上聖神中興，非周宣可彷彿其萬一。蠢茲醜
translation_en:
…is the argument. Once internal administration is thorough and every strategy has been brought into play, we ourselves control responses to changing circumstances, and the decisive initiative rests at the center. What defense will not hold firm? What stronghold will not reveal a weakness? What violence and disorder cannot be quelled? The maritime prohibitions are encompassed within this way of governing internally. These are what you, honored examiners, call the established laws of the imperial ancestors, clearly preserved in their entirety. If actual results are indeed demanded, why worry about idle criticism? Nevertheless, consulting the written records, we find that when Heaven intends to assist a state that possesses the Way, making its foundations firm, enduring, and unshakable—as secure as a great rock or Mount Tai—it invariably brings forth a sagely and divinely wise ruler. Within, he establishes orderly government; abroad, he commands awe. He displays martial might and enforces punishments; his renown and numinous power inspire trembling submission. He campaigns against those who obstruct his transforming influence, bequeathing a settled and tranquil order without end.
Why not look to the Zhou? When King Wu first established his capital and rule, the Sushen people presented arrows of ku wood and stone arrowheads as tribute. The king made manifest how his excellent virtue had brought this about, to instruct later generations. In King Xuan’s time, the Man peoples of Jing and the people south of the Huai rebelled and defied submission. The king ordered Fang Shu and Shao Hu to campaign against them, reaching as far as the Southern Sea. Thus he prolonged the dynasty’s glorious, enduring enterprise of eight hundred years.
Our Emperor Chengzu Wen campaigned in the north and returned with his army; no royal court remained south of the desert. Then the king of Japan, Yuan Daoyi, demonstrated his allegiance by suppressing and apprehending the raiders of Duima and Yi [?]. Chengzu personally composed an inscription to honor the mountain that guarded that kingdom. Now our sagely and divinely wise Emperor has brought about a restoration; King Xuan of Zhou could not approach even one ten-thousandth of his achievement. These vile, restive…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
夷豈自外於覆載之中蓋
天以底定謐寧之功屬於
有道之朝將永我
國家億萬載無疆之祚必有方叔召虎者出
而收來威之績載寧之休以報
闕下采芑之詩曰蠢爾蠻荆大邦爲讎方叔
元老克壯其猶江漢之詩曰明明天子令
聞不已矢其文德洽此四國愚也敢以爲
今日頌
punctuated: 夷，豈自外於覆載之中？蓋天以底定謐寧之功屬於有道之朝，將永我國家億萬載無疆之祚。必有方叔、召虎者出，而收來威之績、載寧之休，以報闕下。《采芑》之詩曰：「蠢爾蠻荆，大邦爲讎。方叔元老，克壯其猶。」《江漢》之詩曰：「明明天子，令聞不已。矢其文德，洽此四國。」愚也敢以爲今日頌。
translation_en:
…barbarians—how could they place themselves outside what Heaven covers and Earth sustains? For Heaven has entrusted the achievement of pacification and lasting peace to a dynasty possessing the Way, intending to perpetuate our state's boundless blessings for countless millions of years. Surely men like Fang Shu and Shao Hu will emerge to win the distinction of bringing them into submission through awe and the glory of restoring tranquility, thereby repaying Your Majesty.

The poem “Gathering Millet” (Cai qi) says: “You stirring barbarians of Jing take the great state as your foe. Fang Shu, the venerable minister, was mighty in his plans.” The poem “The Jiang and Han Rivers” (Jiang Han) says: “Illustrious is the Son of Heaven; his good renown never ceases. He spreads his civil virtue, bringing harmony to the states in all four quarters.” Foolish as I am, I venture to offer these words as a hymn of praise for the present day.

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄕試錄後序
嘉靖戊午秋八月寔天下鄕
試期在河南則監察御史楊
惟平監臨之肅憲振猷章程
畢正豫飭所司展采錯事罔
弗虔廼以延年佐校文錄旣
成宜有言以贅諸末延年惟
===
豫爲
天地之中羲農殷周之所都也我
聖祖統天
駐蹕旬時規圖
定鼎我
皇上龍飛大狩三
幸玆邦
punctuated:
河南鄕試錄後序

嘉靖戊午秋八月，寔天下鄕試期。在河南，則監察御史楊惟平監臨之，肅憲振猷，章程畢正，豫飭所司展采錯事，罔弗虔。廼以延年佐校文。錄旣成，宜有言以贅諸末。延年惟：豫爲天地之中，羲農殷周之所都也。我聖祖統天，駐蹕旬時，規圖定鼎。我皇上龍飛，大狩三幸玆邦。
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the wuwu year of Jiajing [1558], the Provincial Examinations were held throughout the realm. In Henan, Investigating Censor Yang Weiping supervised the examination. He enforced the regulations strictly and put guiding principles into effect; all procedures were duly set in order. He instructed the responsible officials beforehand to discharge their duties and arrange the work, and none failed to act with reverence. I, Yannian, was then appointed to assist in evaluating the compositions. Now that the record is complete, it is fitting that I append some words at its end.

I, Yannian, reflect that Henan lies at the center of Heaven and Earth and is where Fuxi, Shennong, and the Yin and Zhou dynasties established their capitals. When our sagely founder assumed rule over all under Heaven, he stayed here for ten days, considering plans to establish his capital. Since our present emperor ascended the throne, he has visited this land three times on grand imperial tours…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
渥惠洪霑
奎文敷錫
昭曠之典蕩蕩難名焉每竊念是
邦人士何幸而親炙
聖人之化若是哉期耳目其盛而
未之能也玆應聘而來渡河
洛之津瞻峻極之嶽步古莘
===
之野陟圭測之臺廼嘆曰是
非圖書之符會申甫之孕靈
伊尹周公之所以發祥而奮
績者耶河山之美固宜我
聖祖
皇上屬車首幸
鴻澤先加也謂無豪傑士應運而
punctuated: 渥惠洪霑，奎文敷錫，昭曠之典，蕩蕩難名焉。每竊念是邦人士何幸而親炙聖人之化若是哉！期耳目其盛，而未之能也。玆應聘而來，渡河洛之津，瞻峻極之嶽，步古莘之野，陟圭測之臺，廼嘆曰：「是非圖書之符會、申甫之孕靈、伊尹周公之所以發祥而奮績者耶？河山之美，固宜我聖祖、皇上屬車首幸，鴻澤先加也。謂無豪傑士應運而
translation_en:
…His abundant beneficence spread far and wide, and his imperial writings were generously bestowed. These illustrious and far-reaching acts were so magnificent as to defy description. I have often privately reflected: how fortunate are the scholars of this land to receive so directly the transforming influence of the sage sovereign! I hoped to hear and see this flourishing state for myself, but had not been able to do so.

Now, coming in response to an invitation, I crossed the fords of the He and Luo rivers, gazed upon the towering mountain, walked the fields of ancient Shen, and ascended the terrace where shadows were measured with a gnomon. Then I exclaimed: “Is this not where the auspicious signs of the River Chart and the Luo Writing converged, where spiritual potency brought forth Shen and Fu, and where Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou arose auspiciously and accomplished their great deeds? Given the beauty of these rivers and mountains, it was surely fitting that our Sagely Progenitor and our reigning Emperor should have made this a first destination of their imperial processions and bestowed their abundant favors here before other places. Could one say that no outstanding men, answering the call of the age, would…”

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
生者乎旣入簾得多士之文
而縱觀之則見其探研經義
揚搉古今其文詞敷發精華
彪炳曄然而有章其旨趣中
涵雋永淵深恢恢乎而莫可
盡要之於道德仁義之奧不
違也則又嘆曰多士之文彬
===
彬然盛矣非顯被
聖敎之隆而能若是耶廼遵
制額拔其尤者八十人焉雖然文
則盛矣選則嚴矣多士由玆
進矣亦圖所以踐若文否耶昔
孔子論文以猶人自居而以
躬行君子自歉他日傳易則
punctuated:
生者乎？旣入簾，得多士之文而縱觀之，則見其探研經義，揚搉古今，其文詞敷發精華，彪炳曄然而有章；其旨趣中涵雋永，淵深恢恢乎而莫可盡。要之，於道德仁義之奧不違也。則又嘆曰：「多士之文彬彬然盛矣，非顯被聖敎之隆而能若是耶？」廼遵制額，拔其尤者八十人焉。
雖然，文則盛矣，選則嚴矣，多士由玆進矣，亦圖所以踐若文否耶？昔孔子論文，以猶人自居，而以躬行君子自歉；他日傳易，則
translation_en:
…be born? Once I had entered the examiners’ enclosure, I obtained the candidates’ compositions and read them comprehensively. I found that they probed the meanings of the Classics and discussed and assessed past and present. Their language unfolded the finest essence of their subjects, radiant and splendid in its patterned expression; their purport held enduring savor within, profound and so capacious that it could not be exhausted. In sum, they did not depart from the profound truths of the Way, virtue, benevolence, and righteousness. I therefore sighed again: “How richly accomplished are these candidates’ compositions! Could they be thus without having manifestly received the abundant influence of the sage emperor’s teaching?” Accordingly, in compliance with the prescribed quota, we selected eighty of the most outstanding among them.
Yet, although their writing is flourishing, the selection rigorous, and the candidates thereby advanced, do they also consider how to put into practice what they have written? Formerly, when Confucius spoke of literary cultivation, he placed himself on a par with others, but expressed his own shortcomings in personally conducting himself as a gentleman. Later, in his commentary on the Book of Changes, he…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
曰脩詞立其誠所以居業也
夫詞之脩者文也躬行之業
舎立誠奚以哉我
祖宗以科目舉仁賢無心若造化
至公若權衡我
皇上以
閎道訓儒林統一乎
===
聖真成能乎
天地天下之士爭自濯磨以承
德化矧是邦又數覲
耿光者乎是宜懷誠砥礪率四方
而先也今觀多士之文類能
發山川之秘紹羲農伊旦之
言庶幾乎瓌奇俶儻爲
punctuated: 曰：「脩詞立其誠，所以居業也。」夫詞之脩者，文也；躬行之業，舎立誠奚以哉？我祖宗以科目舉仁賢，無心若造化，至公若權衡。我皇上以閎道訓儒林，統一乎聖真，成能乎天地。天下之士爭自濯磨，以承德化，矧是邦又數覲耿光者乎？是宜懷誠砥礪，率四方而先也。今觀多士之文，類能發山川之秘，紹羲農伊旦之言，庶幾乎瓌奇俶儻，爲
translation_en: …he said: “Refining one’s words and establishing one’s sincerity are the means of abiding in one’s work.” Refined words constitute literary accomplishment; but in the work of putting principles into practice, what means are there apart from establishing sincerity? Our imperial ancestors used the examinations to select the humane and worthy, as free from partial intent as the processes of creation, as perfectly impartial as scales and balances. Our Emperor instructs the community of Confucian scholars through the broad Way, bringing them into unity with the true teachings of the sages and fulfilling his capacities in concert with Heaven and Earth. Scholars throughout the realm vie to cleanse and refine themselves, receiving his morally transforming influence. How much more should those of this province, who have repeatedly beheld his radiant glory! They ought therefore to cherish sincerity and discipline themselves, taking the lead among all regions. Now, looking at the writings of these many scholars, we find that they can generally reveal the hidden treasures of the mountains and rivers and carry forward the words of Fu Xi, Shen Nong, Yi Yin, and Dan, the Duke of Zhou. They come close to being extraordinary and outstanding talents, becoming…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖世之英矣然特文焉已矣躬行
以茂業立誠以飭躬非主司
所厚望耶粤稽訓誥諸篇固
伊周之文也考其行若持左
券焉非誠立爾耶爾多士摛
咫尺之詞際
明昌之會異時且奉
===
大對服庶僚將無持此之文以質
厥誠者耶夫誠者善之元立
誠者行之紀故靜言而庸違
色莊而内荏有初而罔終皆
誠之棄也君子期有所建立
必恒其德貞不以紛華悅不
以患害移居
punctuated: 聖世之英矣。然特文焉已矣，躬行以茂業，立誠以飭躬，非主司所厚望耶？粤稽訓誥諸篇，固伊周之文也。考其行，若持左券焉，非誠立爾耶？爾多士摛咫尺之詞，際明昌之會，異時且奉大對，服庶僚，將無持此之文以質厥誠者耶？夫誠者，善之元；立誠者，行之紀。故靜言而庸違，色莊而内荏，有初而罔終，皆誠之棄也。君子期有所建立，必恒其德，貞不以紛華悅，不以患害移。居
translation_en:
…outstanding men of this sagely age. Yet this is merely literary accomplishment. To act personally upon one’s principles so as to advance one’s achievements, and to establish sincerity so as to discipline oneself—is this not what the examination officials earnestly hope for? If we examine the several chapters of instructions and proclamations, these are indeed the writings of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. Examining their conduct is like holding the left half of a contract as proof: was this not because their sincerity was firmly established? You assembled scholars compose your brief writings at a time of enlightened prosperity. In the future, you will present your grand responses before the throne and serve in the various official posts. Will there not then be those who take these writings as a measure of your sincerity?

Sincerity is the source of goodness; establishing sincerity is the guiding principle of conduct. Thus, speaking fine words while acting contrary to them, appearing solemn while inwardly weak, and beginning well without following through—all these amount to abandoning sincerity. A gentleman who hopes to accomplish something must remain constant in his virtue, steadfast, neither beguiled by worldly splendor nor swayed by adversity and harm. When dwelling in…

title: 嘉靖三十七年河南鄉試錄
text:
廟堂則奮其庸守疆域則宣其力
列藩服則保其民樹德業於
當時垂聲光於來祀質今此
之文罔或謬焉斯無負山川
之美祗承乎
聖敎之隆矣若曰弁髦其文詞二
三其心志則豈惟主司者不
===
欲聞將山川亦舍之矣延年
不佞忝執事是貳樂觀多士
大業是居也多士豫之哉
直隸真定府真定縣儒學敎
諭鄭延年謹序
punctuated:
廟堂則奮其庸，守疆域則宣其力，列藩服則保其民，樹德業於當時，垂聲光於來祀，質今此之文，罔或謬焉。斯無負山川之美，祗承乎聖敎之隆矣。若曰弁髦其文詞，二三其心志，則豈惟主司者不欲聞，將山川亦舍之矣。
延年不佞，忝執事是貳，樂觀多士大業是居也。多士豫之哉！
直隸真定府真定縣儒學敎諭鄭延年謹序。
translation_en:
…at court, exert themselves in service; when guarding the frontiers, devote their strength; and when stationed in the provinces, protect their people. They should establish virtue and achievements in their own age and leave a glorious reputation to generations to come. Measured against the writings they have produced here today, their conduct should in no way prove inconsistent. Thus they will live up to the excellence of their native mountains and rivers and reverently uphold the flourishing of the sage emperor’s instruction. But if they discard their compositions like ceremonial caps and childhood hair-tufts once outgrown, and waver in their intentions, then not only will those presiding over the examination refuse to hear of it: even the mountains and rivers will forsake them.
I, Yannian, untalented as I am, have unworthily served as an assistant in conducting this examination. I rejoice to see the many scholars devote themselves to this great undertaking. Scholars, prepare yourselves for it!
Preface respectfully written by Zheng Yannian, Instructor in the Confucian School of Zhending County, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili.
